## Payment Plan Reconciliation Investigation -- JL Code 61566 / Rosenbaum, DIN2025 (2026-10-13) -- READ-ONLY INVESTIGATION, ROOT CAUSE FOUND, FIX PROPOSED, NOT IMPLEMENTED

The owner reported that a newly-uploaded late payment for donor JL
Code 61566, explicitly applied to their open DIN2025 pledge during
import, did not clear the pledge's "Expected payment overdue" status.
Investigated read-only against Production exactly as instructed --
narrowly-scoped queries by known IDs, no broad data pull, no write of
any kind. **Per the owner's explicit instruction, stopping after this
report -- no code or data change has been made.**

### Donor and records (identifiers only, no unrelated donor data exposed)

- Donor: `33426bfe-c176-4980-b2a9-0514976ead9e` (Rabbi & Mrs. Moshe
  Aharon Rosenbaum), `donor_code`/`external_id` = `61566`.
- Open pledge: `626e3556-...`, campaign DIN2025, `committed_cents`
  180000 ($1,800), `paid_cents` 165000 ($1,650), `balance_cents` 15000
  ($150), `category: partially_paid_pledge`, `updated_at`
  2026-10-13T15:54:45Z (today, ~7 minutes before this investigation's
  own first query).
- Payment plan (`pledge_payment_plans`): monthly, `installment_amount_
  cents` 15000, `expected_day_of_month` 4, `next_expected_payment_at`
  2026-10-04, `final_expected_payment_at` 2026-11-04, `ended_at` NULL,
  `commitment_duration_months` 12, `original_pledge_date`
  2025-12-04, plan last edited 2026-10-09 (unrelated to today).
- `jl_payment_assignment_audits` for this donor (exactly 2 rows ever):
  an earlier $150 payment dated 2026-09-04 (applied 2026-09-07,
  `remaining_balance_cents` 30000 after), and **today's new $150
  payment, `payment_date` = 2026-10-12, `decision_type: apply_to_
  pledge`, `pledge_activity_id` correctly = the DIN2025 pledge above,
  `applied_cents` 15000, `remaining_balance_cents` 15000 after,
  `created_at` 2026-10-13T15:54:45Z**, belonging to import
  `5b50aed6-...` (`file_name: payment.csv`, `status: completed`,
  `completed_at` = `created_at` -- the whole import, including this
  audit row and the pledge balance update, committed in one atomic D1
  batch, so there is no partial/stuck-import state to investigate).

### 1. Payment verification -- CONFIRMED, fully and correctly applied

- The payment is real, dated 2026-10-12 (not today's upload date --
  `payment_date` correctly sources `activity.activityDate` from the
  uploaded file, never `now`/upload time, confirmed by reading
  `app/api/import/route.ts`'s own `assignmentAuditRows` construction).
- The explicit "apply to existing open pledge" selection **was
  correctly saved**: `decision_type = 'apply_to_pledge'`,
  `pledge_activity_id` matches the DIN2025 pledge exactly, confirmed
  directly in `jl_payment_assignment_audits`.
- The pledge's own `balance_cents` dropped from $300 to $150 and
  `paid_cents` rose from $1,500 to $1,650 -- an exact $150 decrement,
  proving the application genuinely took effect on the pledge itself,
  not just in the audit log.
- The import batch (`data_imports`) status is `completed`, not
  `processing`/`failed` -- ruling out a stuck-import-status gap (a
  real, separate risk this investigation checked for, see Section 5).

**Conclusion: the payment upload, donor matching, and explicit
pledge-application steps all worked correctly and exactly as
intended.** The defect is entirely downstream, in how the payment
PLAN (not the pledge balance) accounts for a late payment.

### 2. Root cause -- a grace-window "dead zone" in cycle-matching, not a caching, date, or import-freshness defect

Traced the full chain (`app/donors/[id]/page.tsx` -> `evaluatePaymentPlan`
-> `matchPaymentsToCycles`, `lib/relationships/pledge-payment-plan.ts`;
confirmed `lib/workspace/live-data.ts` and `lib/relationships/
recommendation-evidence.ts` feed the Daily Agenda through the exact
same function and the exact same `jl_payment_assignment_audits`-sourced
`linkedPaymentDates` -- one shared source of truth, not two
diverging implementations):

- `evaluatePaymentPlan` is pure and reads fresh D1 data on every page
  load -- **not a caching issue**, confirmed by code inspection; there
  is no persisted/memoized evaluation result anywhere in this path.
- `matchPaymentsToCycles` (`MONTHLY_PAYMENT_PLAN_GRACE_DAYS = 7`)
  matches a payment to a cycle only if the payment falls within
  **exactly** `[cycle - 7 days, cycle + 7 days]`. This window exists to
  keep the match provably unambiguous (monthly cycles are always
  >=28 days apart; a 14-day-wide window can never overlap an adjacent
  one) -- a deliberate, previously-correct design choice, not a typo.
- Today's payment is dated **2026-10-12** -- **8 calendar days** after
  the October 4 due date, i.e. **one day outside** the Oct 4 window
  (which ends Oct 11). It also falls before the November 4 window
  starts (Oct 28), so it lands in a genuine "dead zone" between the two
  windows and matches **neither** cycle.
- Result: `nextUnsatisfiedExpectedPaymentAt` remains **October 4**
  (exactly what the card displays, live-derived, not a stale field --
  confirmed via `page.tsx`'s own `planState.nextExpectedPaymentAt:
  evaluation.nextUnsatisfiedExpectedPaymentAt`), `isLate: true`,
  `daysLate: 2` (today minus Oct 4's grace boundary) -- exactly
  matching the owner's report, despite the $150 the October cycle
  needed having, in every practical sense, already been received.
- **This is a genuine, previously-untested gap, not a misunderstanding
  of intended behavior.** `tests/pledge-payment-plan.test.mjs`
  already has a deliberate "8 days after expected -- LATE" case
  (asserting `isLate`/`daysLate` when **no** payment exists that
  month) and a deliberate "single late payment must satisfy only the
  cycle it falls within" case (a payment 1 day after its OWN due date,
  correctly matching that cycle, not an earlier missed one) -- but
  nothing tests what happens when a real payment DOES arrive, just
  slightly past the OTHER side of that same boundary. Rosenbaum's case
  is exactly that previously-unexercised combination.
- **Not caused by**: payment/upload date confusion (ruled out directly,
  Section 1); import-batch freshness (ruled out, Section 1); double-
  counting (only one $150 payment exists for October, applied once);
  insufficient amount (the $150 payment exactly equals one full
  installment); a stale/cached agenda (ruled out, pure function,
  re-read fresh every time).

### 3. Correct current status, reconciled against actual payment history

With the October $150 installment's money unambiguously received
(just 8 days late) and only one $150 installment's worth of balance
remaining:

- **Correct "Next expected payment": November 4, 2026** (not October
  4 -- October's obligation has been met in substance).
- **Correct status: on track**, not overdue (November 4 has not yet
  arrived).
- The pledge's own balance ($150) is already fully consistent with
  this: exactly one more $150 installment remains, matching the one
  remaining cycle (November) once October is correctly treated as
  satisfied.
- Nothing about this requires inventing a date or a fact -- every
  number above is already present in the real data; only the cycle-
  matching function's own boundary needs to recognize it.

### 4. Daily Agenda impact

**Yes, currently incorrectly flagged.** `lib/relationships/
recommendation-evidence.ts` calls the identical `evaluatePaymentPlan`
with the identical `linkedPaymentDates` source
(`lib/workspace/live-data.ts`'s own `jl_payment_assignment_audits`
query) that the donor page uses -- so the Daily Agenda's "Payment
follow-up needed" / overdue surfacing for this donor is driven by the
exact same `isLate`/`nextUnsatisfiedExpectedPaymentAt` values as the
card, and is wrong for the identical reason. Donor 61566 will keep
being recommended for payment follow-up on the real Production Daily
Fundraising Agenda until this is fixed -- fixing the shared function
fixes both surfaces at once, with no separate agenda-side change
needed.

One secondary, lower-severity inconsistency noticed while tracing
this (not the cause of today's bug, flagged under Section 5 below):
the donor page's own payment-events query additionally joins
`data_imports` and requires `status IN ('active','completed')`
before counting a linked payment; `lib/workspace/live-data.ts`'s
query (which feeds the Agenda, Today page, and Morning Brief) does
not have that same guard. In this specific case it made no difference
(the import's status is `completed`), but the two surfaces are not
literally running the identical SQL, only the identical downstream
evaluation function on (currently) identical input.

### 5. Systemic risk -- other donors likely affected, not yet enumerated

Because the defect lives in the shared `matchPaymentsToCycles`
function itself, **any** active monthly payment plan whose payment
arrives more than `MONTHLY_PAYMENT_PLAN_GRACE_DAYS` (7) days after its
due cycle, but before the next cycle's own window opens (day 8 through
day ~20 late, for a typical monthly cadence), would hit the identical
dead zone -- not specific to Rosenbaum or to JL Code 61566. **This
session did not run a Production-wide query to count how many other
active plans are currently affected** -- doing so would require
re-implementing the cycle-enumeration/matching logic against every
active plan's full payment history (not a simple SQL filter), which
this round scoped out as data-layer work belonging with the fix
itself, pending approval, rather than a quick read-only check. Also
checked by source inspection only (not exhaustively per-donor):
partial payments, multiple payments in one month, and payments
covering/split across multiple installments are not specifically
mishandled by this same mechanism (each cycle's match is a simple
boolean "was ANY unused payment found in this window," so an
additional same-window payment is simply left unused, never double-
counted) -- the dead-zone gap is specifically a LATE-arrival timing
issue, not an amount/double-counting issue.

### 6. Proposed fix (not implemented -- awaiting approval)

Add a second, narrower matching pass inside `evaluatePaymentPlan`
(or as a new exported step `matchPaymentsToCycles` callers can opt
into), run only AFTER the existing ±7-day pass, so every currently-
tested behavior (on-time, early, exactly-at-grace, genuinely-skipped
cycles, the "one late payment must not retroactively erase multiple
earlier missed cycles" guarantee) is completely unchanged:

- Any payment the first pass left unused may satisfy the SINGLE
  oldest still-unsatisfied cycle, but only if:
  1. the payment's date is strictly AFTER that cycle's own due date
     (never pulls an earlier, unrelated payment forward), AND
  2. the payment's date is strictly BEFORE the START of the next
     enumerated cycle's own grace window (`nextCycle - 7 days`) --
     so a payment clearly intended for (and within reach of) a LATER
     cycle can never be misappropriated to cover an earlier one, AND
  3. only one leftover payment may satisfy one leftover cycle, in
     ascending cycle order -- preserving "each payment satisfies at
     most one cycle, each cycle at most one payment" exactly.
- This closes precisely the dead zone Rosenbaum's case fell into,
  changes nothing about any case already covered by the first pass,
  and does not widen the ±7-day window itself (so the file's own
  proven-unambiguous-matching property for the primary pass is
  untouched).
- Worth considering alongside: exposing whether a cycle was satisfied
  by the primary (near-exact) pass or the new fallback pass (e.g. a
  `satisfiedLate: boolean[]` alongside the existing `satisfied`
  array), so a future UI could show "Paid late" rather than looking
  identical to an on-time payment -- not required for correctness, a
  product-polish decision for the owner to make alongside approving
  the core fix.
- Alternative considered and set aside: simply widening
  `MONTHLY_PAYMENT_PLAN_GRACE_DAYS` itself. Rejected because the
  file's own correctness proof depends on the window staying under
  half the minimum cycle gap (14 days); a blanket widen also changes
  the on-time/late THRESHOLD for every plan (a 10-day-late payment
  would newly read as "on track"), which is a different, larger
  product change than the owner asked for and would still eventually
  hit the same dead zone for a payment arriving even later.

### 7. Data impact

**No existing Production record requires correction.** The payment,
the pledge balance, and the audit row are all already correct exactly
as uploaded -- this is purely a presentation/evaluation defect in
`evaluatePaymentPlan`'s cycle-matching, not a data error. Once the fix
above is implemented and deployed, Rosenbaum's plan would correctly
re-evaluate as "on track, next expected November 4" on its very next
page load, with zero data migration or correction script needed.

### 8. Test and deployment plan, once the fix design above is approved

  test (Jan/Feb/Mar, single Mar16 payment) re-run unchanged to prove
  the fallback pass never retroactively rescues a GENUINELY missed
  earlier cycle (only the one immediately preceding an actual, merely-
  late payment); an insufficient/partial payment still correctly

- New end-to-end test reproducing the real `recommendation-evidence.ts`

- Staging/Production isolation test: assert the fix is pure logic with

- Run `node scripts/run-tests.mjs` (full suite) and `tsc --noEmit`

- Deployment, once approved: a `lib/relationships/pledge-payment-plan.ts`

## Payment Plan Reconciliation Fix -- IMPLEMENTED, TESTED, DEPLOYED TO PRODUCTION, LIVE-VERIFIED (2026-10-13)

The owner approved the proposed late-payment dead-zone fix, extended
with an explicit amount-awareness requirement (partial payments must
never falsely satisfy a full installment; an oversized payment covering
multiple installments must not double-count). Implemented, tested,
built, deployed, and live-verified end to end this round.

### Scope decision on amount-awareness

Making the reconciliation amount-aware could in principle mean a full
redesign (a running amortization ledger replacing the per-cycle
windowed-matching model entirely) -- the owner's own task explicitly
asked to stop and present options if that were required. On design
review, it was not: the existing windowed-matching architecture (each
cycle gets its own non-overlapping date range, proven unambiguous by
the file's own correctness property) was EXTENDED, not replaced --
the new late-payment fallback pass now tracks real cents (summed,
oldest-eligible-payment-first, with leftover rolling forward to the
next unsatisfied cycle) instead of a bare boolean "any payment present"
check, while the existing, heavily-tested primary (near-exact-window)
pass is completely untouched. This stayed within the originally-
proposed fix's own shape, so no broader-redesign stop was needed.

### Implementation -- `lib/relationships/pledge-payment-plan.ts`

- `matchPaymentsToCycles` gained a new, OPTIONAL 4th parameter,
  `lateMatch: { amountsCents, installmentAmountCents }`. The existing
  primary pass (every call site/test in this suite that doesn't pass
  it) is byte-for-byte unchanged. When provided, a SECOND pass runs
  after the primary one, only for cycles still unsatisfied: any
  still-unused payment dated strictly between that cycle's own primary
  window and the start of the NEXT cycle's own primary window (or
  unbounded above, for the last cycle) is eligible. If
  `installmentAmountCents` is null, eligibility alone satisfies
  (amount-blind, matching the original narrower proposal). If a real
  installment amount is known, eligible payments' still-available
  amounts are summed (oldest first) until the full installment is
  covered -- a partial payment can never satisfy a cycle on its own --
  and any amount left over after satisfying one cycle rolls forward,
  unconditionally, to the next unsatisfied cycle (never backward),
  with each cent deducted from its source payment exactly once the
  moment it's actually consumed. The "one late payment must never
  retroactively erase multiple earlier genuinely-missed cycles"
  guarantee is structurally preserved: a cycle's own eligible range
  never starts before that cycle's own primary window ends.
- `PaymentPlanFields` gained an OPTIONAL `installmentAmountCents` field.
  `evaluatePaymentPlan` gained an OPTIONAL 6th parameter,
  `linkedPaymentAmountsCents` (parallel to `linkedPaymentDates`).
  Critically, `evaluatePaymentPlan` ALWAYS enables the late-payment
  pass internally (amount-blind if the caller omits the new amounts
  parameter) -- so every existing caller gets at least the date-only
  dead-zone fix automatically, with zero required changes, while
  `matchPaymentsToCycles` called directly (as its own dedicated unit
  tests do) stays fully opt-in/unaffected.

### Callers wired with real amounts (for full amount-aware correctness)

  (already selected `applied_cents` in its existing query; just needed
  threading through) and its own "Suggested Action" evidence

## "Open Pledge Has Gone Stale" Investigation -- Dr. & Mrs. Mordy Goldenberg (2026-10-13) -- READ-ONLY, ROOT CAUSE FOUND AND VERIFIED, FIX PROPOSED, NOT IMPLEMENTED

The owner reported Fundraising Intelligence Brief's "Worth knowing &
doing" section showing "Open pledge has gone stale" for this donor,
despite an active monthly payment plan whose next installment (Oct 23,
2026) is not yet due. Investigated entirely read-only against
Production, per the explicit instruction to report before implementing.

### 1-2. Donor's actual pledges, payment plan, and payment history

Donor `441e198c-...` (JL 64792) has **two simultaneously open pledges**
-- this multi-open-pledge shape is the entire story:

| Pledge | Campaign | Activity date | Balance | Payment plan? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `1c96676d-...` | KOLX2026 | 2026-08-11 | $11,000 of $12,000 | **Yes** -- monthly, $1,000/installment, next due **2026-10-23**, final 2027-08-23 |
| `11764b8e-...` | CHSP2026 | 2026-05-01 | $650 of $650 | No plan at all |

### 3. Does any EARLIER installment remain unpaid on the real plan? No -- verified directly

Ran the REAL, already-fixed `evaluatePaymentPlan` (same function, same
amount-aware late-payment logic from this session's prior round)
against KOLX2026's actual Production data (one real $1,000 payment,
2026-09-23, matching `jl_payment_assignment_audits` exactly) at
`now = 2026-10-13`:

```
isOnTrack: true, isLate: false, daysLate: 0,
nextUnsatisfiedExpectedPaymentAt: 2026-10-23
```

**This plan is genuinely, completely current -- no earlier cycle is
unsatisfied.** The owner's own description of the plan is exactly
correct. The "stale" classification is not disagreeing with this
plan's real status; it is not evaluating this plan AT ALL (see below).

### 4-5. Tracing the "gone stale" logic

`detectPledgeFollowUp` (`lib/fundraising-intelligence/situations.ts:166-204`):

```ts
const hasPlan = donor.pledgePlanOnTrack !== null;
const isStale = (hasPlan && donor.pledgePlanOnTrack === false)
  || (!hasPlan && ageDays !== null && ageDays >= 60);
```

In isolation, **this formula is correct** -- it already refuses to use
raw age when a payment plan exists, exactly satisfying requirement 7's
"an active payment plan... must not be classified as stale" for the
plan it actually looks at. The defect is entirely upstream: which
pledge `donor.pledgePlanOnTrack` was computed FROM.

### The real root cause: inconsistent "which open pledge" selection across the codebase

A donor can have multiple simultaneously open pledges. Three different
places in the codebase each pick ONE to represent "the" open pledge for
recommendation/evidence purposes -- and they do not agree:

| Surface | Selection rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Donor page (`Suggested Action`) | `ORDER BY activity_date DESC` then `.find()` -- **most recent** open pledge wins | `lib/relationships/giving.ts`'s `DONOR_GIVING_SQL` + `app/donors/[id]/page.tsx:314` |
| Daily Agenda / Today / SUGGESTED section | `ORDER BY ga.activity_date DESC`, first-seen-per-donor in a Map -- **most recent** wins | `lib/workspace/live-data.ts` (giving query + `openPledgeByDonor`) |
| **Portfolio Focus + Fundraising Intelligence Brief** | `.sort((a,b) => a.activity_date - b.activity_date)[0]` -- **earliest** wins | `lib/portfolio-focus/aggregate.ts:162` (`aggregatePortfolioFocusInputs`, shared by `lib/portfolio-focus/index.ts` AND `lib/fundraising-intelligence/compute.ts`/`index.ts`) |

For Goldenberg, KOLX2026 (Aug 11, the one with the active plan) is more
recent than CHSP2026 (May 1, the one with no plan at all). The donor
page and the Daily Agenda both correctly pick KOLX2026 -- which is
exactly why the owner's own description of "an active monthly payment
plan, next installment Oct 23" is accurate on those surfaces. Portfolio
Focus's aggregation (the ONLY one of the three sorted ascending) picks
CHSP2026 instead -- a real, genuinely neglected $650 pledge (no plan,
~165 days since its last activity, correctly age-stale on ITS OWN
terms) -- and `detectPledgeFollowUp` evaluates CHSP2026's
plan-less/aged state, under a generic "Open pledge has gone stale"
headline that does not name which pledge it means. The donor's actual,
well-managed, on-track KOLX2026 plan is completely invisible to this
one code path -- not disagreed with, simply never looked at.

**This is confirmed system-wide, not Goldenberg-specific**: any donor
with two or more simultaneously open pledges where the chronologically
EARLIER one lacks a payment plan (or is otherwise worse-off) than a
more recent one will hit the identical contradiction between Portfolio
Focus/Fundraising Intelligence and every other surface. This session
did not run a Production-wide query enumerating every such donor
(would require replicating the full multi-pledge-per-donor join this
investigation did by hand for one donor); flagged as unquantified
system-wide risk, matching this investigation's own read-only scope.

### 9. Consistency across surfaces -- confirmed NOT currently consistent

Directly contradicts requirement 9 as currently implemented: three
different tie-break rules for the same conceptual question ("which open
pledge represents this donor") exist in three different files. The
donor's dashboard and the Daily Agenda already agree with each other;
Fundraising Intelligence Brief (and Portfolio Focus itself) are the
odd ones out.

### 10. Does the recommendation disappear once conditions change? Yes, structurally, already

`app/fundraising-intelligence/page.tsx` uses `export const dynamic =
"force-dynamic"` and calls `computeFundraisingIntelligenceBrief(...)`
fresh on every page load -- no caching table, no persisted brief state
found anywhere in the schema. Once the pledge-selection defect is
fixed, this specific recommendation will correctly stop appearing (or
correctly start referring to CHSP2026 by name, or correctly report
KOLX2026 as on-track) on the very next page load, exactly like every
other recommendation surface already audited in this project -- nothing
about requirement 10 needs separate work.

### Proposed system-wide fix (not implemented -- awaiting approval)

**Recommended**: change the "which open pledge" selection rule in all
three places to the SAME rule, and make that rule stronger than pure
recency: **prefer a pledge that has an active payment plan over one
that doesn't; tie-break by most recent `activity_date`** (matching the
donor page's/Daily Agenda's existing direction). This is a materially
different guarantee than simply flipping Portfolio Focus's sort to
descending -- it structurally guarantees a donor's actively-managed
plan is never shadowed by an unrelated, unmanaged pledge, REGARDLESS of
which happens to be dated more recently (a sort-direction-only fix
would still break if a donor's OLDER pledge were the one with the
active plan -- the inverse of Goldenberg's specific case, but the same
class of bug).

Concretely: a small shared helper,
e.g. `selectRepresentativeOpenPledge(pledges, planByPledgeId)`, used by
`lib/portfolio-focus/aggregate.ts`'s `openPledgeRow`,
`app/donors/[id]/page.tsx`'s `openPledgeSource`, and
`lib/workspace/live-data.ts`'s `openPledgeByDonor` construction --
written once, reused three times, so the three surfaces can structurally
never diverge again (the same "single source of truth" principle this
session's prior payment-plan fix already applied).

**Narrower alternative, if the owner prefers the smaller change**: only
flip `aggregate.ts`'s sort to descending (matching the other two
surfaces' existing direction) without the plan-preference rule. Lower
risk, fixes Goldenberg and the common case, but leaves the
plan-preference guarantee (and therefore the strict reading of
requirement 7) unaddressed for the inverse ordering.

### Production data implications

**None.** This is purely a pledge-selection/presentation defect in the
aggregation layer -- no `giving_activities`, `pledge_payment_plans`, or
`jl_payment_assignment_audits` row is wrong. No data correction of any
kind is needed for Goldenberg or any other donor once the code is
fixed.

### What was deliberately NOT done

No code was changed. No donation record, pledge balance, payment date,
or payment-plan term was modified. This recommendation was not
manually dismissed. No deploy was performed. Staging was not read or
written. **Per the owner's explicit instruction, stopping here, awaiting
approval before implementing or deploying this fix.**

are being retained after their underlying conditions change." Checked

**There is nothing to regenerate or invalidate once the fix lands** --
the very next page load after the pledge-selection fix is deployed
will correctly reflect the corrected state, with zero migration,

the owner's own new requirement ("a newly imported payment applied to
an existing pledge must be reflected in both payment-plan status and
recommendations"): since nothing is ever cached, a new payment already
flows through immediately today, and will continue to once this fix is

never about staleness of the evaluation itself.

Root cause, verification, and proposed fix are otherwise unchanged from

between the two investigation rounds. **Still stopped, per the owner's

## Multi-Open-Pledge Independent Evaluation -- IMPLEMENTATION DESIGN (2026-10-13) -- DESIGN ONLY, NOT CODED, NOT DEPLOYED

The owner approved proceeding, but explicitly rejected the "pick one
representative pledge" fix from the prior round ("Do not simply
prioritize active payment plans if doing so could hide another
genuinely neglected pledge") and asked for every open pledge to be
evaluated independently instead. This section is the requested design,
with compatibility risks, before any code is written.

### Why the simpler fix was rejected (confirmed correct to reject)

A "prefer the pledge with a plan, tie-break by recency" rule still
collapses a donor down to ONE evaluated pledge. For Goldenberg
specifically it would produce the right answer (KOLX2026 has the plan
AND is more recent), but for a donor where the OLDER pledge is the one
with the active plan and a NEWER pledge is the genuinely neglected one,
that same rule would flip to picking the plan-having one correctly
only by coincidence of a tie-break order, and a donor with TWO
genuinely different pledge situations would still only ever surface
one of them, silently dropping the other's real status either way.
Only evaluating every open pledge independently removes this
coincidence entirely.

### Scope boundary (and why) -- the single biggest compatibility-risk decision in this design

`RecommendationEvidence.giving.openPledge` (`lib/relationships/
recommendation-evidence.ts`) is a SINGLE pledge object, and it is read
by four genuinely different consumers, not just the one that generates
the stale-pledge text:

| Consumer | File | Uses `openPledge` for |
|---|---|---|
| `follow_up_pledge` candidate | `recommendation-candidates.ts:128` | the exact bug this investigation is about |
| Solicitation suppression | `recommendation-candidates.ts:208` | `if (evidence.giving.openPledge !== null) return null` -- an open pledge of ANY kind suppresses a NEW solicit candidate |
| Ask-vs-pledge-activity comparison | `recommendation-candidates.ts:285` | whether a pledge's own activity postdates a pending ask |
| Donor-level ranking | `recommendation-rank.ts:104` | scoring |
| Meeting Brief | `meeting-brief.ts:291/320` | a different feature entirely, never reported broken |

Separately, `PortfolioFocusDonorInput`'s singular pledge fields
(`openPledgeBalanceCents`/`pledgePlanOnTrack`/`pledgeAgeDays`/etc.,
`lib/portfolio-focus/types.ts`) feed Portfolio Focus's OWN already-
calibrated ranking/scoring/display (`score.ts`, `components.ts`,
`today-view.ts`, `attention-type.ts`, `dedicated-view.ts`, and the main
`PortfolioFocusExperience.tsx` UI itself -- confirmed by direct source
search), representing real, deliberate, multi-round calibration work
(`docs/PORTFOLIO-FOCUS-CALIBRATION-V2.md`/`-V3.md`) that was never
reported broken either.

**Turning either of these shared singular fields into an array would be
a cross-cutting change touching Meeting Brief, solicitation
suppression, donor ranking, and Portfolio Focus's own calibrated
scoring -- none of which are implicated in the reported defect, and all
of which carry real regression risk if touched without separate,
explicit review.** This design therefore deliberately does NOT change
either shared singular field's shape. Instead:

1. **A genuinely new, ADDITIVE field** carries full per-pledge
   independence to exactly the two places that need it (Fundraising
   Intelligence Brief and Portfolio Focus's own pledge-staleness
   detail) -- every existing consumer of the singular fields is
   completely unaffected, because nothing about those fields changes.
2. **The SINGLE pledge the shared fields still select** gets a smarter,
   shared, consistent selection rule (described below) -- improving
   Suggested Action/SUGGESTED-section/donor-page consistency without
   changing any consuming function's own signature or behavior once it
   has its one pledge.

If the owner wants Portfolio Focus's own ranked list view to ALSO
reason about a donor's second, differently-situated pledge (not just
Fundraising Intelligence Brief), that is a larger, separate initiative
reopening the already-calibrated V2/V3 scoring work -- flagged here as
an explicit option, not assumed or started.

### Part A -- genuinely independent per-pledge evaluation (Fundraising Intelligence Brief + Portfolio Focus's own pledge detail)

**New shared per-pledge evaluator** (new function, `lib/relationships/
pledge-payment-plan.ts` or a small new module next to it -- exact
location is an implementation detail, not a design decision): takes
ONE pledge's own balance/total/activity date/linked plan/linked
payments and returns its own on-track/late/no-plan/stale verdict, by
calling the EXISTING, UNCHANGED `evaluatePaymentPlan` (this session's
donor-61566 fix, reused verbatim -- requirement 8) when a plan exists,
or the EXISTING, UNCHANGED `classifyPledgeStaleness`
(`lib/portfolio-focus/stale-balance.ts`, confirmed already a pure
function of per-pledge-shaped inputs, needing zero changes itself) when
it doesn't. **Neither existing, already-tested function changes at
all** -- this evaluator only changes HOW MANY times, and with which
pledge's own data, they get called.

**`lib/portfolio-focus/aggregate.ts`**: adds a new field,
`openPledges: OpenPledgeEvidence[]`, to `PortfolioFocusDonorInput` --
one entry per `giving` row with `balance_cents > 0` for that donor
(Goldenberg: two entries, KOLX2026 and CHSP2026), each independently
run through the new evaluator above. The EXISTING singular fields
(`openPledgeBalanceCents` etc.) are computed exactly as they are today,
completely unchanged, so every existing Portfolio Focus consumer is
unaffected -- this is a pure addition.

**`lib/fundraising-intelligence/situations.ts`**: `detectPledgeFollowUp`
rewritten to read `donor.openPledges` instead of the singular fields:
evaluate every entry independently (never label an on-track plan
stale, per-pledge -- requirement 2), collect every pledge that is
either genuinely behind schedule (has a plan, not on track) or
genuinely stale (no plan, old), and -- since the Brief's own
architecture is deliberately one situation card per donor (unchanged
by this design, a pre-existing, documented constraint, not something
this fix is expected to lift) -- surface the single highest-priority
one (an off-track PLAN beats a plan-less stale pledge, matching Tier
1's existing "DO" urgency convention) with:
- the headline/explanation naming that pledge's own campaign explicitly
  ("The CHSP2026 pledge has gone stale," never a generic "Open pledge
  has gone stale" -- requirement 3),
- one additional evidence/explanation line naming any OTHER open
  pledge and its own status when more than one exists ("A separate
  KOLX2026 payment plan is on track, next installment Oct 23" --
  requirement 4/7's "without losing the other pledge's status").
`detectCommitmentProgress` updated the same way (iterate, consider each
pledge's own near-complete/on-track state independently) so a donor
with one near-complete AND one stale pledge correctly surfaces the
stale one as Tier 1's "DO," never silently shows only the good news.

### Part B -- smarter single-pledge selection (donor page, SUGGESTED section, consistency)

The pledge `RecommendationEvidence.giving.openPledge` resolves to
(currently: most-recent `activity_date`, via `DONOR_GIVING_SQL` +
`.find()`/`openPledgeByDonor`) changes to: **prefer whichever open
pledge the new shared evaluator calls genuinely actionable (an
off-track plan, or a plan-less stale pledge) over one that's fine;
among equally-actionable or equally-fine pledges, keep today's
most-recent tie-break.** This is a same-shape, lower-risk change --
every one of the four consumers in the table above keeps working
exactly as it does today, they simply get handed the donor's actually-
most-relevant pledge instead of whichever happens to be most recent.
This is what brings the donor page's "Suggested Action" and the Daily
Agenda's SUGGESTED-section `follow_up_pledge` item into agreement with
Fundraising Intelligence Brief's own verdict about which pledge matters
(requirement 6), without restructuring Meeting Brief, solicitation
suppression, or donor ranking at all.

**Explicitly unaffected, re-verified by design, not just assumed**: the
Daily Agenda's real "Payment follow-up needed" / "Verify latest payment
import" line (`lib/workspace/live-data.ts`'s Recurring Payment Alert
loop) already iterates every ACTIVE PLAN independently today (`for
(const planRow of paymentPlanRows.results)`) -- it was never limited to
one pledge per donor and needs no change for this defect. The
donor-61566 late-payment dead-zone fix lives entirely inside
`evaluatePaymentPlan`/`matchPaymentsToCycles`, neither of which this
design touches (requirement 8) -- confirmed by design, will be
re-confirmed by re-running that round's own regression tests unchanged
once this is implemented.

### Requirement-by-requirement mapping

1. Evaluate every open pledge independently -- Part A's new `openPledges` array, one evaluator call per pledge.
2. Never label an on-track plan stale -- unchanged `evaluatePaymentPlan`/`classifyPledgeStaleness`, called correctly per-pledge now.
3. Identify the specific pledge/campaign -- new per-pledge headline wording.
4. Preserve legitimate follow-ups for other pledges -- evidence/explanation line naming the other pledge(s); Part B ensures the SUGGESTED-section pledge selection also reflects the truly actionable one.
5. No duplicate/contradictory recommendations for the same pledge -- structural: each pledge contributes to at most one evaluator verdict, consumed once.
6. Consistency across Fundraising Intelligence/Portfolio Focus/donor pages/Daily Agenda -- Part A for the Brief and Portfolio Focus's own per-pledge detail; Part B for the donor page and SUGGESTED section; the Recurring Payment Alert already independent.
7. Highest-priority pledge chosen when only one slot exists, other pledge's status not lost -- the "off-track plan > plan-less stale > fine" priority order plus the explicit other-pledge evidence line.
8. Donor 61566 fix remains intact -- zero changes to `evaluatePaymentPlan`/`matchPaymentsToCycles`; re-run unchanged as part of the test plan.
9. Regression tests for both older-pledge-has-plan and newer-pledge-has-plan -- see test plan below.
10. Goldenberg's Oct 23 installment not flagged, CHSP2026 evaluated accurately -- the concrete scenario Part A's design is built around; will be the first regression test and the live post-deploy check.

### Test plan (not yet written -- this round is design only)

- New `tests/open-pledge-evidence.test.mjs` (or similar) at the new
  per-pledge-evaluator level: the exact Goldenberg shape (KOLX2026 on

- `tests/fundraising-intelligence.test.mjs`: `detectPledgeFollowUp`/

- `tests/recurring-payment-alert-e2e.test.mjs` and

- New end-to-end case reproducing "late payment applied to an existing

- Full `node scripts/run-tests.mjs`, `tsc --noEmit`, and a production

### Deployment plan (once this design AND the resulting code are both approved)

Build -> test -> `git diff --stat` review (expected: `lib/portfolio-

Fundraising Intelligence Brief, Portfolio Focus, and the real

### Not done this round

No code was written. No test was written. No file was changed except

## Multi-Open-Pledge Independent Evaluation -- IMPLEMENTED AND TESTED (2026-10-13) -- NOT DEPLOYED

The owner approved the design above. Implemented exactly as designed,

`result` parameter from the two rewritten detectors rather than leaving

- `lib/relationships/pledge-payment-plan.ts` -- two new, small, pure,
  exported primitives: `evaluateOpenPledgePlanStatus()` (wraps the
  real, unmodified `evaluatePaymentPlan()` for one pledge's own plan

  changed -- `evaluatePaymentPlan`/`matchPaymentsToCycles` (the

- `lib/portfolio-focus/data.ts` -- added `ga.source_campaign` to the
  existing giving query (one column, same WHERE/JOIN).
- `lib/portfolio-focus/aggregate.ts` -- extracted the existing
  single-pledge evaluation logic into a new, equivalent
  `evaluateOpenPledge()` helper (confirmed byte-for-byte behavior-
  preserving by the full existing Portfolio Focus test suite re-running
  unchanged), then called it once per EVERY open pledge a donor has to
  build a new, additive `openPledges` array. The existing
  `openPledgeRow`/singular fields that feed Portfolio Focus's own

- `lib/portfolio-focus/types.ts` -- new `OpenPledgeEvidence` type and

  `PortfolioFocusDonorInput`, with an explicit doc comment that it is

- `lib/fundraising-intelligence/situations.ts` -- `detectPledgeFollowUp`
  and `detectCommitmentProgress` rewritten to read `donor.openPledges`
  and evaluate every entry independently via the shared
  `isOpenPledgeActionable()`/the real `classifyPledgeStaleness()`
  (reused unmodified). Beyond the design doc: both functions' now-
  unused `result: PortfolioFocusResult` parameter was removed entirely
  (and the two call sites in `detectSituations` updated to match)
  rather than left as dead weight -- a cleaner outcome than the design
  doc's placeholder `_result`, confirmed zero other callers exist.
  `detectPledgeFollowUp` now: evaluates every open pledge, filters to
  the genuinely actionable ones, picks the highest-priority one
  (a behind-schedule ACTIVE PLAN outranks a plan-less stale pledge;
  larger balance tie-breaks), names that pledge's own campaign in the
  headline, uses PLAN-specific wording ("payment plan is behind
  schedule") instead of generic "has gone stale" wording when the

  the Suggested Action/`follow_up_pledge` SUGGESTED-section candidate)

- `app/donors/[id]/page.tsx` -- the donor page's own `openPledgeSource`

  this donor's own already-loaded `paymentEvents`/`paymentPlans`.
- Tests: `tests/pledge-payment-plan.test.mjs` (new unit tests for the
  two shared primitives), `tests/fundraising-intelligence.test.mjs`
  (its `donor()` fixture helper now auto-synthesizes a one-entry
  `openPledges` array from the pre-existing singular fields, so every
  one of that file's pre-existing fixtures keeps working unchanged),
  `scripts/run-tests.mjs` (registered the new test file), and the new
  `tests/multi-open-pledge.test.mjs`.

### Compatibility risks identified during implementation (and how each was resolved)

1. **`PortfolioFocusResult.pledgeStaleClass` becoming dead in two
   functions.** Once per-pledge `classifyPledgeStaleness()` calls
   replaced the single donor-level one, the `result` parameter these
   two functions received had nothing left to read. Resolved by
   removing the parameter entirely (and its two call-site arguments)
   rather than keeping an unused parameter -- confirmed via `tsc`/lint
   that no other code depends on this exact signature.
2. **Existing `tests/fundraising-intelligence.test.mjs` fixtures
   predate `openPledges`.** Every existing test in that file sets only
   the singular `openPledgeBalanceCents`/etc. fields; since
   `detectPledgeFollowUp`/`detectCommitmentProgress` no longer read
   those fields at all, every one of those tests initially broke (the
   detector now saw zero open pledges). Resolved in the test fixture
   helper itself (auto-synthesize the equivalent one-entry array from
   the singular fields when `openPledges` isn't explicitly overridden)
   -- confirmed by that file passing unchanged again afterward, with
   zero changes to any individual test case's own assertions.
3. **The `remainingRatio` near-complete filter and the
   `immaterial_artifact` staleness-class filter both used to run once
   per donor; moving them per-pledge changes WHICH pledge can
   independently qualify.** Verified deliberately with new test cases
   (Goldenberg's own two pledges have very different ratios/ages) that
   each pledge's own filtering is now independent, matching the
   design's explicit intent.
4. **Risk NOT taken**: `RecommendationEvidence.giving.openPledge` and
   Portfolio Focus's own calibrated scoring (`score.ts`/`components.ts`/
   the main ranked list view) were deliberately left completely
   untouched, per the design's own scope boundary -- confirmed by the
   diff itself (neither file appears in the changed-files list) and by
   the full existing test suite (Meeting Brief, solicitation
   suppression, donor ranking, Portfolio Focus's own regression/
   materiality/components/today-view/dedicated-view tests) passing
   completely unchanged.

## October 14 2026 Email Incident -- Investigation, Fix, and Independent Staging Verification (NOT DEPLOYED TO PRODUCTION)

The owner reported that the real "Fundraising Agenda" email received that
morning linked to `fundraising-os-staging.sgoldstein.workers.dev` instead
of `https://shimmydonors.org`. Investigated, root-caused, fixed, and
verified under explicit owner authorization -- Production deployment
explicitly withheld per that same authorization.

### 1. Investigation -- verified findings

- **The email**: sent 2026-10-14T13:01:09Z, `sgoldstein@nirc.edu` to
  itself, subject "Fundraising Agenda -- Wednesday, October 14." Every
  link in both the plain-text and HTML MIME parts points to
  `fundraising-os-staging.sgoldstein.workers.dev`. Confirmed via Gmail's
  RAW message format (base64-decoded MIME), not just the snippet.
- **The data in the email came from Staging's own D1, not just the
  links**: direct, read-only queries against both databases for
  Rosenbaum's pledge (`626e3556-...`) showed Staging's
  `balance_cents: 30000, paid_cents: 150000` (matches the email's
  "$150.00 expected · 3 days behind" exactly) versus Production's
  `balance_cents: 15000, paid_cents: 165000` (on-track, would never
  appear in an agenda at all). This is conclusive, independent proof the
  code ran with `env.DB`/`env.APP_BASE_URL` bound to Independent
  Staging -- not a link-only cosmetic bug, and not the architecturally
  separate Legacy ChatGPT Sites platform (`docs/DEPLOYMENT.md`), which
  has no access to this repository's `fundraising-os-staging-db` binding
  at all.
- **Ruled out**: a GitHub Actions dispatch (grepped `.github/workflows/`
  -- nothing references the agenda-send path); a Worker-name mismatch
  (`wrangler.staging.jsonc`'s `"name"` matches exactly what the email
  links to); causation from the prior day's own Staging verification
  work (there is no HTTP-reachable path to a real send -- enforced by
  this file's own pre-existing `tests/agenda-safety.test.mjs` assertion
  that the preview route never imports the Gmail-sending module).
- **The fix deployed the day before this incident was insufficient at
  the Cloudflare infrastructure level, not just the config-authoring
  level**: `wrangler.staging.jsonc` had carried an explicit
  `"triggers": { "crons": [] }` since 2026-10-13T13:32 UTC, redeployed
  with that same explicit-empty config two more times that same day
  (18:11 and 18:31 UTC) -- the most recent of those three deploys was
  ~18.5 hours before this morning's send. Despite that, Staging's
  `scheduled()` handler evidently still executed. I could not
  independently confirm the exact Cloudflare-side mechanism (the
  Cloudflare dashboard hit a login wall, and I did not enter
  credentials, per this session's standing rule; `wrangler` 4.92 has no
  read/list subcommand for registered Cron Triggers; I deliberately did
  not test Cloudflare's `/cdn-cgi/handler/scheduled` manual-trigger
  endpoint live during the original investigation, since it was inside
  the active send window and the pre-fix code had no deduplication
  guard, so testing it then would have risked sending a third real
  email). **The important, actionable conclusion regardless of the exact
  mechanism**: a `wrangler.jsonc` config change, however many times it
  is redeployed and however correct its own deploy output looks, cannot
  be trusted alone to guarantee a Worker's `scheduled()` handler never
  runs. The fix below does not depend on that trust.
- **A second, independent bug found during this investigation**:
  `wrangler.production.jsonc`'s `APP_BASE_URL` was
  `https://fundraising-os-production.sgoldstein.workers.dev`, never
  `https://shimmydonors.org` -- so even a correctly-environment'd
  Production email would have shown the workers.dev domain. Separately,
  `curl -D -` against `https://shimmydonors.org/` showed it is not a
  true Cloudflare Custom Domain for the Production Worker: it is a
  Cloudflare-zone-level **301 redirect** to that same workers.dev
  hostname (confirmed via the real `Location:` header, followed by a
  second Cloudflare Access 302 and the final 200). So even after this
  round's `APP_BASE_URL` fix, a clicked link will still bounce through
  the workers.dev hostname once, until that redirect rule is corrected
  outside this repository.

### 2. Why Production's own email did not arrive on October 14 -- verified facts vs. hypotheses

**Verified facts:**
- Only one "Fundraising Agenda" email exists for 2026-10-14 in Gmail
  (checked including Trash) -- the Staging-linked one. No second,
  correctly-linked Production copy arrived anywhere in the mailbox.
- `wrangler.production.jsonc`'s `"triggers"` was, and remains,
  `{"crons": ["0 * * * *"]}` -- confirmed present in the working copy
  and unchanged in the diff reviewed before the prior day's own
  Production deploy.
- The prior day's 18:48 UTC Production deploy output explicitly printed
  "Deployed fundraising-os-production triggers" and
  `schedule: 0 * * * *`, ~18 hours before today's expected 13:00 UTC
  firing.
- `isDailyAgendaSendHour`/`currentEasternHour` (`lib/agenda/timezone.ts`)
  is pure and environment-independent -- the same code, called with the
  same real timestamp, cannot evaluate differently for Production vs.
  Staging.
- `STAGING_OWNER_EMAIL` (the recipient variable, confusingly named but
  used identically by both configs) is correctly set to
  `sgoldstein@nirc.edu` on `wrangler.production.jsonc` too -- confirmed
  by direct read.
- `lib/logger.ts` writes only to `console.info`/`console.error`
  (Cloudflare Observability) -- there is no D1 or other queryable
  persistence of scheduled-invocation history anywhere in this
  codebase, so I had no way to directly query whether Production's
  `scheduled()` handler fired, succeeded, or threw.

**Hypotheses -- explicitly not verified, listed in order of how much
independent evidence supports each:**
1. Production's Cron Trigger, despite the prior deploy's output text,
   was not actually registered/active at Cloudflare's infrastructure
   level at 13:00 UTC today -- symmetric to the exact same unverified
   failure mode this whole incident is about. No way to confirm or rule
   out without Observability/dashboard access.
2. Production's `scheduled()` did fire, but `sendDailyAgenda` threw
   (e.g. a transient Gmail OAuth/network failure) -- per the
   pre-existing design this would have been logged and rethrown, so it
   would be visible in Observability, but invisible to every tool
   available this round.
3. Production's `scheduled()` fired and succeeded, but the resulting
   email never reached this mailbox (a Gmail-side delivery anomaly) --
   considered least likely: the Gmail search covered Trash and a 2-day
   window with no narrowing filters, and the prior day's own two
   Production-linked agenda emails (Oct 12 and Oct 13, both correctly
   linked once the environment was right) delivered normally to the
   same self-to-self mailbox.

**Recommendation**: this requires Cloudflare Observability/dashboard
access to resolve conclusively. It does not change anything about the
fix below -- the fail-closed guard and the real `APP_BASE_URL` make
Production's own successful send correct by construction once it does
fire; this open question is about *whether* it fires reliably at all,
which is a reliability question, not a correctness-of-content one.

### 3. Fix implemented

**A. Fail-closed environment guard, covering every scheduled email, not
only the Daily Agenda (new `lib/agenda/email-send-guard.ts`)**

`isRealEmailSendAllowed(environment)` is an **allowlist** of exactly one
value, `"production-independent"` -- deliberately not a denylist of
known-bad values, so any value this check has never seen (a typo, a new
build script, a genuinely missing/unresolved case) fails closed by
construction rather than silently failing open. Enforced inside
`sendGmail()` itself (`lib/agenda/gmail-client.ts`), the single chokepoint
every current real-email caller already goes through (the Daily Agenda
*and* the Backup Scheduling Reliability Stage 3 alert,
`lib/backup-alert/run.ts`) -- checked first, before even reading Gmail
credentials, so no current or future caller can reach a real Gmail API
call from any environment other than Independent Production, regardless
of whether that caller remembers to check first. A blocked attempt throws
`EmailSendBlockedError` (never a silent no-op), so a lingering Staging
trigger firing again is visible in Observability as a clear, named error
rather than invisible.

The identity it checks is `deploymentEnvironment`
(`lib/environment.ts`) -- a pure, **build-time-resolved** constant baked
into the bundle by the specific build script invoked
(`scripts/build-staging.mjs` sets `FUNDRAISING_OS_ENVIRONMENT:
"staging-independent"`, `scripts/build-production-independent.mjs` sets
`"production-independent"`, confirmed by direct read of both scripts) --
never a runtime config value like `APP_BASE_URL`, which this exact
incident showed can be wrong independent of which Worker is actually
running, and never anything derived from a request (there is no request
in a `scheduled()` invocation to derive anything from). This is a
strictly stronger trust boundary than anything URL-based.

**B. Concurrency-safe, persistent idempotency for the Daily Agenda (new
`lib/agenda/send-log.ts`, `drizzle/0043_agenda_send_log.sql`)**

One row per `(user_id, send_date)` (`send_date` = `easternDateKey(now)`,
the same DST-safe America/New_York calendar day the 9 AM send-hour guard
already uses). A single atomic UPSERT (`buildAgendaClaimQuery`) claims
the row before any send is attempted:

```sql
INSERT INTO agenda_send_log (user_id, send_date, status, claimed_at)
VALUES (?, ?, 'pending', ?)
ON CONFLICT(user_id, send_date) DO UPDATE SET claimed_at = excluded.claimed_at
  WHERE agenda_send_log.status = 'pending' AND agenda_send_log.claimed_at < ?
```

D1/SQLite serializes concurrent writers, so of any number of simultaneous
claim attempts for the same day, exactly one can ever report a changed
row; every other invocation observes zero and must not send. After a
successful send, `buildAgendaSentCommitQuery` marks the row `'sent'` --
the claim query's `WHERE status = 'pending'` can then never match it
again, regardless of age, so a confirmed send is permanent. Wired into
`runScheduledAgendaSend` (`lib/agenda/send-agenda.ts`) strictly after the
hour gate (so 23 of 24 hourly ticks never touch D1 at all) and strictly
before `sendDailyAgenda` (so a lost claim race never reaches Gmail).

**Chosen delivery semantics, explained (not just asserted):** Gmail's
send API has no idempotency-key support, so true "exactly once" is not
achievable from this side alone. This design deliberately chooses
**at-least-once** delivery: a claimed-but-failed or abandoned attempt
(the invocation threw, or the Worker was killed mid-flight) is left
`'pending'` rather than explicitly released, and becomes reclaimable
once its `claimed_at` is older than `AGENDA_CLAIM_STALE_AFTER_SECONDS`
(120 seconds -- generous enough that a normal Gmail OAuth refresh+send,
observed well under a few seconds, is never mistaken for an abandoned
attempt still legitimately in flight, while short enough that a genuine
crash or hang is retried promptly within the same 60-minute Eastern-9am
window rather than only the following day). Crash recovery and
explicit-failure recovery deliberately share this one reclaim path
rather than two.

**Disclosed remaining risk** (the user's own explicit ask -- not hidden):
- *Duplicate-send risk*: if Gmail's send actually succeeds but the
  response is lost before this code observes success (a network
  partition, or a Worker CPU/wall-clock cutoff between the send and the
  commit), the row stays `'pending'`, a later invocation reclaims it
  after the staleness window, and a second, genuinely duplicate real
  email is sent for a day that was already, unknowably, delivered. This
  is the accepted cost of at-least-once semantics and cannot be fully
  closed without Gmail-side idempotency-key support, which does not
  exist.
- *Missed-delivery risk*: the claim-eligible window is bounded to the
  one Eastern-9am hour each day. If every attempt made during that
  specific 60-minute window fails (e.g. a Gmail OAuth outage spanning
  the whole hour), that day's email is genuinely not sent, and no
  further automatic retry happens until the same hour the next day.
  This is visible, not silent -- every failed attempt is still logged
  and rethrown by `runScheduledAgendaSend` (unchanged pre-existing
  behavior), so it surfaces in Observability even though no user-facing
  retry occurs that day.

This choice -- occasional duplicate accepted, silent miss avoided --
deliberately matches this codebase's own pre-existing philosophy for the
analogous backup-alert email (`lib/backup-alert/run.ts`'s own header
comment: the dedupe write happens strictly *after* a successful Gmail
send, so a post-send failure there already risks a duplicate alert
rather than a missed one) and the Daily Agenda's own pre-existing
failure handling (log-then-rethrow, never swallowed). Low-stakes
justification: this is an internal, single-recipient digest, never
donor-facing or financial.

**Per the user's explicit instruction, not assumed**: the two
environments' D1 databases being separate is *not* what prevents
cross-environment duplication here. `agenda_send_log` is per-environment
state (each D1 has its own copy) and would do nothing by itself to stop
Staging from sending if it ever reached a send attempt -- it is Part A's
fail-closed allowlist, enforced inside `sendGmail()` regardless of which
environment's D1 the caller is bound to, that ensures only one
environment can ever reach a real send at all. The idempotency table
only ever matters for whichever single environment's own `scheduled()`
handler the allowlist has already decided is allowed to send.

**C. `APP_BASE_URL` corrected to `https://shimmydonors.org`
(`wrangler.production.jsonc`) -- SOURCE ONLY, NOT DEPLOYED**, per the
owner's explicit instruction. The still-required, separate,
Cloudflare-zone-level redirect-rule correction (shimmydonors.org's
existing 301 pointed at the workers.dev hostname needs to become a real
Custom Domain binding instead) remains outside this repository and
requires the owner's own action in the Cloudflare dashboard -- not
something any command in this repository can perform.

**D. Stale comments corrected.** `worker/index.ts`'s and
`lib/agenda/send-agenda.ts`'s header comments on the `scheduled()`
handler and `runScheduledAgendaSend` still said the cron was "registered
in wrangler.staging.jsonc," left over from before the 2026-10-12
Production Daily Email Cutover and never updated -- actively misleading
for the next reader (human or AI). Both now describe the real,
current state and explicitly name `email-send-guard.ts` as the actual
safety boundary, not the wrangler config.

  succeeds exactly once; a second, simultaneous claim attempt for the
  same day changes zero rows (the concurrency-safety property); a
  `'sent'` day can never be re-claimed, immediately or after any amount
  of time; a stale `'pending'` claim (crash/failure recovery) becomes

## Production Health Correction -- Stale Baseline Stamp No Longer Blocks Launch Readiness (2026-10-14), DEPLOYED TO PRODUCTION

The owner authorized a permanent, design-level correction to the
Production Health warning (rather than a one-line data re-stamp) and
explicitly authorized its Production deployment, subject to the safety
checks below.

### 1. Root cause, confirmed via source (not re-investigated from scratch)

`lib/data-health/model.ts` already carried its own comment explaining
that `production_schema_baseline` "is a historical, point-in-time
stamp -- it is never rewritten automatically when a later migration is
applied" -- and Independent Staging's own analogous "Baseline lineage"
card already treated a stale stamp (`hash-mismatch`) correctly, as
informational (`"info"`), non-blocking. Production's own equivalent
logic never got the same treatment: `productionBaselineCheck`'s
`hash-mismatch` branch rendered `status: "critical"`, value `"0019 ·
Mismatch"`, `businessDataAtRisk: true`, and `repairStep: "Do not
launch."`; the inline "Production migration history" card collapsed
"verified" and every non-verified state into a flat
healthy/"Unverified" binary; and `productionBaselineApplied` (the
variable actually feeding `productionReady`/`productionBlockers`) only
accepted the literal `"verified"` state. All three compounded into
exactly what migration `0043_agenda_send_log.sql` triggered: Production
Health read "Needs attention" / "Blocked" despite the live schema being
structurally correct the entire time (proven by the same report's own
"Production ↔ baseline schema: Match").

### 2. Fix -- `lib/data-health/model.ts` only, no other file

- `productionBaselineCheck`'s `hash-mismatch` branch: `critical` ->
  `info`, `"0019 · Mismatch"` -> `"0019 · Stale stamp"`,
  `businessDataAtRisk` `true` -> `false`, `repairStep` `"Do not
  launch."` -> `"None. ... not a repair, and never automatic."` -- now
  matching Independent Staging's own `INDEPENDENT_STAGING_BASELINE_
  STATUS` precedent for the identical fact, word-for-word in spirit.
- New `productionMigrationHistoryCheck()` function replaces the old
  inline verified/non-verified binary: `"verified"` and
  `"hash-mismatch"` both now correctly answer "yes, genuinely created
  from the verified baseline" (critical only for
  `not-applied`/`unreadable`/`not-applicable` -- states that genuinely
  could not confirm that), with the stale case showing an explicit
  `"Baseline 0019 · Stale stamp (date)"` value instead of a flat
  `"Unverified"`.
- `productionBaselineApplied` (inside `buildDataHealthReport`)
  redefined from `state === "verified"` to `state === "verified" ||
  state === "hash-mismatch"` -- this is the one change that actually
  stops a stale stamp from reaching `productionReady`/
  `productionBlockers`. Every other readiness input --
  `facts.schemaMatchesBaseline` ("Production ↔ baseline schema"),
  `liveSchemaMatchesExpectedLevel` ("Live schema version"),
  `givingHealthy`, `relationshipIntegrityHealthy`, and backup/restore
  freshness -- is completely untouched and still independently blocks
  launch readiness on any genuine failure.
- **The distinction the owner asked to be preserved is preserved
  exactly**: historical baseline record ("Production rehearsal
  baseline"/"Production migration history," now correctly
  non-blocking for a stale-but-genuine stamp) vs. current schema
  integrity ("Production ↔ baseline schema" -- unchanged, still fully
  blocking) vs. migration verification ("Live schema version" --
  unchanged, still fully blocking) vs. backup/restore readiness
  ("Automated backup"/"Monthly restore test" -- unchanged, still fully
  blocking). None of these four were merged or conflated by this fix.
- **`production_schema_baseline`'s historical hash was never
  overwritten anywhere** -- this is a pure read-side/display-logic
  correction. No D1 write of any kind appears in this diff.

### 3. Regression tests -- comprehensive, as requested

`tests/production-readiness-diagnostics.test.mjs`: updated the two
pre-existing hash-mismatch assertions (legacy `"production"` and
`"production-independent"`) to their corrected values and added:

- A dedicated test for the new "Production migration history" card's
  stale-stamp wording, and a second proving it stays visibly distinct
  (`"Unverified"`, critical) from a genuinely missing marker
  (`not-applied`).
- Seven new **overall `report.status` rollup** tests (not just
  individual check fields -- what the owner actually sees as "Healthy"
  vs. "Needs attention"): a stale stamp alone resolves to `healthy`;
  every genuinely blocking `productionBaselineState`
  (`not-applied`/`unreadable`) still resolves to `critical`; a genuine
  structural schema mismatch, a genuinely stale live migration level, a
  genuine relationship-data integrity failure, and a failed
  giving-total reconciliation all still resolve to `critical`,
  completely unaffected by this fix; and a stale stamp combined with a
  **genuinely failed backup** still blocks on the backup failure alone
  -- proving the fix cannot mask an unrelated real problem.

### 4. Implemented and tested in Staging first

Built and deployed to Independent Staging (`pnpm run
build:staging-independent` / `deploy:staging-independent`) before any
Production action. **Staging Worker version:
`c4f99303-a4b1-450c-85f4-8887ea670a75`.** Live-verified, read-only:
Staging's own "Baseline lineage" card (built by the pre-existing,
unaffected `independentStagingSummaryChecks` code path -- Production's
specific cards this fix touches are gated behind
`isProductionEnvironment`, which Staging never satisfies) continued to

## Production Gmail OAuth 401 -- Root Cause Investigation (2026-10-14, read-only, resolves most of the prior audit's open questions)

The owner obtained real Cloudflare Observability evidence (access this
session does not have) and reported it verbatim: on 2026-10-14 at
9:01:16 AM Eastern, the **Production** Worker logged
`workspace_brief_render` immediately followed by **"Gmail token refresh
failed: HTTP 401 Unauthorized"** and `daily_agenda_send_failed`. The
dashboard also showed Production carrying an active hourly Cron
Trigger and Staging carrying none. **This investigation treats that
report as reliable, owner-supplied evidence** (this session still has
no Observability access of its own) and builds the analysis below on
top of it. Zero commands beyond read-only source inspection and
`wrangler secret list` (names only) were run this round; **no secret
was read, no Google Cloud setting was touched, no email was sent, no
deploy occurred.**

### 1. This resolves three of the prior audit's open questions directly

- **Production's Cron Trigger is real and fires on schedule.** The
  9:01:16 AM Eastern timestamp matches this session's own DST-safe
  analysis exactly (13:01 UTC = 9:01 AM EDT on 2026-10-14) and is
  consistent with `workspace_brief_render` succeeding immediately
  before -- the data-loading half of the pipeline worked. The
  previously-disclosed "cannot verify whether Production's cron
  actually fires" gap is now closed, affirmatively, in Production's
  favor.
- **Staging currently has zero registered Cron Triggers**, per the
  owner's own dashboard check -- consistent with (not contradicting)
  the earlier finding that it kept firing through the morning of
  2026-10-14 itself: the Staging redeploys that implemented and tested
  the fail-closed guard (versions `95310d2e-...` and later) all happened
  *after* that morning's 13:01 UTC send, so it remains entirely
  plausible one of those later redeploys is what finally cleared the
  live trigger, consistent with Cloudflare's own best-effort sync
  behavior already documented in this incident's history.
- **A genuine Production send attempt, and its specific failure point,
  are now established**: the pipeline reached the Gmail OAuth
  token-refresh call and Google's own token endpoint
  (`oauth2.googleapis.com/token`) rejected it with HTTP 401.

### 2. What a 401 (vs. 400) on Google's token-refresh endpoint specifically means

`lib/agenda/gmail-client.ts`'s `refreshAccessToken()` (re-read this
round, confirmed unchanged) sends exactly one request:
`POST https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token`, form-urlencoded body
`client_id`, `client_secret`, `refresh_token`, `grant_type=refresh_
token`. Per the OAuth 2.0 spec (RFC 6749 §5.2) and Google's own
implementation of it, the token endpoint distinguishes two different
rejection classes by HTTP status:

- **`invalid_client` -> HTTP 401**: the authorization server could not
  authenticate the *client itself* -- the `client_id`/`client_secret`
  pair is wrong, unrecognized, or the client has been deleted/disabled.
  This check happens **before** Google ever looks at the refresh token.
- **`invalid_grant` -> HTTP 400**: the client authenticated fine, but
  the specific `refresh_token` presented is invalid, expired, revoked,
  or was issued to a *different* client than the one now authenticating.

**The observed failure is 401, not 400.** Per this spec-level
distinction, the evidence points first and most strongly at Production's
stored `GMAIL_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID` and/or `GMAIL_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET`
values being wrong, mismatched, or referring to a client Google no
longer recognizes -- **not**, primarily, at the refresh token's own
validity. Per the explicit instruction not to assume the refresh token
is invalid without identifying the cause: this distinction is exactly
that identification, and it points away from the refresh token as the
primary suspect, not toward it.

Two of the specific risks the original OAuth setup research flagged
(docs/AI-HANDOFF.md's "Daily Fundraising Agenda Email" investigation,
point 9) are **not consistent with a 401** and can be reasonably
deprioritized as the explanation here: exceeding the 50-live-refresh-
token cap, and manual revocation at `myaccount.google.com/permissions`
-- both invalidate a specific *grant*, which Google surfaces as
`invalid_grant`/400, not a client-authentication failure.

### 3. Do Production's client ID, client secret, and refresh token belong to the same authorization?

**Cannot be determined by reading the values** (forbidden by this
round's own safety constraint, and Cloudflare Worker secrets are
write-only even to the account owner once set -- there is no "view" to
compare against). **But comparative behavioral evidence answers the
more important question**: Staging's Gmail credentials are proven
working right now -- a real token refresh + send succeeded as recently
as this morning (2026-10-14, Section "Pre-October-15 Read-Only Audit"
above) and on at least four prior consecutive days. **If the underlying
Google OAuth Client itself (the Internal "gmail.send" app) were
deleted, disabled, or had its secret regenerated, Staging's credentials
-- which were set up against that exact same client -- would fail
identically.** They did not. This rules out a client-wide, Google-side
problem as the explanation and narrows the cause specifically to
**Production's own stored secret values on Cloudflare** -- most likely
entered incorrectly during the one manual step in this whole chain
that was never automated: "the owner entered Production's three Gmail
OAuth secrets directly in the Cloudflare dashboard" (the "Complete
Production Daily Email Cutover" entry above). A manual, one-time,
three-long-string dashboard entry is exactly the kind of step where a
transcription error, a truncated paste, incidental whitespace, or the
client ID and client secret being pasted into each other's fields
would produce precisely this symptom -- all equally plausible
candidates, none confirmable without the owner's own comparison
against Google Cloud Console (which this session cannot access).

### 4. Recommended correction -- NOT performed, requires the owner's separate explicit approval

**Preferred approach: re-point Production at the exact same,
already-proven-working Internal OAuth Client Staging uses**, rather
than guessing at what's wrong with Production's current values:

1. **In Google Cloud Console** (the project containing the Internal
   `gmail.send` OAuth app from the original 2026-08-26 setup): APIs &
   Services -> Credentials -> locate that exact OAuth 2.0 Client ID.
   Confirm it still exists and is not deleted/disabled. Its Client ID
   is visible directly (not secret, by OAuth convention); its Client
   Secret can be re-copied or, if needed, reset from that same page.
2. **In Cloudflare**, overwrite (not compare -- secrets cannot be
   diffed, only replaced) Production's two values to match exactly:
   `wrangler secret put GMAIL_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID --config
   wrangler.production.jsonc` and `wrangler secret put
   GMAIL_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET --config wrangler.production.jsonc`
   (interactive prompts; values never echoed, matching every prior
   secret-entry round in this project's history).
3. **The refresh token requires one more judgment call**: a refresh
   token is cryptographically bound to the specific client that issued
   it. If Production's *existing* `GMAIL_OAUTH_REFRESH_TOKEN` was
   originally minted against this same Client ID, leaving it as-is
   after step 2 should be sufficient. If there's any doubt how it was
   originally obtained, the safer path is minting a **fresh** one:
   repeat the original one-time interactive authorization (Google's
   OAuth Playground, "use your own OAuth credentials," pointed at the
   Client ID from step 1, scope `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/
   gmail.send`) and `wrangler secret put GMAIL_OAUTH_REFRESH_TOKEN
   --config wrangler.production.jsonc` with the newly-issued value.

## Production Gmail OAuth 401 -- Second Root-Cause Round, Read-Only (2026-10-14)

The owner explicitly instructed: do not assume another copy/paste mistake;
investigate systematically before asking for a third credential re-entry.
**This round was entirely read-only** -- source inspection, `wrangler
deployments list`, `wrangler secret list` (names only), and the one D1 read
already shown above. No secret was read, no OAuth client or Cloudflare
setting was modified, no new email was sent, no new claim was created, and
the failed test record above was left untouched.

### 1. Ruled out: deployment/propagation problems

`wrangler deployments list --config wrangler.production.jsonc` shows every
version at **100%** -- there is no gradual/split rollout on this Worker, so
there is no scenario where some traffic still hits a pre-update version with
stale secrets. The secret updates landed at `2026-10-14T15:29:02.755Z`
(`GMAIL_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID`) and `15:30:19.921Z` (`GMAIL_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET`);
every deployment since, including the test-send mechanism's own
`1527fa4f-...` (`16:03:01.257Z`) -- the version that actually served the
request above -- was created strictly after both. Cloudflare Worker
deployments always carry forward the Worker's current secret values, so the
call that failed definitely used the newly-entered credentials, not stale
ones.

### 2. Ruled out: duplicate/ambiguous configuration

`wrangler secret list --config wrangler.production.jsonc` shows exactly the
three expected secret names (`GMAIL_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID`,
`GMAIL_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET`, `GMAIL_OAUTH_REFRESH_TOKEN`) -- no stray,
misspelled, or duplicate-looking secret name exists alongside them.
`wrangler.production.jsonc` has a single flat config with no named `env.*`
blocks, so there is no "secret landed on the wrong named environment"
scenario possible here (unlike projects that use Wrangler's multi-environment
feature) -- this file has only one environment, full stop.

### 3. Ruled out: the request never reached Google using Production's real secrets

`sendGmail()`'s fail-closed allowlist (`isRealEmailSendAllowed`) is the first
statement in that function, before credentials are even read. The test
request returned a **Gmail-specific 401 from `oauth2.googleapis.com/token`**,
not `EmailSendBlockedError` -- which is only possible if `deploymentEnvironment`
correctly resolved to `"production-independent"` and the call genuinely
reached Google using Production's own stored secret values. This also
confirms (re-reading `scripts/build-production-independent.mjs` and
`package.json`'s `deploy:production-independent` script, both unchanged) that
the correct, dedicated build/deploy path was used, not the legacy
`build:production` script that sets a different environment value.

### 4. Not yet ruled out, and not rule-out-able without more information: which specific credential is wrong

`lib/agenda/gmail-client.ts`'s `refreshAccessToken()` deliberately never reads
the response body on failure -- only `response.status`/`response.statusText`
are captured, by design (see that file's own header comment: a Gmail/Google
error body must never reach a log line or thrown-Error message, since it
could in principle echo request contents). **This is the single biggest gap
preventing a more specific diagnosis.** Per RFC 6749 section 5.2, Google's token
endpoint returns a 401 with a JSON body `{"error": "invalid_client",
"error_description": "..."}` for a bad/unrecognized client, versus a 400
`invalid_grant` for a bad refresh token -- but confirming this is really
`invalid_client` (and reading Google's own `error_description`, which often
says something specific like "The OAuth client was not found" or "Unauthorized")
requires actually reading that response body, which the code today never
does.

**This response body is safe to read and surface.** Google's OAuth 2.0 token
endpoint error response is a fixed, well-documented, two-field JSON shape
(`error`, `error_description`) describing the *rejection itself* -- it is
generated by Google's server, not an echo of the request, and contains no
credential, token, or secret value by construction. Surfacing just those two
fields (never the raw body, never request contents) would not violate this
round's "no secrets in logs" constraint.

### 5. Leading hypotheses, in order of likelihood, given everything ruled out above

1. **The re-entered `GMAIL_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID` and/or `GMAIL_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET`
   still don't match a real, enabled Google OAuth client exactly** --
   transcription error, incidental whitespace, a partial paste, or the two
   values swapped between fields. This was the leading theory before the
   first correction and evidently was not resolved by it.
2. **A client/token mismatch**: the deployment log shows
   `GMAIL_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID` was itself explicitly updated (not just the
   secret), which means the Client ID value changed, not only the secret
   tied to an unchanged client. If that new Client ID refers to a
   *different* OAuth client than the one that originally issued the
   unchanged `GMAIL_OAUTH_REFRESH_TOKEN`, Google would reject the pair --
   classically surfaced as `invalid_grant`/400 per the RFC, but Google's
   implementation is not guaranteed to follow that mapping strictly in every
   case, so this cannot be excluded on status code alone.
3. **The Google Cloud OAuth client itself is disabled, deleted, or
   misconfigured** -- lower likelihood, since nothing in this session's
   evidence points at it directly, but not excludable without Google Cloud
   Console access (which this session does not have and will not attempt to
   sign in to).

No command exists in this session that can distinguish between these three
without either (a) reading Google's own `error`/`error_description` from a
real attempt, or (b) the owner directly comparing the values in Google Cloud
Console against what's stored in Cloudflare -- something only the owner can
do, since Cloudflare secrets are write-only even to the account owner once
set.

### 6. Precise next corrective action -- NOT implemented, requires explicit authorization

Add a minimal, narrowly-scoped capture of Google's own `error`/
`error_description` fields (only those two fields; never the raw body; same
"never log a credential" discipline this file already follows) in
`refreshAccessToken()`'s failure branch, so the next attempt's D1 failure
record reads something like `"Gmail token refresh failed: invalid_client --
The OAuth client was not found."` instead of just a bare HTTP status. This
would turn hypothesis 1 vs. 2 vs. 3 above from a guess into a direct answer,
without the owner needing to blindly re-enter credentials a third time.

This requires: a small, reviewed code change to `gmail-client.ts`; the full
test/lint/typecheck gate; a Staging deploy (to confirm the code path shape
only -- Staging's guard still blocks any real send, so this cannot verify

### What was built

- `lib/agenda/oauth-error-code.ts` (new, dependency-free, directly
  unit-testable -- same split this codebase already uses for
  `mime-message.ts`): `extractAllowlistedOAuthErrorCode(body)` returns one of
  a fixed 7-code allowlist (`invalid_request`, `invalid_client`,
  `invalid_grant`, `unauthorized_client`, `unsupported_grant_type`,
  `invalid_scope` -- the full RFC 6749 section 5.2 token-endpoint set -- plus
  Google's own `deleted_client` extension) or `null`. Never reads
  `error_description`; never returns a code outside the allowlist; a

  all degrade to `null`.

  attempts `extractAllowlistedOAuthErrorCode(await response.json())` inside a
  `try/catch` (so a non-JSON or malformed body never throws past this point)
  and appends the result, if any, as `(code)` to the existing status-only
  message -- e.g. `"Gmail token refresh failed: HTTP 401 Unauthorized
  (invalid_client)"` instead of just the bare status. `sendGmail()`'s
  fail-closed Production-only guard (`isRealEmailSendAllowed`) and the
