  round-trips correctly; `error_description` never affects the result;
  non-allowlisted codes (including a crafted string that merely *contains*
  an allowlisted substring padded with extra text) are discarded; every
  malformed shape (`null`, a bare string, a number, an array, an object with

  `error_description` is never read, that the failure branch's parsed body

### Step 1: a safety check DID fail -- a self-introduced deployment-process incident, found and corrected before the test ran

Verifying "Production is running the new diagnostic code and the guard
remains intact" (requirement 1) surfaced a real problem: a fresh,
cache-disabled fetch of `https://shimmydonors.org/` was rendering the
`app/layout.tsx` `StagingBanner()` -- server-rendered, and only ever shown
when the Worker's own **build-time-baked-in** `deploymentEnvironment` equals
`"staging-independent"` (confirmed via `cache-control: no-store, must-revalidate`
on the response and a `cf-ray` header proving it was a genuine live request,
not a cached one).

**Root cause, fully traced:** during the prior round's own Staging test step,
`pnpm run build:staging-independent` was run to produce the Staging bundle
(correctly deployed to Staging). But the subsequent `pnpm run
deploy:production-independent` command **does not build** -- it deploys
whatever is currently in `dist/`, which at that point was still the
Staging-flavored bundle from the step before. The result: Production's
`6aece8e1` version had Production's correct D1 binding, secrets, cron, and
`APP_BASE_URL` (all controlled by `wrangler.production.jsonc`, independent of
the bundle), but the **application code itself** believed it was running as
Staging.

**Impact, assessed precisely, not performed to confirm:**

- `lib/agenda/email-send-guard.ts`'s `isRealEmailSendAllowed` would have
  **blocked** tomorrow's genuine 9 AM Eastern send with `EmailSendBlockedError`
  -- the real October 15 agenda email would NOT have gone out, with no
  credential problem at all being the cause.
- `lib/operations/staging-reset.ts:132`'s environment gate
  (`deploymentEnvironment !== "staging-independent"` -> 404) was satisfied,
  meaning `/api/operations/staging-reset` -- a **destructive, staging-only
  reset endpoint** that, per `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md`, deletes rows -- was
  reachable (not a 404) against **Production's real D1 database** for anyone
  who could separately pass its own owner-email check (the same single
  owner authorized on both environments; this is not an open vulnerability to
  a third party, but a defense-in-depth layer that exists specifically to
  prevent exactly this kind of accident was itself disabled). **This endpoint
  was never called** -- its exposure was identified from source
  (`authorizeStagingReset()`'s own logic) and corrected without ever invoking
  it, to avoid any risk of triggering it.
- Donor data, `agenda_send_log`, and the existing failed test claim were
  **not** affected by this incident at any point -- it changed which code
  branches were reachable, not any stored data, and nothing reachable through
  it was ever actually invoked.

**Fix applied and verified before proceeding:** `pnpm run
build:production-independent` (the correct script) rebuilt `dist/` fresh,
confirmed via `grep` to have `var deploymentEnvironment =
"production-independent";` constant-folded into the bundle (not merely
present as a string literal elsewhere). Redeployed --
**`554f865b-f859-45e9-bfdc-7481034bc418`**. Verified via a fresh,
cache-disabled fetch: the Staging banner is gone; a full page screenshot
after a hard navigation confirmed the same visually. Re-confirmed via
read-only D1 query immediately after: donors (254), giving activities
(5,464), `agenda_send_log` (0 rows), and the original failed claim row are
all exactly unchanged. This rebuild also happened to carry this round's own
already-gated-and-tested claim-ID change (see Step 2) in the same deploy,
since both were sitting in the working tree together -- not a scope
expansion, just one corrected deploy instead of two.

**Process lesson, recorded so it isn't repeated:** `deploy:*` scripts in this
repo never build -- always run the matching `build:*-independent` script
**immediately before** the matching `deploy:*-independent` script, with no
other build command in between, especially when a Staging test step is
interleaved before a Production deploy in the same session.

### Step 2: the minimal change, gated exactly as required

`lib/agenda/test-send-log.ts`'s `TEST_SEND_CLAIM_ID` advanced from
`"2026-10-14-production-gmail-oauth-verification"` to
`"...-verification-2"` -- the entire mechanism for authorizing one more
attempt, reusing the exact same atomic `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT(id) DO
NOTHING` idempotency already in place. This is the only source change this
round (`git diff --stat`: 1 file). Full gates re-run and passed: 188/188
tests (the e2e test imports the constant rather than hardcoding the old

"test-send-log"` that this module has exactly one importer in the entire
codebase (`app/api/agenda/test-send/route.ts`) -- nothing in the real

### Step 3: execution and result

With the owner authenticated at `https://shimmydonors.org` in their own
browser session, the one-time call was made:

```
POST /api/agenda/test-send -> 500
{ "error": "Gmail token refresh failed: HTTP 401 Unauthorized (unauthorized_client)" }
```

**This is a materially different, more specific result than the first
test's bare 401.** Per RFC 6749 section 5.2, `unauthorized_client` is
distinct from `invalid_client`: it means the client authenticated
successfully (Google recognized the `client_id`/`client_secret` pair as
real and matching) but that client **is not authorized to use the specific
grant presented** -- here, the `refresh_token` grant with this specific
`refresh_token` value. In Google's own implementation, this is the
well-documented symptom of presenting a `refresh_token` together with
`client_id`/`client_secret` from a **different OAuth client than the one
that originally issued that refresh token**.

This directly confirms hypothesis 2 from the prior root-cause round: the
deployment log independently showed `GMAIL_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID` was itself
explicitly updated (not just the secret) during the owner's correction, and
`GMAIL_OAUTH_REFRESH_TOKEN` was explicitly left unchanged. **The new Client
ID now stored on Production does not match the OAuth client that issued the
currently-stored refresh token.** Hypothesis 1 (a transcription/typo error
in the credential values themselves) is now ruled out -- a typo would
produce `invalid_client` (Google never recognizing the client at all), not
`unauthorized_client` (Google recognizing the client but rejecting this
specific grant).

## `unauthorized_client` -- What It Actually Means, and Owner Instructions for a New Refresh Token (2026-10-14, read-only, no credentials touched)

Per explicit instruction, this round confirmed `unauthorized_client`'s
meaning against Google's own documentation rather than relying on the prior
round's own inference, and does **not** treat it as definitive proof of a
refresh-token/client mismatch specifically.

### 1. What the research actually found

- **Google's own developer documentation does not define `unauthorized_client`
  for the token endpoint.** Two of Google's own pages were checked directly:
  the "Using OAuth 2.0 for Web Server Applications" guide (both halves of its
  content) and the Nest Device Access "Authorization Errors" reference.
  Neither mentions `unauthorized_client` at all. Google's docs define
  `invalid_client` ("the OAuth 2.0 Client Secret is incorrect") and
  `invalid_grant` (expired/invalidated/revoked token) explicitly, but this
  specific code has no first-party Google definition that could be found.
- **The generic OAuth 2.0 spec (RFC 6749 section 5.2)**, which Google's token
  endpoint implements, defines it generically: "the authenticated client is
  not authorized to use this authorization grant type." This is a real,
  load-bearing standard but is generic across all OAuth providers, not
  Google-specific guidance.
- **Third-party sources describe three distinct, real-world causes**, not
  one:
  1. **Client/refresh-token mismatch** -- a Google Developers forum report
     (a user got this exact error with an OAuth-Playground-issued refresh
     token; completing the authorization step for the correct client fixed
     it).
  2. **Wrong OAuth client type** -- a Gmail-SMTP-specific troubleshooting
     guide (WP Mail SMTP, itself built around the same `gmail.send`-via-
     refresh-token pattern this app uses) names this as **the single most
     common cause**: the OAuth credential was created as a **Desktop app**
     instead of a **Web application**.
  3. **Google Workspace admin restriction** -- the same guide describes an
     admin blocking third-party API access for a specific OAuth client in
     the Workspace Admin Console ("Manage Third-Party App Access"), which
     can apply per-client, not only domain-wide -- so a newly-created or
     newly-regenerated client could hit this even though the original,
     long-used client never did.
- **What the existing evidence (independent of this new research) still
  favors, without being definitive:** the deployment log shows
  `GMAIL_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID` was itself explicitly updated (a distinct secret
  -put event from `GMAIL_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET`), while `GMAIL_OAUTH_REFRESH_TOKEN`
  was explicitly left unchanged (confirmed, not assumed, via `wrangler
  deployments list`'s own per-secret labels). This is consistent with
  cause 1 (and arguably cause 2, if regenerating credentials meant creating
  a new client rather than rotating the existing one's secret) but does not
  rule out cause 3. **This document now states only what the evidence
  actually supports: the current Client ID/Secret pair and the current
  refresh token do not work together, for one of these three reasons, not
  definitively the first one.**

### 2. Should a new refresh token be issued for the existing Client ID/Secret?

**Yes -- this remains the correct next step regardless of which of the three
causes is actually true**, and it is informative either way:

- If cause 1 (mismatch): a new refresh token minted against the *current*
  Client ID/Secret directly fixes it.
- If cause 2 (wrong client type): the interactive authorization step itself
  may still succeed in issuing a token, but the question "is the current
  Client ID actually a Web application?" can and should be checked directly
  in Google Cloud Console (Credentials page) at the same time -- this is a
  **read-only check in Google's own console**, not something this session
  can do remotely.
- If cause 3 (Workspace-blocked): the interactive consent step commonly
  surfaces an explicit "blocked by your administrator" message, which would
  itself be immediately diagnostic and point straight at the Workspace Admin
  Console setting named above.

No credential was changed and no email was sent to reach this conclusion --
this section is pure research and analysis of the error already captured in
the prior round's D1 record.

### 3. Step-by-step instructions for the owner -- to be performed entirely outside this chat

**Nothing below should ever be pasted into this conversation.** The owner
performs every step in their own browser and their own terminal; this
session never sees, requests, or handles a credential or token value at any
point, matching this incident's established practice throughout.

1. Open [Google OAuth 2.0 Playground](https://developers.google.com/oauthplayground/)
   in your own browser.
2. Click the gear icon (top right) to open settings. Check **"Use your own
   OAuth credentials."** Enter the **Client ID** and **Client Secret**
   currently stored on Production (the same values you entered into
   Cloudflare earlier today). Close settings.
3. In the left panel's scope list (or "Input your own scopes" box at the
   bottom), enter exactly: `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.send` --
   this one scope only, matching the original setup.
4. Click **"Authorize APIs."** Sign in with the same Google/Workspace account
   this app sends email as, and approve. **If you see any message here about
   the app being blocked, restricted, or requiring admin approval, stop and
   note the exact wording** -- that would directly confirm cause 3 above and
   point at the Workspace Admin Console rather than the refresh token.
5. After the redirect back to the Playground (Step 2 of its own flow), click

6. Copy the **Refresh token** value shown (not the Access token -- this app

7. In your own terminal, with `wrangler` available, run:
   ```
   wrangler secret put GMAIL_OAUTH_REFRESH_TOKEN --config wrangler.production.jsonc
   ```
   and paste the refresh token only at that interactive prompt -- never into

8. Let this session know once that's done. Verification can then happen

## Deployment Safeguard Proposal -- Fail-Closed Build-Manifest Check (2026-10-14, NOT YET WIRED IN -- for review)

Kept deliberately separate from the Gmail repair above, per explicit
instruction. This section proposes, but does not activate, a fix for the
deployment-process class of bug found and manually corrected earlier today
(the "Staging-bundle-on-Production" incident).

### Independent re-investigation of the incident (requirement 5)

- **Root cause re-confirmed from first principles, not just re-asserted**:
  `package.json`'s `deploy:staging-independent` and
  `deploy:production-independent` scripts are, and always have been, exactly
  `wrangler deploy --config wrangler.*.jsonc` -- neither has ever invoked a
  build step. `dist/` is `/dist/`-gitignored (confirmed in `.gitignore`, line
  40; confirmed via `git check-ignore -v` and `git log -- dist/` returning
  nothing) -- meaning no build artifact from any past deploy, correct or
  not, was ever retained anywhere this session could inspect it after the
  fact. This is precisely why the bug was invisible until a live,
  cache-disabled fetch of the running Worker was checked -- nothing in
  source control could have revealed it.
- **Whether this happened in any earlier round**: this document's own history
  was searched for every past `build:staging-independent`/
  `build:production-independent`/`deploy:staging-independent`/
  `deploy:production-independent` mention (100+ matches). Every round that
  interleaved a Staging and a Production deploy explicitly logged a fresh
  `build:production-independent` immediately before its
  `deploy:production-independent` (e.g. the 2026-10-12 cutover round:
  "`build:staging-independent` -> `deploy:staging-independent` ->
  `build:production-independent` -> `deploy:production-independent`", in
  that exact order; the 2026-10-14 production/backup round similarly builds
  both independently and explicitly before each deploy). **No other
  documented round shows the broken sequence** (a Staging build with no
  intervening Production build before a Production deploy) -- today's
  incident appears to be an isolated, first-time slip, not a systemic
  pattern, though this is necessarily based on what was logged in this
  document rather than independent proof of every command actually run.

### Proposed implementation -- written, tested standalone, NOT wired into any deploy script

**New file, inert on its own:** `scripts/verify-build-manifest.mjs` -- reads
`dist/build-manifest.json`, exits non-zero (refusing to deploy) if it's
missing, was built for the wrong environment, or is older than 10 minutes
(catching a long-forgotten stale `dist/` the environment check alone
wouldn't). Takes the expected environment as its one argument. Has zero
effect unless something calls it.

**`scripts/build-production-independent.mjs` and `scripts/build-staging.mjs`**,
both edited identically: after a successful build only, write
`dist/build-manifest.json` with `{ environment, builtAt }`. This file lives
at `dist/` (not `dist/client/`, which is the only directory `wrangler`
actually uploads as static assets, and not `dist/server/`, which is the only
file `wrangler` bundles as the Worker itself) -- it is a pure local
build-tooling artifact, never deployed, never publicly served, never part of
the Worker bundle.

**Tested standalone, nothing deployed:** built Staging, confirmed the
manifest; ran the verify script asking for `"production-independent"` --
**it failed, reproducing the exact incident** ("dist/ was built for
"staging-independent", not the expected "production-independent". Refusing
to deploy..."). Built Production, confirmed the manifest; ran the verify
script asking for `"production-independent"` -- passed. Confirmed the
missing-argument case also fails closed. `node -c` syntax-checked all three
files; `pnpm run lint` re-run at the unchanged 94-error/43-warning baseline.

### Proposed `package.json` change -- NOT applied, for review only

```diff
-    "deploy:staging-independent": "wrangler deploy --config wrangler.staging.jsonc",
-    "deploy:production-independent": "wrangler deploy --config wrangler.production.jsonc",
+    "deploy:staging-independent": "pnpm run build:staging-independent && node scripts/verify-build-manifest.mjs staging-independent && wrangler deploy --config wrangler.staging.jsonc",
+    "deploy:production-independent": "pnpm run build:production-independent && node scripts/verify-build-manifest.mjs production-independent && wrangler deploy --config wrangler.production.jsonc",
```

This makes each `deploy:*-independent` command **always** rebuild
immediately before deploying -- eliminating the entire class of "stale or
wrong `dist/`" mistake at its root, not merely detecting it -- with the
manifest check as a second, independent layer of defense (e.g. against a
build script itself someday writing to the wrong environment without
actually failing). Because `&&` short-circuits, a failed build or a failed
verify both stop `wrangler deploy` from ever running.

### Risks and limitations, disclosed for review

1. **Does not cover raw `wrangler deploy` run outside these npm scripts.**
   Anyone invoking `wrangler deploy --config wrangler.production.jsonc`
   directly, bypassing `pnpm run deploy:production-independent` entirely,
   is not protected by this check. This matches every deploy actually
   performed and documented in this project's history (always through the
   `pnpm run deploy:*` scripts), but it is a real gap if that practice is
   ever not followed.
2. **Every deploy now always rebuilds**, adding the build's own duration
   (observed: well under a minute) to every deploy invocation, including
   ones where the `dist/` was already correct. This trades a small, constant
   time cost for eliminating the failure mode outright.
3. **The 10-minute freshness window is a judgment call.** Too short risks a
   spurious failure on a slow machine or network; too long weakens the
   "stale build" defense. 10 minutes was chosen as generously longer than
   any observed build time this session, but is easy to revisit.
4. **The manifest file itself is trusted input to the verify script** -- it
   is plain, unsigned JSON written by the same build process it's meant to
   check. It defends against the specific incident class (a leftover build
   from a *different, legitimate* build invocation), not against a
   deliberately falsified manifest, which was never the threat model here.

**Awaiting explicit approval before applying the `package.json` change above
and treating this safeguard as active.**

### Remaining bypass risks (unchanged from the proposal, restated for the now-active safeguard)

1. **Direct `wrangler deploy` run outside these npm scripts is not

   matches every deploy actually performed and documented in this project's
   history (always through the `pnpm run deploy:*` scripts), but remains a
   real gap if that practice is ever not followed, including by a future AI
   session that reaches for `wrangler deploy` directly instead of the npm
   script.
2. **CI/automation gap**: this repository has no CI pipeline this session
   has found that runs `pnpm run deploy:*` itself (deploys throughout this
   project's history have been manual, human- or session-initiated) -- so
   there is no separate automated enforcement point beyond the npm script
   itself. If a CI-based deploy pipeline is ever added, it should invoke the

3. **A manually/externally edited `dist/build-manifest.json`** would be
   trusted as-is -- the file is plain, unsigned JSON, and the safeguard's
   threat model is a stale-but-legitimately-built `dist/`, never a
   deliberately falsified manifest. Not a realistic risk given who can reach
   this project's filesystem, but worth stating precisely rather than
   implying a stronger guarantee than what was actually built.
4. **The 10-minute freshness window remains a judgment call**, unchanged
   from the proposal -- generous relative to observed build times, but not
   derived from a hard requirement.
5. **A build that silently writes the wrong `environment` value into the
   manifest** (a bug in `build-production-independent.mjs`/`build-staging.mjs`
   themselves, rather than in which script was run) would not be caught --
   the manifest is written by the same process it's meant to check, by
   design, since the actual incident class this responds to was "the right
   build script was run, just not immediately before the right deploy," not
   "a build script lied about what it built."

## Completed Outreach Action Fix (2026-10-14)

### The report

Today's Production Daily Fundraising Agenda recommended, for Mr. & Mrs.
Yaakov Zachter:

> **Reach out and reference:** Texted video from first day of Zman and
> thanked him for his support that makes it happen.
>
> **Why:** A specific, currently-relevant fact is on file and no open
> reminder currently covers this.

The owner had already performed that exact outreach -- the recommendation
was asking him to do something he had already done.

### Root cause (verified against real Production data, read-only)

Traced the exact donor record via read-only D1 queries against
`fundraising-os-production-db`:

```
donor_relationship_facts:
  id: 1550c6b7-ba7d-4bce-a819-a9cbfb320ee7
  donor_id: 19af69d6-f147-474b-88ad-f6358ff65b9a (Yaakov Zachter)
  category: engagement
  lifecycle: durable
  status: current
  fact_text: "Texted video from first day of Zman and thanked him for
              his support that makes it happen."
  source_interaction_id: null
  source_interaction_occurred_at: 1787336520  (2026-08-21, ~54 days ago)
```

`recommendations` for this donor: **zero rows** -- confirming "no open
reminder currently covers this" was literally true, and that the problem
was never a missing-reminder bug.

The actual defect is in `lib/relationships/fact-classification.ts`'s
lifecycle waterfall (`classifyFactLifecycle`). This fact's category
(`engagement`) is not one of the two singular-state categories
(`solicitation`, `health`), and its text matched neither
`COMPLETED_WELL_WISH_PATTERN` (no "wish ... happy birthday/mazel tov")
nor `COMPLETED_MILESTONE_EVENT_PATTERN` (no bare "<relation> had a/an
<event>" shape) -- the two existing, narrow patterns from the October 8
and October 12 fixes for this exact category of bug (see this file's own
earlier entries). With no step-3 signal firing, the fact fell through to
step 4's `durable` default and was given a fixed, never-decaying
relevance score (`DURABLE_BASELINE_SCORE = 0.3`), permanently clearing
`RELEVANCE_FLOOR` and staying "currently actionable" forever, regardless
of age. `isConfirmedOutreachCompletion()`'s completion-awareness check
(the October 12 fix) never even ran, because it only applies to
`time_bound` facts -- and separately, this fact's `source_interaction_id`
is `null`, so that mechanism could not have helped here anyway (it
requires a linked, confirming interaction row, which this backfilled fact
never had).

### Scope: systemic, not isolated to one donor

Investigating further (read-only) found a **second, independently-worded
live Production fact with the identical defect**:

```
donor_id: a5bde812-4bb0-456c-96f5-5f4960bd5cba
category: engagement, lifecycle: durable, source_interaction_id: (set,
  but linked interaction type is "personal", which
  OUTREACH_CONTACT_INTERACTION_TYPES already excludes)
fact_text: "Spoke with him and gave him a tour of the new gym."
source_interaction_occurred_at: 2026-08-24 (~51 days ago)
```

No shared vocabulary with Zachter's text at all -- proving the defect is
a general shape (a completed-action report defaulting to `durable`
whenever its category isn't singular-state and its wording doesn't
happen to match one of the two existing narrow phrase patterns), not a
donor-specific wording quirk. A full read-only scan of every
`status='current'` fact row in Production (12 rows total) found exactly
these 2 affected; the other 10 (4 solicitation, 6 family_milestone,
already `time_bound`) were correctly classified already.

The much larger population of donors with **zero structured
`donor_relationship_facts` rows** (the legacy `relationship_summary`/
`institutional_memory` free-text path in `relationshipOpportunityCandidate`'s
"legacy path" branch) has no per-fact date metadata at all and therefore
no decay or completion-awareness mechanism whatsoever -- a pre-existing,
already-disclosed architectural gap from the original Stage 1-3
migration design (see this file's "Relationship Snapshot Architecture"
entries), not something this fix could address without a much larger
migration, and not something newly introduced by this investigation. This
remains an **unresolved risk**, flagged below.

### The fix

`lib/relationships/fact-classification.ts` adds
`COMPLETED_OUTREACH_ACTION_PATTERN`: rather than a third narrow phrase
list, this generalizes the SHAPE -- a fact sentence that OPENS with a
past-tense outreach-contact verb (`called`, `texted`, `visited`,
`stopped by`, `dropped off`, `sent a/an text/email/card/gift/video/note`,
`emailed`, `wrote`, `spoke with/to`, `met with`, `wished`) is, by
construction, a narration of a completed action the fundraiser already
performed, never a standing fact about the donor. Wired into:

- `classifyFactLifecycle` step 3 (an additional `time_bound` trigger,
  alongside the two existing patterns).
- `resolveDecayWindowDays` (reuses the same fast, 30-day window as the
  two existing completed-touch patterns) -- **deliberately gated to
  non-singular-state categories only** (`!isSingularStateCategory`), so a
  solicitation/health fact keeps its own, deliberately longer 90/180-day
  window even if its text happens to open with a contact verb (e.g.
  "Called and discussed building naming opportunity." -- the call is
  done, but the ask itself may not be). This is the explicit guard
  against reintroducing the previously-fixed stale-pledge/solicitation
  problem.

Deliberately NOT wired into `isConfirmedOutreachCompletion`'s
interaction-summary confirmation side: that check must still verify the
linked interaction is topically about the SAME action (its own
`MILESTONE_OUTREACH_COMPLETION_PATTERN` requires a milestone noun), and
loosening it to "any contact verb anywhere in the summary" would let an
unrelated interaction wrongly suppress a genuinely different, still-open
fact (this is exactly what the existing "unrelated interaction must never
suppress" regression test in
`tests/relationship-fact-completion-awareness.test.mjs` protects against).
The fast decay window alone is sufficient to fix both real cases found
(both already well past 30 days old) without that risk.

### What was independently verified against real data vs. inferred from code

- **Verified live, read-only, against `fundraising-os-production-db`**:
  Zachter's exact fact row (category/lifecycle/text/null source
  interaction/occurred-at), the second affected donor's fact row and its
  linked interaction's `type`/`summary`, zero `recommendations` rows for
  Zachter, and a full scan confirming exactly 2 of 12 current fact rows
  are affected.
- **Verified via a throwaway, read-only dry-run script** (imported the
  real `classifyFactLifecycle` directly, fed it all 12 real Production
  rows, never written to the repo) that after this fix, **exactly those
  same 2 rows** compute a different lifecycle (`durable` -> `time_bound`)
  and **all 10 other rows are byte-identical** to their currently-stored
  value -- i.e., the fix touches precisely the affected population and
  nothing else. Script was deleted after use; not part of the commit.
- **Inferred from code, not independently re-derived**: the exact
  `relationshipOpportunityCandidate`/`findMostActionableFact`/`scoreFact`
  call chain that turns a `durable` fact into a permanent recommendation
  (already traced and documented in this file's October 12 entry;
  re-read, not re-verified against new evidence this round).

### Regression tests added

- `tests/relationship-fact-classification.test.mjs`: unit coverage for
  `COMPLETED_OUTREACH_ACTION_PATTERN`/`classifyFactLifecycle`/
  `resolveDecayWindowDays`, including the real Zachter and
  gym-tour-donor text, several other completed-touch openers (proving
  the fix is shape-based, not a second phrase list), the start-anchor
  sanity check (mentioning a touch in passing must not trigger it),

## Completed Outreach Action Fix, round 2 (2026-10-14)

The owner reviewed round 1 (above) with a second party and raised two
specific, correct objections, plus asked for the legacy pathway and the
Production correction plan to be addressed directly.

### What was found

**Objection 1 -- round 1 still had a grace window.** Round 1's fix gave a
completed-touch fact a shorter (30-day) decay window instead of the
previous never-decaying `durable` default. That is a real improvement
over the original bug, but it still meant a completed outreach action
could be recommended for up to 30 days after it was performed -- exactly
the outcome the owner said was still wrong: *"My goal is not simply to
make completed outreach recommendations disappear after 30 days. My goal
is to prevent Fundraising OS from recommending work that has already
been completed."*

**Objection 2 -- relying too heavily on vocabulary.** Investigated
whether today's schema has ANY field that structurally distinguishes "a
report of a completed one-time action" from "a standing fact about the
donor" without reading the sentence's own grammar. It does not: interaction
`type`, `occurred_at`, move/ask status, and `source_interaction_id` all
already exist and are already used (the completion-awareness mechanism
from the October 12 fix), but none of them records *what kind of sentence*
a fact's text is -- that is purely a property of the free text itself.
This is disclosed honestly rather than papered over with a fake
structural signal: **there is no way to make this determination today
without reading the fact's own text in some form.**

What the investigation DID find, though, is a genuine, principled
narrowing of which text shapes are actually ambiguous:

- An **EVENT report** ("Son had a bar mitzvah.", no stated actor) is
  genuinely ambiguous -- it could be a brand-new milestone the fundraiser
  hasn't acted on yet, or something from weeks ago already addressed.
  Age-based decay (round 1's approach, from the October 12 fix) is the
  right, conservative answer for this shape, and is UNCHANGED this round.
- An **ACTION report** ("Texted ... and thanked him for his support")
  names the fundraiser as the actor performing a contact verb. This
  cannot be ambiguous about completion: recording it as a fact in the
  past tense IS the record that the action already happened. There is no
  "not yet done" reading available. This is the shape round 1's fix
  (`COMPLETED_OUTREACH_ACTION_PATTERN`) and the October 8 fix
  (`COMPLETED_WELL_WISH_PATTERN`) both target, and is what justifies
  dropping the grace window entirely for exactly these two patterns,
  while leaving `COMPLETED_MILESTONE_EVENT_PATTERN` (the EVENT-report
  case) completely untouched.

**Legacy pathway**: a read-only Production scan found `relationship_
summary`/`institutional_memory` populated for exactly 12 donors, and all
12 already have a structured `donor_relationship_facts` row -- meaning
`relationshipOpportunityCandidate`'s legacy branch is **not currently
reachable by any donor in Production at all** (`hasStructuredFacts` is
true for every donor who has any narrative text). The code path exists
and has zero completion-awareness, but it is dormant today, not actively
misfiring. This is a forward-looking gap (a future donor could reach it
before migrating to structured facts), not a second live incident.

### What was changed

- **`lib/relationships/fact-classification.ts`**: new
  `isUnambiguousCompletedOutreachAction(factText, category)`. Returns
  true only for `COMPLETED_WELL_WISH_PATTERN`/`COMPLETED_OUTREACH_ACTION_
  PATTERN` matches (the ACTION-report shapes), and only when `category`
  is NOT a singular-state category (`solicitation`/`health`) -- the same
  guard already used for round 1's decay-window override, carried
  forward so a solicitation note that happens to open with "Called" is
  never unconditionally suppressed; the ask's own subject matter may
  still need follow-through even though the touch itself is done.
- **`lib/relationships/fact-synthesis.ts`**: `scoreFact()` now checks
  `isUnambiguousCompletedOutreachAction(fact.factText, fact.category)`
  FIRST, before even the `durable` early-return, returning `0`
  immediately, at any age. Checked against the fact's own TEXT, never
  its stored `lifecycle` -- this is what makes the fix **self-healing for
  the two already-written Production rows with zero data migration
  required**: whatever `lifecycle` value is currently stored for
  Zachter's and the gym-tour donor's rows, the next time either is read
  through `scoreFact()`, the text itself is reclassified correctly.
  `COMPLETED_MILESTONE_EVENT_PATTERN`'s existing age-based/confirmed-
  completion treatment (October 12 fix) is completely unchanged.
- **`lib/relationships/recommendation-candidates.ts`**:
  `relationshipOpportunityCandidate`'s legacy branch now splits
  `relationship_summary`/`institutional_memory` into sentences (reusing
  `lib/capture/interaction.ts`'s own existing `sentenceList`, now
  exported, never a second splitter) and suppresses the candidate only
  when EVERY sentence is an unambiguous completed-action report (via
  `classifyFactCategory()` per sentence, feeding the same guarded check
  above -- never a second classification scheme). A narrative that mixes
  an action report with other content is left completely untouched, so
  no real donor context is ever silently dropped -- this is the direct
  answer to the owner's explicit "preserve useful donor context"
  instruction for a population without the structured-facts migration's
  per-sentence granularity.

### Alternative considered, not implemented this round

A stored `fact_kind: 'action_report' | 'event_report' | 'standing_fact'`
column, decided once at accept time, would let every later read skip
re-running a text classifier at all. **Not implemented**, because it would
either (a) need a new UI prompt at capture time asking the fundraiser to
classify their own note (added friction, and the owner did not ask for a
UI change), or (b) run this exact same pattern-based classifier at accept
time instead of at read time -- moving today's judgment call earlier in
the pipeline, not eliminating it, while adding a migration (backfilling
the column for all 12 existing rows) and a permanent schema commitment.
Flagging as an option for a future round if the owner wants it, not
proceeding speculatively, per the explicit instruction to explain
tradeoffs before building a larger architectural change.

### Verified against real data vs. inferred from code (this round)

- **Verified, read-only, against Production**: re-confirmed the same 2
  affected structured-fact rows and their exact stored values; confirmed
  all 12 donors with any legacy narrative text already have a structured
  fact row (so the legacy path has zero current exposure); ran the new
  `isUnambiguousCompletedOutreachAction` directly (via a throwaway,
  read-only script, deleted after use) against all 12 real current fact
  rows and confirmed it flags exactly the 2 Zachter/gym-tour rows plus
  the 3 already-`time_bound` "wish happy birthday" rows (correctly
  dropping their remaining grace window too, per the owner's explicit
  instruction), and leaves the 3 bare "<relation> had a bar mitzvah"
  rows and all 4 solicitation rows completely untouched.
- **Inferred from code**: the legacy-path sentence-splitting behavior for
  a hypothetical future donor (no such donor exists in Production today
  to verify against live).

### Regression tests

- `tests/relationship-fact-classification.test.mjs`: direct unit coverage
  for `isUnambiguousCompletedOutreachAction`, including the critical
  solicitation/health guard (a sentence opening with "Called" must stay
  unaffected under `solicitation`/`health`, and must still be flagged
  under any other category) and the EVENT-vs-ACTION-report contrast
  (`"Son had a bar mitzvah."` must NOT be flagged; the real Zachter/
  gym-tour text must be).
- `tests/relationship-fact-completed-outreach-action.test.mjs`: rewritten
  for round 2 -- no-grace-window (suppressed even at day 0), the
  self-healing property (stored `lifecycle` left at the real, uncorrected
  `durable` value and still correctly suppressed), a genuinely
  forward-looking fact remaining actionable (the real contrast case), a
  second genuinely-new fact for the same donor still surfacing, dashboard/
  Daily Agenda consistency, the solicitation decay-window guard, and three
  new legacy-pathway scenarios: an all-action-report narrative suppressed,
  a mixed narrative preserved verbatim, and a pure standing-fact narrative
  completely unaffected.
- `tests/relationship-fact-recommendation-actionability.test.mjs`: the
  round-1 "a 10-day-old well-wish must still be actionable" assertion
  was itself round 1's now-acknowledged mistake -- replaced with "must
  NOT be actionable, at any age," plus a new case proving suppression
  works even when the stored `lifecycle` is still `durable`.
- `tests/relationship-fact-completion-awareness.test.mjs` (October 12
  fix, EVENT-report case): unchanged and still green, confirming this
  round did not touch that pattern's own, separately-justified, age-based
  behavior.

**Results: 190/190 test files passing, `tsc --noEmit` clean, lint
baseline unchanged (94 errors/43 warnings, via the real `pnpm run lint`).**

### Staging deployment and verification

Deployed via the protected `pnpm run deploy:staging-independent` script.
New Staging Worker version: `f2721843-769b-4a2d-9f4a-f15de04ea6de`.
Confirmed Staging responds normally post-deploy. As with round 1,
Staging's own D1 does not contain the real Zachter/gym-tour donors, so
live-data verification for this round was done read-only against
Production directly, and the fix itself was proven against that real
data through the throwaway script described above plus the full,
real-pipeline test suite.

### Completed outreach can still be incorrectly recommended? / Is the
legacy pathway addressed?

For the two patterns this investigation has evidence for
(`COMPLETED_WELL_WISH_PATTERN`, `COMPLETED_OUTREACH_ACTION_PATTERN`):
**no grace window remains** -- suppression is immediate, at any age, and
self-healing regardless of stored `lifecycle`. The legacy pathway now
applies the identical check and is the direct, system-wide answer to the
owner's "propose a system-wide solution rather than special-case
exclusions" instruction (same function, same patterns, one additional
caller). The disclosed, still-open gap is narrower than before: a
completed-action sentence worded in a way that matches NEITHER existing
pattern (no explicit past-tense contact verb at all) would still not be
caught -- this remains a text-pattern system, by the owner's own
instruction not to invent a new completion status, and a pattern-based
system can only recognize shapes it has evidence for.

### Production data correction plan -- NOT executed, awaiting explicit authorization

Important context for this decision: because round 2's fix checks the
fact's own TEXT before ever consulting the stored `lifecycle` column,
**this correction is no longer behaviorally required** for the Daily
Agenda/Today page to stop recommending Zachter's and the gym-tour
donor's completed touches -- that already happens the moment the code
itself is deployed to Production, regardless of this metadata value.
This plan exists purely to keep the stored `lifecycle` column accurate
(it currently reads the stale `durable` value for both rows), which the
owner separately asked to have prepared.

**Preconditions** (all must hold before running):
1. The round-2 code fix has been deployed to Production (this plan
   corrects metadata to match the code's own classifier; running it
   against Production while Production is still running the OLD code
   would leave the data correct but the behavior unprotected by the
   self-healing mechanism in the interim -- low risk either way, but the
   intended order is code first).
2. Owner's explicit, separate authorization for this specific action.
3. Immediately before running: a fresh read-only re-check of both rows'
   current `lifecycle`/`category`/`fact_text` (matching `scripts/
   relationship-facts-lifecycle-reclassify.mjs`'s own existing
   "re-fetch and re-plan, never trust an earlier read" convention), in
   case either row was independently touched since this plan was written.

**Target rows and exact statements** (D1 database `fundraising-os-
production-db`; `?NOW?` is the Unix epoch seconds at execution time):

```sql
-- Row 1: Yaakov Zachter
UPDATE donor_relationship_facts
SET lifecycle = 'time_bound', updated_at = ?NOW?
WHERE id = '1550c6b7-ba7d-4bce-a819-a9cbfb320ee7' AND lifecycle = 'durable';

-- Row 2: the gym-tour donor
UPDATE donor_relationship_facts
SET lifecycle = 'time_bound', updated_at = ?NOW?
WHERE id = '208a5d68-705d-43b2-9037-578995819445' AND lifecycle = 'durable';
```

Each statement's reported `changes` count MUST equal exactly 1. A count
of 0 means the row's `lifecycle` has already changed since the
precondition re-check (a concurrent writer) -- stop, do not force, and
re-investigate rather than retrying blind. No other column is touched by
either statement: `fact_text`, `category`, `status`, `donor_id`,
`source_interaction_id`, `source_interaction_occurred_at` are untouched
for both rows, matching the existing reclassify script's own scoping
discipline.

**Expected before/after:**

| id | donor | before | after |
|---|---|---|---|
| `1550c6b7-ba7d-4bce-a819-a9cbfb320ee7` | Yaakov Zachter | `lifecycle: durable` | `lifecycle: time_bound` |
| `208a5d68-705d-43b2-9037-578995819445` | (gym-tour donor) | `lifecycle: durable` | `lifecycle: time_bound` |

**Rollback procedure** (trivial -- a single-column, non-cascading
metadata field with no derived/cached state stored elsewhere that reads
it):

```sql
UPDATE donor_relationship_facts
SET lifecycle = 'durable', updated_at = ?NOW?
WHERE id = '1550c6b7-ba7d-4bce-a819-a9cbfb320ee7' AND lifecycle = 'time_bound';

UPDATE donor_relationship_facts
SET lifecycle = 'durable', updated_at = ?NOW?
WHERE id = '208a5d68-705d-43b2-9037-578995819445' AND lifecycle = 'time_bound';
```

**Verification queries** (read-only, run both before and after, and
compare):

```sql
SELECT id, donor_id, category, lifecycle, status, fact_text,
       source_interaction_id, source_interaction_occurred_at, updated_at
FROM donor_relationship_facts
WHERE id IN ('1550c6b7-ba7d-4bce-a819-a9cbfb320ee7', '208a5d68-705d-43b2-9037-578995819445');
```

Confirm: both rows present, `status` still `current` for both, every
column except `lifecycle`/`updated_at` byte-identical to the
precondition read, and `lifecycle` is now `time_bound` for both. Also
re-run the full donor-record safety checks already established earlier
in this session (donor/giving-activity counts unchanged) as a final
sanity pass, though neither statement above touches those tables.

### Whether this is ready for Production

**The code fix is ready and recommended for Production deployment**,
pending the owner's explicit authorization (not yet given this round,
per standing instruction -- no Production deploy was performed). It is
deployed and verified on Staging, 190/190 tests pass, `tsc` is clean,
lint is at its unchanged baseline, and it has been checked against all
12 real current Production fact rows with the exact expected,
narrowly-scoped effect. The data correction above is optional (the fix
is self-healing without it) and should be run, if at all, only after the
code is live and only with separate, explicit authorization.

## Geographic Audit for Travel Planning -- Phase 1 (2026-10-14, read-only)

Requested: help the owner organize fundraising travel by city/region,
eventually letting him filter donors by travel region on the existing
priority-ranked lists. This round is audit-only -- no feature was built,
no Production or Staging write of any kind was made, and no city
grouping was applied. Proposed groupings below are **not yet approved**.

### How addresses are stored today

`donors` has both a legacy single-line `address` column and a
structured set (`address_line_1`, `city`, `state`, `postal_code`,
`country`) -- the structured set is what every current consumer (the
donor directory, donor profile, imports) actually reads. `city`/`state`
are stored exactly as imported, verbatim, with **no normalization of any
kind** -- `lib/import/jl-solutions.ts`/`lib/import/recognition.ts` map a
source spreadsheet's own "City"/"State" columns straight through. There
is no existing geography/region concept anywhere in the schema or code:
`city`/`state` are read today only for on-screen display (`app/donors/
page.tsx`'s directory query, the donor profile page) and are **never**
part of search or filtering -- `lib/relationships/donor-search.ts`'s
`matchesDonorQuery()` matches only last name, name, spouse, code, email,
and phone; city/state are not in that list at all.

### Audit scope

Read-only queries against `fundraising-os-production-db`, scoped to
`data_source = 'live' AND archived_at IS NULL` -- the exact same
population `app/donors/page.tsx` itself queries (**254 donors**). No
donor name, email, phone, or street address was included in any query
result used for this report -- only `city`, `state`, `country`,
aggregate counts, and (for the handful of incomplete rows) `postal_code`
presence/absence.

### Data quality: cleaner than typical

- **0 of 254** donors are missing `city` or `address_line_1`.
- **3 of 254** have no `state` -- all three are Israel addresses
  (Betar Illit, Jerusalem, Ramat Beit Shemesh), where a US-style state
  genuinely does not apply; this is not a data-entry defect.
- **4 of 254** have no `postal_code` -- the same 3 Israel donors plus
  the 1 Toronto, Ontario donor; again consistent with non-US addresses
  rather than missing data.
- **Zero** case/whitespace spelling duplicates (e.g. `"teaneck"` vs.
  `"Teaneck"`) were found -- verified by grouping on
  `LOWER(TRIM(city))`/`LOWER(TRIM(state))` and comparing against the
  exact-match grouping; every normalized group contains exactly one raw
  spelling.
- **Zero** cities recorded under more than one state value (checked
  directly) -- no "same city name, conflicting state" data errors.
- **49 distinct city/state combinations** across the 254 donors; country
  breakdown is 250 United States, 3 Israel, 1 Canada.

This is a genuinely clean, single-source-of-truth address dataset -- the
grouping work below is about geography (which nearby cities travel
together), not data cleanup.

| La Jolla | CA | 3 | none |
| Los Angeles | CA | 8 | none |

### Recommended design: flexible groups without touching donor records

**Never modify `city`/`state`/`address_line_1` on any donor row.** The
grouping itself should be a separate mapping, read-only with respect to
`donors`, so regions can be renamed, merged, split, or re-scoped at any
time with zero data migration and zero risk to the underlying address
record (which is also the source of truth for the JL re-import
reconciliation and mailing-label systems elsewhere in this app).

Two options, by increasing flexibility:

- **Option A -- a small, pure, code-defined matcher** (recommended
  starting point): a `TRAVEL_REGIONS` list, each entry `{ id, label,
  matches: (city, state) => boolean }`, evaluated at read time against a
  donor's existing `city`/`state` -- the exact same "deterministic, pure,
  unit-testable function" pattern this codebase already uses throughout
  (e.g. `classifyFactCategory` in `lib/relationships/fact-classification.
  ts`). A donor can match zero, one, or several regions simply because
  `matches()` is evaluated independently per region -- this is what
  naturally supports a donor belonging to more than one useful region
  (e.g. a Passaic donor matching both a tight "Passaic" grouping and a
  broader "North Jersey" grouping, if the owner wants both to exist at
  once). Zero schema change, trivially reversible, and matches "no
  automatic city grouping changes" exactly -- the mapping lives in code,
  reviewed and approved like any other change, never silently applied to
  data.
- **Option B -- an editable database table** (a natural later upgrade,
  not recommended for the first cut): a `donor_travel_regions` or
  `travel_region_rules` table mapping `(city, state) -> region_id`,
  editable from a settings screen without a code deploy. More flexible
  long-term (the owner could rename/merge/split regions himself), but is
  a real schema migration plus a new CRUD UI -- worth building only once
  the region definitions above are approved and have proven stable
  through actual use.

Recommend starting with Option A once the groupings above are approved,
with an explicit path to Option B later if the owner finds himself
wanting to edit region boundaries through the UI rather than asking for
a code change each time.

### Recommended integration with existing filtering and priorities

The donor directory (`app/donors/page.tsx` /
`DonorDirectoryExperience.tsx`) already fetches `city`/`state` for every
donor and already has one working precedent for a single-select filter
layered on top of search: the A-Z last-name letter filter in `lib/
relationships/donor-search.ts`'s `filterDonorDirectory()` (letter narrows
the list, then free-text search narrows further within that). A region
filter is the same shape -- one more narrowing dimension, not a new
search engine.

A closer architectural match for the EVENTUAL "pick a region, see
matching donors, use existing priority to decide who to visit" UI is
Portfolio Focus (`app/portfolio-focus/PortfolioFocusExperience.tsx`,
`lib/portfolio-focus/dedicated-view.ts`'s `PORTFOLIO_FOCUS_FILTERS`):
a server-rendered array, already ranked by score, with client-side
filter buttons (`{ id, label, matches() }`, "All" plus one button per
category, each showing a live count) that only ever **narrow** that same
ranked array -- filtering never re-sorts or renumbers. A Travel Region
filter would reuse this identical mechanic: compute each donor's
matching region id(s) once (Option A's pure function), add one filter
button per region (plus "All"), and let the existing priority
score/ranking already used by the Today page and Portfolio Focus decide
the order within whichever region is selected. No new scoring model is
needed -- this is purely a new filter dimension over an already-solved
ranking problem.

Simplest path for Phase 2, in order of effort: (1) add a region filter
to the existing donor directory first (lowest effort, reuses the
existing letter-filter pattern and the city/state data already fetched
there); (2) if the owner wants priority-ordered results specifically for
trip planning, add the same region filter to a ranked list (Portfolio
Focus or a new dedicated view), reusing its exact filter-button
mechanics rather than inventing a new one.

### Safeguards honored this round

No Production or Staging write of any kind; no address correction; no
city grouping applied to any donor record; no Staging or Production
deployment; every query result used in this report contains only
city/state/country and aggregate counts, never donor name, email, phone,
or street address. **Phase 2 (building the filter) has not begun and
will not begin without the owner's explicit approval of the groupings
above.**

## Geographic Filtering for Travel Planning -- Phase 2 (2026-10-14)

The owner approved all 15 proposed regions from the Phase 1 audit above,

### Implementation

- **`lib/relationships/travel-regions.ts`** (new) -- the 15 approved
  regions and their exact city/state membership, copied verbatim from
  the Phase 1 audit table (no city added, removed, or re-scoped).
  `regionsForCityState(city, state)` returns EVERY region whose
  membership list matches (an array, never a single id), which is what
  structurally supports a city belonging to more than one region later
  without any further code change -- no two of the 15 approved regions
  currently share a city, but nothing in this function assumes that
  stays true. Matching is case/whitespace-tolerant (`cityStateKey()`
  trims and lowercases before comparing); the real Production data has
  no case/whitespace variation today (per the Phase 1 audit), so this is
  a forward-looking robustness property, not a fix for an observed
  defect. Never reads or writes `donors` directly -- it is a pure
  function over whatever `city`/`state` text a caller hands it.
- **`lib/relationships/donor-geo-filter.ts`** (new) -- `filterByGeo()`
  and `cityOptionsForRegion()`, deliberately written against the
  minimal `{ city, state }` shape rather than the donor directory's own
  row type, so this exact logic can be reused from Portfolio Focus or a
  future dedicated Travel Planning view (per the owner's own "prepare
  for future travel planning" instruction) with zero changes.
  `cityOptionsForRegion()` is what makes "the City filter should offer
  only cities within that region" true: it derives the city list live
  from whichever donors are actually passed in, scoped to the selected
  region, rather than from a static list -- it will stay correct as
  donors are added, archived, or edited.
- **`app/donors`** -- `DonorDirectoryExperience.tsx` adds two `<select>`
  filters (Travel Region, City) alongside the existing free-text search.
  Region and city compose with search by plain array filtering
  (`filterByGeo(searched, regionId, cityKey)`, applied AFTER the
  existing search-based narrowing) -- never a second search engine.
  Choosing a region that no longer contains the currently-selected city
  resets City back to "All Cities" automatically, rather than silently
  showing zero results. The donor count line now reflects search,
  region, AND city together (previously it only reflected search).
  `lib/navigation/donor-navigation.ts` gained `donorDirectoryFilterPath()`
  (the same convention as the existing `donorDirectorySearchPath()`) so
  region/city round-trip through the existing return-path URL params
  automatically -- `donorDirectoryReturnPath()` already preserves every
  query param generically, so no change was needed there.
- **Donors outside every approved region, and international donors,
  remain fully visible**: "All Regions" applies no region constraint at
  all, and any city -- grouped or not -- is always offered in the City
  dropdown when "All Regions" is selected.
- **Mobile-friendly by construction, not a separate mobile UI**: both
  filters are native `<select>` elements (no custom dropdown widget),
  styled with `flex-wrap` so they stack to full width on narrow screens
  using the exact same pattern `.directory-actions` already uses
  elsewhere on this page, and a 44px minimum touch target height
  matching this codebase's own existing convention (see `app/globals.css`).
- **No donor address, pledge, payment, interaction, or recommendation
  logic was touched.** `app/donors/page.tsx`'s own SQL remains the
  exact same single, unmodified `SELECT` it was before this round --
  the only change there is reading two more optional URL parameters.
  No new scoring model was introduced; existing donor priorities,
  recommendations, and the Daily Fundraising Agenda are completely
  unaffected (no file under `lib/relationships/recommendation-*`,
  `lib/agenda/`, or any giving/pledge/payment-plan module was touched --
  confirmed directly from `git diff --stat`, not merely asserted).

## Geographic Filtering -- UI Usability Fixes (2026-10-14)

Owner feedback from using the Production deployment: (1) the City
dropdown was sorted state-first, which made a long, flat list of ~49
cities hard to scan; (2) there was no way to search it, only scroll.

### What changed

- **`lib/relationships/donor-geo-filter.ts`**: `cityOptionsForRegion()`'s
  sort is now city name first (A-Z), with state used only as a
  tiebreaker when two cities share the exact same name -- no real pair
  like that exists in current Production data, but the sort handles it
  correctly regardless (proven with a synthetic three-state "Springfield"
  fixture in the test suite). New `searchCityOptions(options, query)`:
  a pure, case-insensitive partial match against an already-built
  option list (city name or state), directly unit-testable with no
  React or DOM involved -- the same "empty query shows everything"
  convention `lib/relationships/donor-search.ts`'s `searchDonors()`
  already uses, not a differently-shaped rule.
- **`app/donors/CityComboBox.tsx`** (new): replaces the City `<select>`
  with an accessible combobox. Typing narrows the option list live
  (case-insensitive, partial match); "All Cities" is always the first,
  always-reachable row regardless of what's typed; a separate explicit
  clear (×) button is also provided once a specific city is selected.
  Full keyboard support: ArrowUp/ArrowDown moves the highlighted option,
  Enter commits it, Escape reverts to the last committed selection
  without changing it. Modeled directly on the existing `DonorAutocomplete`
  pattern (ARIA `combobox`/`listbox`/`option` roles, the same
  mousedown-`preventDefault()` guard that keeps a tap from being
  cancelled by blur before the click handler runs) -- not a copy of it,
  since donors and cities are different data shapes with no shared
  rendering needs, and NOT a second donor-search engine: the component
  imports nothing but React and this app's own `donor-geo-filter`
  module, confirmed directly by a test that inspects every import line
  in the file.
- **Mobile**: a plain text `<input>` (the OS's own keyboard, no custom
  widget to fight), 44px minimum touch targets (matching this
  codebase's own established convention), and a `flex-wrap` filter row
  that already stacks to full width on narrow screens -- no separate
  mobile layout needed, same approach as the Phase 2 filters themselves.
- **Everything else is unchanged by design**: `handleCityChange`, the
  region-change city-reset logic, `donorDirectoryFilterPath()`'s URL
  round-tripping, and the Travel Region `<select>` were not touched --
  confirmed directly from the diff, not merely asserted. Region scoping
  (the City combobox's own options are still exactly
  `cityOptionsForRegion(relationships, regionId)`, so selecting a
  region still narrows which cities are offered), composition with the
  existing donor search, and dynamic matching for a newly created or
  imported donor are therefore automatically preserved -- none of that
  logic lives in the combobox itself.

### Regression tests added

- **`tests/donor-geo-filter.test.mjs`** (extended): the new city-first
  sort order, proven against the real roster (Baltimore, Bergenfield,
  Chicago, Jerusalem, Savannah, Silver Spring, Teaneck -- spanning
  MD/NJ/IL/none/GA/MD/NJ, showing state plays no grouping role); the
  state-tiebreaker case via a synthetic same-named-city fixture;
  `searchCityOptions()` covering partial/case-insensitive matching,
  empty and whitespace queries returning everything, a query matching
  nothing returning an empty list, multiple matches staying in sorted
  order, and state-abbreviation matching.
- **`tests/city-combobox.test.mjs`** (new): since this codebase has no
  React component-rendering test harness anywhere (and this round was
  explicitly told not to add one), these verify the component's actual
  source the same way `tests/donor-navigation.test.mjs` already verifies
  other component wiring -- ARIA combobox/listbox/option attributes;
  all four keyboard keys (ArrowDown/ArrowUp/Enter/Escape) handled, with
  Escape reverting rather than clearing; the mousedown-preventDefault
  guard present on both the clear button and every option; "All
  Cities" and the clear action both present; confirmation that only
  React and the local geo-filter module are imported (no new
  dependency, no reference to `searchDonors`); and that
  `DonorDirectoryExperience.tsx` wires `<CityComboBox>` in with the
  exact same `options`/`value`/`onChange` props the old `<select>` used,
  while the Travel Region `<select>` is confirmed unchanged.

**Results: 193/193 test files passing (192 before this round, +1 new
file), `tsc --noEmit` clean, lint baseline unchanged (94 errors/43
warnings).**
