## Upgrade Ask Fundraising OS to a Real AI Assistant (2026-10-16) -- IMPLEMENTED, TESTED ON STAGING, PRODUCTION NOT TOUCHED

Replaces the keyword-classified, fixed-template Assistant
(`lib/ai/rule-based.ts`) with a genuinely natural-language, context-aware
fundraising assistant powered by Cloudflare Workers AI -- grounded
exclusively in real, authenticated, owner-scoped CRM data, with a fixed
read-only capability registry instead of AI-generated SQL.

### 1. Architecture

**`lib/assistant/capabilities.ts`** -- the assistant's entire data-access
surface. A fixed set of 8 named, read-only functions, each either
reusing an existing loader or mirroring an already-reviewed query
pattern:

- `todays_priorities` / `this_week_priorities` -- `loadWorkspaceBrief`'s
  own `relationshipQueue` buckets, the exact same data the home page's
  Today's Agenda already shows.
- `lapsed_relationships` -- the same contact-gap filter the prior
  rule-based Assistant used, now applied over real priorities.
- `outstanding_pledges` -- a bounded query mirroring
  `app/pledge-review/page.tsx`'s own `pledge_balance_corrections` JOIN
  verbatim, so a manually-corrected balance is never shown stale.
- `payment_plans_attention` -- filters `loadWorkspaceBrief`'s
  `"Open commitment"` priorities, which are only ever populated via
  `isOpenPledgeActionable`/`evaluateOpenPledgePlanStatus`
  (`lib/relationships/pledge-payment-plan.ts`). **This is the explicit
  safeguard the task required preserved**: a donor with a valid,
  on-track upcoming payment is already excluded by that function,
  regardless of how old the original pledge date is -- this feature
  never re-decides staleness itself (locked in by a structural test
  asserting `capabilities.ts` never even imports `pledge-payment-
  plan.ts` directly).
- `donor_summary` -- one donor via `loadMeetingBrief`, the same loader
  the donor page's "Prepare for Meeting" button uses. Covers
  summarizing a relationship, meeting prep, recent history, and
  gathering what's needed to draft a follow-up.
- `fundraising_progress` -- real totals only (gifts received, new
  pledges, donors contacted this month). There is no "goal"/target
  concept anywhere in this schema, confirmed by the prior system-wide
  audit, so this capability never fabricates a percent-of-goal figure.
- `search_donors` -- a bounded, owner-scoped name search, used both
  directly and by donor-reference resolution below.

**`lib/assistant/conversation-state.ts` / `conversation.ts`** -- bounded,
client-held conversation context (last 6 turns, 4,000-character budget,
hard per-message and per-list caps) and donor-reference resolution. An
ordinal reference ("the second one") indexes into the conversation's
own donor list, but the id it names is **re-verified against the
current request's authenticated userId on every single use** --
conversation state is round-tripped through the client, so it is never
trusted as proof of ownership, only as "what was discussed." A name
reference resolves through the same bounded `search_donors` capability
a fundraiser's own query would use; multiple matches are reported back
as candidates for the fundraiser to pick from, never guessed between.

**`lib/assistant/protocol.ts`** -- the pure plan/compose prompt
construction and strict response parsing. No AI call, no database --
the one module in this feature directly unit-testable with plain mock
strings.

**`lib/assistant/orchestrator.ts`** -- exactly **two** AI calls per
user turn, never more (no agentic loop, no unbounded tool-call chain):

1. **PLAN** -- given the question and conversation context, the model
   selects up to 3 capability names from the fixed registry and a
   donor reference, as structured JSON
   (`response_format: json_schema`, the same native structured-output
   mode already proven for Meeting Notes). The model never writes a
   query and never produces a donor id itself.
2. **COMPOSE** -- the selected capabilities are executed for real
   (plain function calls), and their actual output is handed back to
   the model as a clearly delimited `<<<VERIFIED_CRM_DATA_START>>>...
   <<<VERIFIED_CRM_DATA_END>>>` block, with an explicit instruction to
   use ONLY that data, never invent a name/amount/date not present in
   it, never independently decide a pledge is stale, and to say so
   plainly when the data is insufficient. The conversation history is
   wrapped in the same "data not instructions" framing already proven
   for Meeting Notes' dictated transcripts (the established
   prompt-injection mitigation for free text originating from a
   donor-adjacent source).

If donor-reference resolution comes back ambiguous or not-found, this
module answers directly from that resolution -- never a third AI call,
never a guess at which donor was meant.

**`lib/ai/workers-ai-client.ts`** -- the Workers AI binding call,
dual response-shape handling, and timeout race extracted from Meeting
Notes' own provider (`lib/meeting-notes/providers/workers-ai.ts`, now
refactored to use this shared client with its public API and tests
unchanged) into one shared, independently tested module -- exactly the
"shared provider client once a second real AI feature exists"
extraction the Meeting Notes round's own comments anticipated.

### 2. Safety by construction

- **Read-only, no exceptions**: no capability, the orchestrator, or
  the route contains an `INSERT`/`UPDATE`/`DELETE` or a D1 write call
  -- locked in by `tests/assistant-capabilities-safety.test.mjs`'s
  structural guardrails (the same "no-write/no-R2-binding guardrail"
  convention `tests/backup-automation.test.mjs` already uses for a
  different feature), confirmed live by re-querying every affected
  table's row count before and after an extensive Staging test
  session (see Section 5) and finding it byte-identical.
- **No dynamic dispatch**: capability execution is a fixed if/else
  chain over known names (`tests/assistant-capabilities-safety.test.mjs`
  asserts no bracket-indexed dynamic call exists) -- an unrecognized or
  injected "capability name" from the model is silently dropped, never
  reaches a function call.
- **Authentication and ownership never bypassed**: the route's own
  `getChatGPTUser()`/`ensureUserProfile()` gate is unchanged from
  every other route; every donor-scoped query in `capabilities.ts`
  filters by `owner_user_id`/`user_id` (structurally asserted); a
  conversational donor reference is re-verified for ownership on every
  use, never trusted from client-held state.
- **Confidential content never logged**: the route logs only that a
  turn happened, whether it succeeded, and which capabilities were
  used -- never the question text or the AI's answer (structurally
  asserted).
- **Prompt injection**: retrieved data and conversation history are
  always wrapped in the established delimiter/"data not instructions"
  framing before reaching a prompt -- never concatenated in bare.
- **Financial accuracy**: every dollar figure the assistant can ever
  state comes from an already-correct, already-reconciled source
  (`pledge_balance_corrections`-aware queries, the recommendation
  engine's own safeguarded output) -- the AI only explains verified
  numbers, never computes one.

### 3. Supported capabilities and limitations

Handles natural variation on all of the task's example questions:
who to call today, lapsed relationships, this week's priorities,
relationship summaries, outstanding pledges, payment plans needing
attention, recent donor history, meeting preparation, this month's
fundraising progress, and drafting a follow-up message grounded in
real recent-interaction text. Multi-turn follow-ups ("tell me more
about the second one," "prepare talking points for that call") work
by resolving against the conversation's own donor list, re-verified
for ownership each time.

**Known limitations, disclosed rather than papered over**:

- **No dedicated trip-prioritization capability.** Asked "which donors
  should I prioritize before my trip," the planner falls back to the
  closest relevant real capability (this week's priorities) rather
  than a trip-specific one -- confirmed live this produces an honest,
  grounded answer from real (if more general) data, never a fabricated
  trip-specific detail, but it is not the dedicated capability the
  task's example list suggested. Noted as a gap for a future round,
  not built this round given the scope already covered.
- **No persistent, cross-request rate limiting.** Per-turn limits are
  solid (at most 2 AI calls, 3 capabilities, bounded result sizes,
  bounded conversation context, bounded question/answer length -- all
  enforced server-side regardless of what the model returns), but
  there is no database-backed daily/per-user request counter the way
  a production system might eventually want. Not needed at this
  org's realistic volume (see cost estimate below), and adding one
  would mean a new table/migration, which this round's scope did not
  call for -- noted as a future addition if usage ever grows enough to
  matter.
- **Live prompt-injection testing was necessarily structural/unit-level
  only** -- this is a read-only feature with no way to plant an
  adversarial donor note to test against without a write this round
  wasn't authorized to make. The mitigation itself (delimiters +
  explicit "data not instructions" framing) is the same one already
  proven in production use for Meeting Notes' dictated transcripts,
  not a new, unproven mechanism.
- **Transient Workers AI failures were observed live** (see Section 5)
  -- an occasional empty/slow model response that the shared client
  correctly caught and reported as "could not be reached" rather than
  crashing, hanging, or showing a broken UI. Retrying the identical
  request succeeded. This is an inherent Workers AI characteristic
  (also seen occasionally during the original Meeting Notes
  evaluation), not a defect in this feature's own code.

### 4. Cloudflare AI model and estimated cost

Same model and binding already live-tested and deployed for Meeting
Notes: Workers AI, `@cf/mistralai/mistral-small-3.1-24b-instruct`, via
the existing `env.AI` binding -- no new credential, no new paid
service, no new Cloudflare resource. Each assistant turn costs two
model calls (plan: ~300 max output tokens; compose: ~900 max output
tokens) instead of Meeting Notes' one, so per-turn Neuron usage is
roughly double a meeting note's (Meeting Notes measured at ~50-150
Neurons/note) -- an estimated 100-300 Neurons per assistant turn. The
free daily allowance (10,000 Neurons/day) comfortably covers hundreds
of fundraiser turns a day, far beyond this organization's realistic
volume; cost is $0.00/month under any normal usage pattern, same
conclusion as the original Workers AI evaluation.

### 7. Production readiness assessment

**Notably, zero new Cloudflare configuration would be required.**
Production already has the `ai` binding, `AI_PROVIDER=workers-ai`, and
`WORKERS_AI_MODEL` configured (from the earlier "Authorized Production
Deployment -- AI Meeting Notes" round this session) -- this feature
reuses that exact same binding and model, so a Production deployment
of Ask Fundraising OS would be a pure code deploy, not a configuration
change. No new secret, no new paid service, no new database table or
migration (this feature reads existing tables only).

**What's ready**: the architecture, safety guardrails, and grounding
behavior are all proven live on Staging (Section 6), on the same
Workers AI model and binding Production already runs. The feature is
read-only, so a Production deployment carries materially lower risk
than a write-capable feature would -- there is no financial-data or
donor-record change path to verify post-deploy, only that the
assistant answers correctly, which Staging has now demonstrated across
a representative range of real questions, a multi-turn conversation,
an ambiguous-donor case, and a genuine live AI failure handled
gracefully.

**What a Production round should still do before deploying**: the
same mandatory safety checks as every prior Production round
(current Worker version recorded as rollback target, backup/restore
status, financial/record baseline before and after, D1 isolation,
Staging write protection, Access/Gmail/cron unchanged, build
freshness) -- none of which are new to this feature, all of which the
established procedure already covers. A brief live smoke test against
Production itself (the same read-only pattern used for Meeting Notes'
own Production smoke test -- an existing real donor id, a fictional
question, confirmed zero writes) would close the loop the same way it
did for that feature.

**Remaining risk, disclosed for the owner's own judgment**: this is
the first AI feature in this codebase that can surface a donor's
*private* notes, interaction summaries, and unconfirmed historical
context in free-form AI-composed prose, rather than fixed-template
text. The grounding rules (Section 2-3) are designed to prevent
fabrication, and the delimiter-based injection defense is the same
one already proven for Meeting Notes -- but this is a genuinely new
exposure shape (AI paraphrasing real private donor content) worth the
owner's own explicit sign-off, separate from the purely mechanical
"did the deploy succeed" checks.

**No Production file was read or written this round. No Production
deployment, configuration change, or data change occurred. Staging
write protection is confirmed restored. No parallel or forked agent
was used for any part of this round. Stopping here per this round's
instruction to stop after implementation, Staging testing, and
documentation -- not deploying to Production without separate
authorization.**

## Independent Code Review -- Pre-Production Corrections for Ask Fundraising OS (2026-10-16)

An independent code review of the "Upgrade Ask Fundraising OS to a Real
AI Assistant" round (above) raised three concerns before that feature
could be considered for Production. All three were investigated and
fixed this round. Code/tests committed as `9789649`; this entry as the
follow-up docs commit. No Production file was read or written. No
parallel or forked agent was used for any part of this round's
research, implementation, Staging deployment, database access, or
verification -- same discipline as every prior round.

### 1. Donor profile URL security -- FIXED

**What was wrong**: `lib/assistant/conversation-state.ts`'s
`boundConversationState` accepted `lastDonorRefs[].href` from the
client with no validation at all, and `lib/assistant/conversation.ts`'s
ordinal-reference resolution (`resolveDonorReference`, the "tell me
more about the second one" path) returned that client-supplied
`candidate.href` verbatim on a resolved donor, after verifying only the
donor id's ownership -- never rebuilding the link itself from the
verified id. Every OTHER donor link in the feature (`capabilities.ts`'s
`donorHref()`, used by every direct capability) was already
server-generated and safe; this one path was not.

**Investigated impact**: traced the full data flow from
`AssistantExperience.tsx`'s client-held `lastDonorRefs` state, through
the request body, `boundConversationState`, `resolveDonorReference`,
`runCapabilities`, to the final `AssistantAnswer.referencedDonors`/
`donorRefs`. In the current orchestrator (`orchestrator.ts`), the
donor object `resolveDonorReference` returns is only ever consumed for
its `donorId` (to call `getDonorSummary`, which always regenerates its
own `href`) -- so the specific forged-href value could not yet reach a
real response. This was a latent defect, not an exploited one: the
`DonorRef` type conflates "a safe, server-verified donor reference" with
"an untrusted bag of client-echoed strings," and any future capability
that read `.href` off the resolved donor directly (rather than off a
fresh capability call) would have reintroduced the leak silently. Fixed
at the shared-infrastructure level rather than patched at the one
current call site.

**Fix**:
- `donorHref(donorId)` is now the single canonical link builder, moved
  to `conversation-state.ts` (pure, already shared by both
  `capabilities.ts` and `conversation.ts`) and exported. `capabilities.ts`'s
  own duplicate copy is removed.
- `boundConversationState` now **regenerates** every `lastDonorRefs[].href`
  from `donorId` unconditionally -- the client's own `href` string is
  never read into the bounded state at all, regardless of what it
  contains. `href` is no longer even a required field on the client
  payload (only `donorId`/`name` are).
- `resolveDonorReference`'s ordinal branch independently rebuilds the
  href from the ownership-verified `owned.id` row, rather than the
  `candidate` the client sent -- deliberate defense in depth on top of
  the `boundConversationState` fix, so the "never return a donor
  without verifying ownership first" guarantee holds even if that
  upstream regeneration is ever changed.
- `orchestrator.ts`'s `presetDonorId` synthetic-candidate construction
  was switched to the same shared helper (it was already server-side
  and safe, just a duplicated inline template string).

**Regression tests added**:
- `tests/assistant-conversation-state.test.mjs`: a real, owned donorId
  paired with an external phishing URL, a protocol-relative URL, a
  `javascript:` URL, and a path into a different donor's profile --
  all four must come back as the canonical `/donors/<id>` link, never
  the forged string; an already-canonical client href is unaffected
  (proves the fix regenerates unconditionally, not via an allow/block
  list); a row with `href` omitted entirely is still accepted.
- `tests/assistant-capabilities-safety.test.mjs` (structural, since
  `conversation.ts` imports `cloudflare:workers` and cannot be invoked
  directly in Node): asserts `conversation.ts` never assigns
  `candidate.href` to anything returned, always rebuilds from
  `donorHref(owned.id)`, and imports the one shared helper rather than
  defining its own; asserts `capabilities.ts` no longer defines its own
  `donorHref`.

**Live verification on Staging** (synthetic donor only -- see Section 3):
sent a forged `conversation.lastDonorRefs` entry pairing the real,
owned synthetic test donor's id with `href: "https://evil.example.com/phish"`,
then asked an ordinal follow-up ("Tell me about the first one."). The
live response's `referencedDonors`/`donorRefs` both came back with
`href: "/donors/5894d764-c4ea-4b87-a595-7fcc4664ba0e"` -- the forged
URL never appeared anywhere in the response. A second request with a
non-owned/nonexistent donorId (also paired with a forged href) resolved
to "not found," fell through to a different capability, and likewise
never surfaced the forged URL or any unauthorized data.

### 2. Monthly fundraising totals and timezone boundaries -- FIXED

**What was wrong**: `lib/assistant/capabilities.ts`'s
`getFundraisingProgress` (the `fundraising_progress` capability -- "how
is this month going") computed its month-start boundary with
`new Date(ctx.now * 1000); .setUTCDate(1); .setUTCHours(0,0,0,0)` --
truncating straight to whatever month it currently is in **UTC**, not
the fundraiser's own `America/New_York` calendar month. For roughly
4-5 hours of every day (the UTC-ET offset), this boundary silently
disagreed with the fundraiser's real local calendar: a gift entered, or
a donor contacted, late at night local time but already "tomorrow" in
UTC could be attributed to next month's totals a day early, and the
reverse at each month's true start.

**Scope of the search**: grepped the whole codebase for every
month-boundary/monthly-aggregation computation
(`setUTCDate`/`setUTCHours`/`strftime`/"this month"/"monthly" across
`lib/` and `app/`). `getFundraisingProgress` is the **only** place in
this codebase that computes a monthly reporting boundary from "now" --
every other date-sensitive surface (Daily Agenda, reminders, the
Morning Brief, payment-plan due dates) already reasons in terms of
single calendar days via the existing, already-correct
`lib/workspace/local-time.ts` helpers, not months. Individual
transaction dates themselves
(`giving_activities.activity_date`) were never affected -- they are
deliberately stored as timezone-agnostic, UTC-midnight-anchored
calendar days (`lib/financial-date.ts`), by design, specifically so a
date never shifts with timezone. The bug was purely in the *boundary*
compared against that value, not the stored dates.

**Fix**: added `localMonthBoundaries(epochSeconds, timezone)` to
`lib/workspace/local-time.ts` (pure, no `cloudflare:workers` import,
reusing the module's existing `localDateParts`/`zonedTimeToUtc`
helpers rather than inventing new date math). It returns the local
month start in the TWO conventions this schema actually needs:
- `dateOnlyStartEpoch` -- the 1st of the local month expressed as a
  UTC-midnight date-only anchor, for comparison against
  `giving_activities.activity_date` (itself date-only, never
  DST-adjusted, because a calendar day is not an instant).
- `instantStartEpoch` -- the real, DST-safe UTC instant that local
  midnight on the 1st corresponds to (via the already-proven
  `zonedTimeToUtc`), for comparison against `interactions.occurred_at`
  (a true moment-in-time).
- `periodLabel` -- the human-readable month/year, in the fundraiser's
  own timezone (unchanged in behavior from before, just relocated).

`getFundraisingProgress` now calls this once and uses
`dateOnlyStartEpoch` for both `giving_activities` queries and
`instantStartEpoch` for the `interactions` (donors-contacted) query --
each value matched to the actual semantics of the column it is
compared against, rather than reusing one UTC-truncated timestamp for
both.

Profile timezone policy: `lib/auth/profile.ts` already defaults every
user's `timezone` to `"America/New_York"`, confirmed still the case --
no change needed there; this fix makes `fundraising_progress` actually
respect that stored value instead of silently falling back to UTC
regardless of it.

**Regression tests added** (`tests/local-time.test.mjs`, pure/unit,
all against `America/New_York`):
- A plain midday case (no boundary trickiness) confirms both epoch
  conventions compute correctly and differ from each other as
  expected.
- **The exact bug this fix targets**: `now` = Nov 1, 2026 02:00 UTC,
  which is still Oct 31, 2026 22:00 EDT -- asserts the boundary still
  reports "October 2026," not "November," proving a late-UTC-night
  moment no longer closes out the local month early.
- The mirror case just after the real local rollover (Nov 1 06:00 UTC
  = Nov 1 02:00 EDT) asserts the boundary HAS rolled over to November.
- A year-rollover case (Jan 1, 2026 03:00 UTC = Dec 31, 2025 22:00 EST)
  asserts it still reports December of the PRIOR year.
- A DST-transition case: evaluated well after March's "spring forward,"
  the month-start instant for March 1 itself must still use the
  EARLIER (EST) offset, since DST does not begin until March 8.
- Asserts `dateOnlyStartEpoch`/`instantStartEpoch` never collapse to the
  same value for a real (non-UTC) timezone -- guards against a future
  "simplification" silently reintroducing the single-boundary bug for
  the `occurred_at`-based count.
- `tests/assistant-capabilities-safety.test.mjs` (structural): asserts
  `capabilities.ts` never reintroduces `setUTCDate(1)` and does call
  the shared `localMonthBoundaries` helper.

**Live verification on Staging**: asked "Summarize this month's
fundraising progress for me" through the real live pipeline after
deploying the fix -- correctly labeled the real current period
"October 2026" (America/New_York) and returned real, internally
consistent aggregate totals (gift count/total, new-pledge count/total,
donors contacted) with no error. This round deliberately does not
restate those aggregate figures here (see Section 3 below) -- the
point verified is that the capability still functions correctly and
reports the correct LOCAL month post-fix, not the specific numbers.
Verifying the exact midnight-boundary edge case against a real
transaction dated precisely at a month boundary was NOT additionally
performed live, by design: doing so would have required either using
real donor financial records (ruled out by Section 3) or fabricating a
new backdated transaction on the synthetic test donor purely for this
test, which risks looking like real financial activity in the data and
was judged unnecessary -- the pure unit tests above already prove the
boundary arithmetic itself is correct for exactly this scenario,
deterministically and repeatably, which is the appropriate verification
method for date arithmetic (the same method every other date-logic fix
in this codebase, e.g. the due-date-resolver fixes, has used).

## Final Financial Accuracy Fix for Ask Fundraising OS (2026-10-16)

A second independent review, focused specifically on `getFundraisingProgress()`
in `lib/assistant/capabilities.ts`, found that the query had no upper
month boundary, excluded only `'open_pledge'` (letting
needs_review/nonfinancial_entry/pending_gift/pending_pledge rows count
as real donations), and could misrepresent a payment against an
existing pledge as either a new commitment or money received in the
wrong month. This entry documents the full investigation, the fix, the
authoritative definitions adopted, reconciliation evidence, and Staging
verification. Code/tests committed as `8431f49`, on top of `9789649`/
`a2fba82` (the prior independent-review round, above). No Production
file was read or written. No parallel or forked agent was used for any
part of this round's investigation, implementation, Staging deployment,
database access, or verification.

### 1. Investigation: how the financial data model actually works

Read in full: `lib/assistant/capabilities.ts`, `lib/financial-date.ts`,
`lib/workspace/local-time.ts`, `db/schema.ts` (giving_activities,
jl_payment_assignments, jl_payment_assignment_audits,
pledge_balance_corrections), `lib/import/jl-donations.ts` (the category
classifier), `lib/import/jl-refresh.ts`, `lib/import/jl-payment-assignment.ts`
(the payment-to-pledge reconciliation planner), `app/api/import/route.ts`
(the actual INSERT/UPDATE/UPSERT statements -- not assumed from the
schema or the planner alone), `lib/giving/management.ts`
(COUNTED_GIVING_SQL, the system-wide "what counts as real" filter), and
`lib/relationships/trip-financial-attribution.ts` (the Trip Fundraising
Results Dashboard's own `summarizeTripFinancials` -- the one other
place in this codebase that computes "new commitments" and "cash
collected").

**The central, load-bearing fact, confirmed directly against the exact
SQL this app runs (not inferred from the schema):**
`giving_activities.activity_date` is the JL Solutions export's own "Due
Date" column -- a forward-looking commitment/obligation date, explicitly
documented as such by `lib/import/jl-refresh.ts`'s own comment ("An open
or partially-paid pledge's stored date is the JL export's 'Due Date' for
an UNRESOLVED balance -- a forward-looking commitment/obligation, not a
record that money was actually received"). Critically, **it is never
updated once a payment is applied to that row**: the real UPDATE
statement (`app/api/import/route.ts`'s `pledgeUpdateStatements`) sets
only `paid_cents, balance_cents, category, source_snapshot, updated_at`
-- never `activity_date` -- and the ordinary re-import upsert path
(`ON CONFLICT ... DO UPDATE SET paid_cents=excluded.paid_cents, ...`)
likewise never touches it. A pledge paid off two years after its
original due date still carries that original due date forever.
`created_at`, by contrast, is set once at INSERT and is never touched by
either update path -- it reliably means "when this specific row first
entered the system."

**How a payment actually gets applied, and where (if anywhere) its real
date survives:** three distinct mechanisms exist.
1. **Ordinary reimport refresh** (the common case for a periodic full
   JL re-export): the SAME pledge line item (matched by
   `source_fingerprint`, which does NOT include Paid/Balance Due) is
   silently upserted with its new cumulative paid/balance figures. No
   record of which date that increase happened on survives anywhere --
   only that it had happened by the time of this particular import.
   This is a genuine, disclosed gap in the data model, not something
   this round invented a workaround for (see Section 6).
2. **Explicit "apply to pledge" decision** (the payment-review screen,
   triggered only for full-export rows recognized as payment-shaped by
   Item/Desc text): creates a `jl_payment_assignment_audits` row with a
   real `payment_date` (the source payment transaction's own date, not
   the import's processing time) and `applied_cents`/`new_gift_cents` --
   this is the one place a dated payment event against a pre-existing
   pledge actually exists.
3. **"New gift" decision** (same screen, when the payment doesn't match
   any pledge, or as an overpayment's remainder): creates a NEW
   `giving_activities` row (via `app/api/import/route.ts`'s
   `manualNewActivities`) AND a `jl_payment_assignment_audits` row. For
   a plain new-gift decision, the new row's `source_fingerprint` equals
   the audit row's own `payment_fingerprint`. For an overpayment's
   remainder specifically, the new row's fingerprint is instead
   `remainderGiftFingerprint(paymentFingerprint)` (`lib/import/
   jl-payment-assignment.ts`, exported and reused here rather than
   re-implemented) -- a DIFFERENT string than the main audit row's own
   fingerprint. Both cases must be excluded from "new money" sums to
   avoid double-counting; only the first is obvious from the fingerprint
   alone (see Section 3).

**The Trip Fundraising Results Dashboard's own precedent**
(`summarizeTripFinancials`) sidesteps this entire date-reliability
problem by using explicit, fundraiser-confirmed ATTRIBUTION rather than
date-range inference, and already treats `event_or_ad` (event/ad
revenue) as excluded from both "new commitments" and "cash collected."
This fix reuses that dashboard's exact `REAL_COMMITMENT_CATEGORIES` set
(`open_pledge`, `partially_paid_pledge`, `completed_gift`) for "what
counts as a real commitment," and deliberately excludes `event_or_ad`
from `fundraising_progress` too -- a consistency choice with that
existing dashboard, not a new decision invented here.

### 2. Authoritative financial definitions adopted

- **Money received this month**: the sum of every dollar with a KNOWN,
  dated receipt event falling in the fundraiser's local calendar month
  -- (a) a brand-new commitment-category row's `paid_cents` at the
  moment it was first recorded (`created_at` in-period), plus (b) every
  `jl_payment_assignment_audits` row whose `payment_date` (falling back
  to `created_at` only if that is somehow null, the exact same fallback
  the import route itself uses) falls in-period, summing
  `applied_cents + new_gift_cents`. **Never** activity_date-filtered.
  Counted once, reconciled against the two giving_activities-insert
  paths that can otherwise double it (Section 1.3 above).
- **New commitments this month**: the sum of `committed_cents` for every
  `REAL_COMMITMENT_CATEGORIES` row whose `created_at` falls in-period,
  regardless of payment status -- a pledge still unpaid, partially paid,
  or already paid in full all count in full the moment they are first
  recorded, exactly matching the Trip Dashboard's own "a pledge counts
  in full the moment it is confirmed" rule. A later payment against an
  OLDER pledge can never retroactively inflate this figure, because that
  pledge's `created_at` never changes.
- **Outstanding pledges**: unchanged by this round -- `getOutstandingPledges`
  already correctly joins `pledge_balance_corrections`
  (`COALESCE(pbc.corrected_balance_cents, ga.balance_cents)`), the exact
  pattern `app/pledge-review/page.tsx` itself uses. Confirmed still
  correct; this round added no new query for it.
- **Fundraising activity**: this capability already keeps new
  commitments, money received (split into new-gift vs.
  existing-pledge-payment), and donor contact counts as clearly separate
  fields -- never one blended figure -- so the assistant can answer "is
  this a new pledge or a payment on an old one" without guessing.

**Alignment with the Financial Dashboard**: the Trip Fundraising Results
Dashboard does not compute a period-bounded "money received this
calendar month" at all -- it reports lifetime-to-date paid/committed
figures for whatever records are explicitly attributed to a trip. There
is therefore no existing Financial Dashboard definition this capability
could contradict for that specific figure; this is the first place in
the codebase that computes it, and it is built to the most conservative,
defensible definition the data actually supports (Section 6 discloses
exactly where that falls short of "every dollar, no matter how it was
recorded").

### 3. Code changes

- **`lib/assistant/fundraising-progress.ts`** (new, pure, no
  `cloudflare:workers` import): exports the four literal SQL query
  strings (`NEW_COMMITMENTS_SQL`, `NEW_GIVING_ROWS_SQL`,
  `PAYMENT_ASSIGNMENT_AUDITS_SQL`, `DONORS_CONTACTED_SQL`) AND the
  reconciliation arithmetic (`summarizeFundraisingProgress`) -- the SQL
  lives here, not in capabilities.ts, specifically so a Node test can
  execute the real, literal queries without pulling in `cloudflare:workers`.
  The dedup set is built from both of a payment's possible giving_activities
  fingerprints (plain and `:remainder`-derived, via the imported
  `remainderGiftFingerprint`), not just one.
- **`lib/workspace/local-time.ts`**: `localMonthBoundaries` extended with
  `dateOnlyEndEpoch`/`instantEndEpoch` -- every monthly query now has a
  proper exclusive upper bound, computed with the same December-rollover-
  safe arithmetic as the existing start boundary.
- **`lib/assistant/capabilities.ts`**: `getFundraisingProgress` rewritten
  to run the four queries above and call `summarizeFundraisingProgress`;
  `FundraisingProgress`'s return shape changed to
  `moneyReceivedTotal`/`moneyReceivedTransactionCount`/`newGiftsReceivedTotal`/
  `paymentsOnExistingPledgesTotal`/`newCommitmentsTotal`/`newCommitmentsCount`/
  `donorsContacted`/`limitations`. The capability description shown to
  the planning AI was rewritten to describe the new breakdown.
- **`lib/assistant/protocol.ts`**: the compose system prompt gained two
  rules -- always relay a `limitations` entry when reporting that
  figure, and never state a donor/household/people count unless the
  data explicitly labels a field that way (Section 5 explains why the
  second rule exists).
- **`tests/relationship-snapshot-stage3.test.mjs`**: one pre-existing
  D1-query-count ceiling for `capabilities.ts` moved from `<=5` to
  `<=6`, with a comment explaining the one new query is in the unrelated
  `fundraising_progress` capability, not a second Snapshot lookup in
  `donor_summary` (that guarantee was independently re-verified, not
  merely assumed).

### 4. Reconciliation results -- synthetic scenarios

Ran against a real in-memory SQLite database (`node:sqlite`'s
`DatabaseSync`, built from this repo's own `drizzle/*.sql` migrations --
the same harness `tests/asks.test.mjs`/`tests/data-health.test.mjs`
already use), executing the literal exported SQL constants, for October
2026 in `America/New_York`:

| Scenario | Expected treatment | Actual result |
|---|---|---|
| Direct donation, no pledge | New commitment + money received, both $1,000 | ✅ Both $1,000 |
| New unpaid pledge, future due date | New commitment $500; $0 received | ✅ Exactly that -- future due date never read |
| New partially-paid pledge | New commitment $800; $300 received (its initial paid amount) | ✅ Exactly that |
| Payment on a pledge from a prior month | $0 new commitment (pledge predates this month); payment counted via audit | ✅ $0 commitment; $700 received via audit |
| Multiple installments, same pledge | Both installments summed independently | ✅ $700 + $200 = $900 |
| Payment imported after its true transaction date | Attributed to the TRUE payment date's month, not the import month | ✅ Placed in September (true date), confirmed absent from October AND present when September's own window is queried |
| Corrected pledge balance | Zero effect on either figure | ✅ No change (this capability never reads pledge_balance_corrections) |
| Cancelled/reversed transaction | Fully excluded | ✅ Excluded (workspace_status != 'active') |
| Future-dated transaction/pledge | Counted as a new commitment; NEVER as money received | ✅ $150 commitment; $0 received |
| Transaction at month start/end boundary | Inclusive start, exclusive end | ✅ At-start row included; at-end row excluded (belongs to next month); one-second-before-end row included |

Two additional scenarios, not in the review's list but essential to
this implementation's own correctness, also verified: a plain "new
gift" reconciliation decision (giving_activities row and audit row share
one fingerprint) counted exactly once, and an overpayment remainder
(giving_activities row under the DERIVED `:remainder` fingerprint, audit
row under the plain one) also counted exactly once.

### 5. AI safety -- two defects found, both fixed

**Structural (never relied on the model to self-police):** the AI plans
only by selecting from a fixed capability registry and a donor
reference; `fundraising_progress` performs zero writes, zero dynamic
SQL, and returns only the deterministic result of the queries above.
The compose step is instructed never to add, combine, or recompute a
dollar figure itself.

**Found only through live testing, fixed at the source:** asking the
real, live Staging assistant "How much money did we actually receive
this month, and how much of that came from existing pledges versus new
gifts?" returned a correct dollar breakdown but prefaced it with
**"you received $4,825 from 15 donors"** -- 15 was actually
`moneyReceivedCount`, a count of giving/payment ROWS (4 new rows + 11
payment-assignment audits), not a count of distinct donors. The model
inferred "donors" from an ambiguously-named field, which is exactly the
kind of confident misstatement this task was created to prevent. Fixed
by renaming the field to `moneyReceivedTransactionCount` everywhere (so
neither this code nor the model can relabel it) and adding an explicit
compose-prompt rule: never state a donor/household/people count unless
the data explicitly labels a field that way. Re-tested live after the
fix -- the same question now returns "$4,825 in total" with the correct
breakdown and no fabricated donor count. A new structural test
(`tests/assistant-capabilities-safety.test.mjs`) locks in that the
ambiguous field name can never reappear and that the compose prompt rule
stays present.

### 6. Disclosed limitation -- payments without a recorded date

Payments applied to an existing pledge through an ordinary JL reimport
refresh (mechanism 1 in Section 1) have no payment date recorded
anywhere in this schema -- only that the pledge's paid/balance figures
had changed by the time of that particular import. This capability does
**not** estimate or guess at that date; it is excluded from "money
received this month" entirely, and every `fundraising_progress` result
carries an explicit `limitations` entry stating this plainly, which the
compose prompt is instructed to always relay. **This means the
assistant's "money received" figure can be a genuine UNDER-count**
relative to the fundraiser's own intuitive sense of "everything that
came in," specifically for pledge payments that were never run through
the payment-review screen.

**The safest system-wide solution, proposed but NOT implemented this
round** (per the task's own instruction to stop and explain before a
schema/import-process change): route every ordinary reimport-detected
paid/balance increase through the same `jl_payment_assignment_audits`
trail the explicit review screen already uses, recording a payment date
derived from the import's own processing time (an honest "when we found
out" date, clearly distinguished from a payment-review-confirmed "when
it actually happened" date) rather than leaving it unrecorded. This
would require a product decision (is "when we found out" an acceptable
date for a reimport-detected payment, or should the fundraiser be asked
to confirm/correct it, as they already are for explicitly payment-shaped
rows?) and a migration-free code change to `app/api/import/route.ts`'s
existing upsert path -- not attempted here, since it changes import/
payment-processing behavior beyond this review's own scope and was
explicitly called out as something to stop and discuss first.

### 7. Donor privacy during this round's own testing -- disclosed

Direct SQL verification against Staging (via `wrangler d1 execute`,
read-only, no AI involved) used only account-wide AGGREGATE totals --
no individual donor name or identifying detail. Live AI-pipeline testing
of `fundraising_progress` itself (aggregate totals only) and of
`donor_summary` (the existing synthetic "QA TEST" donor only) stayed
within that same boundary.

**One incidental exposure, disclosed rather than hidden**: a single
broader test question ("How much was newly pledged this month, and how
much is still outstanding?") was answered by the planner selecting BOTH
`fundraising_progress` and `outstanding_pledges` -- the second
capability lists real donors by name, and its response surfaced five
real donor names and ids in this session. This was not anticipated when
the question was written; it demonstrates that the donor-privacy
safeguard established in the prior round (reuse the synthetic donor)
protects against a tester deliberately asking about a specific real
donor, but does **not** by itself prevent an innocuously-phrased,
multi-capability question from incidentally invoking a donor-listing
capability during financial-feature testing. No real donor name is
repeated in this document. **Recommended safeguard for future rounds**:
when verifying one capability live, phrase test questions narrowly
enough that the planner cannot reasonably select an unrelated,
donor-listing capability, or test via conversation.lastDonorRefs/direct
capability dispatch rather than an open-ended natural-language question
whenever the capability under test is not itself donor-scoped.

## Final Payment Accuracy and Financial Data Integrity Review (2026-10-16)

A second, more targeted independent review of the prior round's own fix
found that it could still misattribute money to the wrong month in one
specific way, and that its disclosed-limitation wording made a claim
the system cannot actually honor. Both are fixed here. Code/tests
committed as `36eddff`, on top of `8431f49`/`9789649` (the two prior
independent-review rounds, above). No Production file was read or
written. No parallel or forked agent was used for any part of this
round's investigation, implementation, Staging deployment, database
access, or verification.

### 1. The cumulative-payment problem, traced exactly as asked

**The example traced, stage by stage, against a real giving_activities
row and a real synthetic SQLite database** (`tests/fundraising-progress.test.mjs`'s
own "Part C"): a pledge is imported October 5 with $200 of $1,000
already paid (a brand-new row -- `created_at = updated_at` = Oct 5).
October 20, a ROUTINE reimport (no payment-review decision -- JL's own
re-export simply shows a higher cumulative Paid value for the SAME
pledge line, matched by `source_fingerprint`) bumps the row's
`paid_cents` to $500; `created_at` is untouched, `updated_at` moves to
Oct 20. November 10, another routine reimport bumps it to $800;
`updated_at` moves to Nov 10.

**What the PRIOR round's fix would have reported, confirmed by
re-running its own logic against this exact lifecycle**: querying
"October's money received" immediately after the Oct 20 reimport (still
in October) returned $500 -- defensible, since both $200 and the extra
$300 happened within the same calendar month either way. But querying
the SAME "October" figure again AFTER the Nov 10 reimport -- e.g. the
fundraiser asking in December "how much did we actually raise in
October" -- returned **$800**, silently including the $300 that was
only discovered in November. A previously-reported, closed month's own
total was changing purely because of when the query happened to run,
with no real underlying change to what happened in October. Confirmed
directly against the real SQL (not assumed): the prior round's
`NEW_GIVING_ROWS_SQL` read `paid_cents` LIVE at query time for any row
whose `created_at` fell in the requested window, with nothing
distinguishing "what was paid at creation" from "what is currently
paid, including everything added since by unrelated later imports."

**Verified against the exact question list:**
- **Attribute later payments to the original import month?** Yes --
  confirmed this was happening (the $300 from November's reimport was
  being reported as part of October's total when queried after the
  fact). Fixed.
- **Count the same payment twice?** No -- the existing fingerprint-based
  dedup against `jl_payment_assignment_audits` was already correct and
  remains unchanged; this defect was about mis-DATING money, not
  double-counting it.
- **Change historical monthly totals when a later import occurs?**
  Yes, confirmed directly -- this was the core defect. Fixed; October's
  own figure is now provably stable across any number of later imports
  (Section 2).
- **Confuse the date a record was imported with the date money was
  received?** Yes, for this one path specifically (the ordinary reimport
  refresh) -- confirmed there is no recorded payment date anywhere for
  it, and the prior fix's `created_at` gate was not sufficient protection
  once a row is touched again after its own creation.
- **Overstate or understate cash received?** Both were possible
  depending on when the query ran: overstated for a closed month
  re-queried after a later reimport (as traced above); and, after this
  round's fix, intentionally UNDERSTATED by design going forward --
  Section 4 explains why understating, with a clear disclosure, is the
  safer failure mode than overstating.

### 2. The fix

`VERIFIED_NEW_GIVING_ROWS_SQL` (renamed from the prior round's
`NEW_GIVING_ROWS_SQL`) adds `AND updated_at = created_at` to its
existing `created_at` window filter. `updated_at` is set once, at
INSERT, to the exact same value as `created_at`; both payment-processing
paths (the ordinary reimport upsert and the explicit payment-review
screen's pledge update) bump `updated_at` to the import's own `now` on
any GENUINE change -- confirmed directly against `app/api/import/route.ts`'s
own `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE`/`pledgeUpdateStatements` SQL, not assumed.
`updated_at = created_at` is therefore the one already-populated,
reliable signal that a row's current `paid_cents` is still exactly what
it was at that single creation event -- nothing added since. The
moment a later import touches an in-period row, its contribution to the
VERIFIED figure drops to **zero**, not a partial or estimated amount --
it can only re-enter a reported total through the dated
`jl_payment_assignment_audits` path, which already has a real date.

This makes the verified total provably **stable**: once computed for a
closed month, nothing a later import does can change it, because every
row that could still change has already been excluded from it. Traced
and confirmed directly: re-querying October's figure after the November
reimport in the test above returns the exact same value it did
immediately after the October reimport -- not what it eventually
becomes.

**The explicit trade-off, by design**: this is more conservative than
the prior round's fix, not less. It can now UNDER-report real money
received (the $300 added in November is never counted as received
anywhere, in any month, by this capability), but it can never again
OVER-report, and it can never again change its mind about a closed
month. Per this round's own stated priority ("trustworthy financial
information, not making the AI appear more capable than the underlying
records allow"), under-reporting with a clear, mandatory disclosure is
the correct trade-off against over-reporting or an unstable figure.

**The CURRENT cumulative balance is still visible**, just honestly
relabeled: `NEW_COMMITMENTS_SQL` now also returns
`cumulativePaidTotal` (`SUM(paid_cents)` across the same
in-period commitment rows, with no `updated_at` filter -- a live
snapshot, by design) surfaced as `recordedCumulativePaidTotal` in
`capabilities.ts`'s own `FundraisingProgress` type. This is the second
category the task asked to be distinguished: "recorded cumulative
payments" vs. "verified money received." It is never labeled
"received," and the capability description shown to the planning AI
says so explicitly.

### 3. The limitation wording, corrected

The prior wording said an omitted payment "will be reflected once that
pledge is fully paid or its payment is processed through the review
screen" -- false, and now removed. This capability has no mechanism
that EVER retroactively attributes a past, undated payment increase to
any month, no matter what later happens to that pledge (including
becoming fully paid). The revised text
(`lib/assistant/fundraising-progress.ts`'s `RECONCILIATION_LIMITATION`):

> "Verified dated payments above include only: (1) new pledges or gifts
> first recorded this period whose balance has not changed since, and
> (2) payments confirmed through the payment-review screen with a known
> date. They do NOT include a later increase to an existing pledge's
> paid balance that arrived through a routine data refresh with no
> payment-review decision -- this system has no record of which date
> that money arrived, cannot place it in any specific month, and will
> never retroactively add it to a later total even once that pledge is
> fully paid. The actual total received this period may be understated
> as a result. A payment-event ledger recording the date and amount of
> every individual payment, not just each pledge's current cumulative
> balance, would be needed to close this gap."

This states plainly which records ARE included, which CANNOT be placed
in a month and why, that the total may be UNDERSTATED (not simply
"incomplete" in some vaguer sense), and what would actually close the
gap (Section 4's design).

**Enforced in the deterministic response layer, not solely the
prompt**: `lib/assistant/protocol.ts`'s new `appendFinancialLimitations(answer,
limitations)` unconditionally appends every `fundraising_progress`
limitation string to the final composed answer, called from
`lib/assistant/orchestrator.ts` after the compose AI call returns --
regardless of whether the model's own text already mentioned it. The
compose prompt still separately instructs the model to relay it (belt
and suspenders), but the actual guarantee no longer depends on the
model remembering to. Verified live (Section 7): the real Staging
response contained BOTH the model's own paraphrase of the limitation
AND the literal, deterministically-appended text -- redundant on
purpose, never dropped.

### 4. Investigation: a reliable payment-event ledger

**What already exists**: `jl_payment_assignment_audits` is, structurally,
exactly the shape of a payment-event ledger already -- `payment_date`,
`payment_cents`/`applied_cents`/`new_gift_cents`, `pledge_activity_id`
(link to the original pledge), `import_id` (provenance), and a unique
`(import_id, payment_fingerprint)` index that already makes repeated
imports of the identical payment idempotent (confirmed: a re-imported
file containing the same payment fingerprint is recognized via
`jl_payment_assignments`' own "remembered decision" lookup and never
re-processed). It is **immutable once written** -- confirmed no code
path in this repository ever issues an `UPDATE` against this table, only
`INSERT`. The one thing it does not have is a `reversed_at`/correction
mechanism of its own (unlike `pledge_balance_corrections`, which does).

**Why it does not cover every payment today**: it is populated ONLY
when an incoming row is recognized as "payment-shaped" by
`lib/import/jl-donations.ts`'s `isExplicitJlPayment` -- `Item Num`/`Desc`
text matching `/\b(?:payment|pmt|pymt|installment)\b/i`, with a positive
`Paid` value. A row that does not match this pattern, but whose
Paid/Balance Due columns changed from the previously-stored value for
the same pledge line item, is instead treated as an ordinary
`proposedUpdates` row (`lib/import/jl-donation-match.ts`) and silently
upserted with no audit trail at all.

**A concrete, fixable finding (code-level, confirmed, not
speculative)**: this repository's OWN test fixtures
(`tests/payment-assignment.test.mjs`) model JL Solutions' full export
format as carrying a SEPARATE line item per payment transaction (e.g.
`Item Num: "PAYMENT", Desc: "Pledge payment"`) alongside the pledge's
own line item (`Item Num: "PLEDGE"`) -- meaning JL's export format DOES
appear to support genuine per-payment granularity with its own date, at
least for payments recorded this way. The regex above, however, is
narrower than the full space of plausible real-world payment
descriptions -- it would miss, for example, "Check #1234," "ACH Debit,"
"Auto-Pay," "Credit Card," or "CC" (none contain "payment," "pmt,"
"pymt," or "installment" as a whole word). **It is plausible that some
genuinely itemized payment rows in a real JL export are currently
mis-routed to the ordinary, undated upsert path purely because of this
text-matching gap** -- a real, narrow, fixable importer defect, not a
schema limitation.

**What remains genuinely uncertain, disclosed rather than guessed at**:
whether JL Solutions' own export ALWAYS includes a dedicated transaction
line for every payment, or whether some payment types (e.g. one
recorded directly inside JL's own software without flowing back out as
a distinct exported row) genuinely have no line-item representation at
all in any export this importer could ever see. This cannot be resolved
from this codebase alone -- it requires inspecting an actual recent JL
Solutions export file's raw `Item Num`/`Desc` columns around a pledge
whose Paid value is known to have changed via the ordinary reimport
path, which was not available to check this round. **Recommended next
step, not performed here**: the owner (or whoever runs the next JL
export) checks one real file for this directly.

**Recommended payment-event ledger design** (for a future,
separately-authorized round -- not implemented here):
- Extend the existing `jl_payment_assignment_audits` role (or a new,
  equivalently-shaped table) to record a payment event for EVERY
  detected `paid_cents` increase on reimport, not only text-pattern-
  recognized "payment-shaped" rows -- i.e. route `proposedUpdates`'
  paid-amount deltas through the same ledger `apply_to_pledge` already
  uses.
- Record the DELTA (new minus previously-stored paid_cents), never the
  full cumulative value, so idempotency is preserved automatically by
  the existing diffing in `lib/import/jl-donation-match.ts` (already
  confirmed to only flag genuinely changed rows).
- Add an explicit `date_confidence` field distinguishing an
  EXPLICIT/CONFIRMED payment date (from a recognized payment-shaped row,
  or a fundraiser's own confirmation) from a DISCOVERY date (the
  import's own processing time, used only when no better date is
  available) -- never silently blur the two.
- Broaden `isExplicitJlPayment`'s text pattern per the finding above, as
  its own small, separately-reviewable fix, independent of the larger
  ledger work.
- Decide, separately, whether to backfill historical rows with a
  discovery-dated event derived from each row's own `updated_at` -- this
  is a genuine historical-backfill decision requiring its own
  authorization, not a mechanical migration.

**What this round explicitly did NOT do, per the task's own
restriction**: no new table, no migration, no change to
`app/api/import/route.ts`'s actual import/payment-processing behavior,
and no historical backfill. The design above is a recommendation for a
separate, future, separately-authorized round.

**1. Can Ask Fundraising OS now report monthly money received without
overstating what the records prove?** Yes. The verified figure is now

## Resolve Historical Payment Totals Before Production (2026-10-16)

A fourth independent review identified a genuine contradiction in the
immediately prior round's own fix: requiring `updated_at = created_at`
stopped a verified total from ever being inflated by a later reimport,
but introduced the opposite defect -- it could retroactively DEFLATE a
previously-reported total to $0. This entry documents the root cause,
confirms it against the exact example given, and replaces the blunt
all-or-nothing rule with a reconstruction that is both accurate and
genuinely stable. Code/tests committed as `960ba6a`, on top of
`36eddff`/`8431f49`/`9789649` (the three prior independent-review
rounds on this feature, above). No Production file was read or
written. No parallel or forked agent was used for any part of this
round's investigation, implementation, Staging deployment, database
access, or verification.

### 1. The contradiction, confirmed against the exact example

Traced directly against the prior round's own logic (not assumed):
`updated_at = created_at` is a correlated fact about a SINGLE row's
entire lifetime -- the moment ANY later import touches that row for ANY
reason, the condition becomes permanently false, and `VERIFIED_NEW_GIVING_ROWS_SQL`
excludes the row from the verified total **for every period it was ever
asked about, past or future, forever** -- not just the period in which
the touch happened.

Confirmed exactly as given: a pledge imported October 5 with $200
already paid, queried October 20 -- correctly reports $200 (nothing has
touched it yet). A routine reimport on November 10 then bumps its
cumulative paid to $500. Querying "October's money received" again on
December 1 -- after that November reimport -- returns **$0**, not $200.
The original $200 was never contradicted, reduced, or shown to be
wrong; it simply stopped being reportable because the row's
`updated_at` had moved. This is confirmed to be a real defect, not a
misreading of the prior round's own intent: that round's own
documentation called the figure "stable," which was true in the narrow
sense of "cannot inflate," but false in the broader sense the word
actually implies -- the figure could, and did, retroactively change.

### 2. The correct reporting standard

Per the task's own four categories, re-stated against what this
capability can now actually prove:

1. **Verified dated payment events** -- payments confirmed through the
   payment-review screen (`jl_payment_assignment_audits`, a real
   `payment_date`). Unchanged by this round.
2. **Cumulative paid balances** -- `recordedCumulativePaidTotal`, the
   CURRENT, live `paid_cents` on commitments created this period.
   Explicitly never called "received"; expected to keep moving for an
   open period.
3. **New commitments** -- `newCommitmentsTotal`/`newCommitmentsCount`,
   gated on `created_at` (immutable) and `committed_cents` (never
   touched by any payment-processing path). Unchanged by this round.
4. **Unverified historical payment timing** -- payments applied to a
   PRE-EXISTING pledge (created in an earlier period) via an ordinary
   reimport, with no payment-review decision. This is the one category
   that remains genuinely unverifiable with the current import pipeline,
   and is disclosed, not guessed at (Section 3).

**Neither `created_at` nor `updated_at` is ever treated as a payment
date** -- both are used only as structural anchors for determining
WHICH ROW and WHICH REPORTING PERIOD a reconstruction applies to, never
as evidence of when cash was physically received. This distinction is
what the fix in Section 3 is built around: it reconstructs "what the
record showed as of a period boundary," which is a fact this app's own
import history can prove, not "what day the money arrived," which it
generally cannot.

### 3. The fix: reconstruct from the existing import change log

**The data this fix reuses already exists and already captures exactly
what is needed, confirmed directly, not assumed:**
`giving_activity_import_changes` was introduced in the SAME migration
that created `giving_activities` itself (`drizzle/0003_jl_donation_import.sql`)
-- there is no historical gap for any row this app has ever stored. Its
`previous_json` column records a row's PRIOR state -- including
`paid_cents` -- immediately before every single UPDATE this app makes to
a `giving_activities` row, and this is written atomically, in the SAME
D1 batch as the UPDATE itself (confirmed against `app/api/import/route.ts`'s
own single `env.DB.batch(statements)` call -- the two writes can never
drift apart).

**The reconstruction**: for a row created in period P, "verified
paid_cents as of P's own end" is computed by `VERIFIED_NEW_GIVING_ROWS_SQL`'s
correlated subquery: find the EARLIEST change-log entry for this row
whose own `created_at` falls ON OR AFTER period P's end, and read
`paid_cents` from THAT entry's `previous_json` -- the value that was
true immediately before that later change, which is exactly the value
that held for the entire remainder of P. When no such later entry
exists (the row has never been touched since, or P has not ended yet),
the row's CURRENT `paid_cents` already IS that value, and the query
falls through to it directly.

**Why this is genuinely, provably stable, not merely "less wrong"**: a
change-log entry's `created_at` is real wall-clock time, set once, when
that specific import actually ran. No future import can ever insert an
entry timestamped before a period that has already ended -- so once
period P closes, every entry that could ever affect "what was true as
of P's end" already exists, and the computed value can never change
again. Re-querying October in December now correctly and permanently
returns **$500** -- not the first round's inflated $800, and not the
second round's deflated $0, both confirmed directly via the real
reconstruction query against synthetic data (Section 5).

**No new table, no backfill, no import-pipeline change** -- this is a
read-only reporting enhancement over data the import pipeline already
writes on every single update, exactly matching the task's own
"evaluate... whether the current payment audit table can be extended
safely" question for a RELATED table it already keeps without being
asked to touch it.

**What this does NOT fix, disclosed plainly**: a payment applied to a
PRE-EXISTING pledge (one created in an EARLIER period than the one being
queried) via the ordinary reimport path still has no verifiable date --
the reconstruction above only recovers "what a row created THIS period
looked like by this period's end," not "exactly which day within this
period an older pledge's balance changed." The limitation wording
(`lib/assistant/fundraising-progress.ts`'s `RECONCILIATION_LIMITATION`)
was corrected accordingly -- it previously said new rows were only
verified "whose balance has not changed since," which was true of the
prior round's fix, not this one, and has been replaced with the
accurate, narrower statement about pre-existing pledges specifically.

**A further discovery, documented for a future round, not implemented
here**: the SAME reconstruction technique generalizes cleanly to
PRE-EXISTING pledges too -- for any `giving_activity_import_changes`
entry whose own `created_at` falls within a queried period, the DELTA
between its `previous_json.paid_cents` and the value that replaced it is
a real, dated amount of money that changed hands during that period,
regardless of whether the row itself was created in that period or
years earlier. This would close the remaining gap entirely using data
that already exists today, with no new table and no import-pipeline
change -- a materially simpler path to a complete solution than the
`jl_payment_assignment_audits`-extension design proposed in the prior
round's Section 4, and likely the preferred "Phase 1" recommendation for
whichever future round implements a full payment-event ledger. Not
implemented this round because it was not what this review asked for,
and because generalizing "payments on existing pledges" to include this
new source would change that figure's own definition in a way that
deserves its own dedicated review rather than being folded in
unprompted.

### 4. A second live-discovered donor-count fabrication, fixed

During this round's own mandated Staging verification (Section 7), a
SECOND instance of the donor-count fabrication the prior round fixed
was found live: asked "How much was newly pledged this month?", the
model answered **"$1,910 was newly pledged by 4 donors"** -- 4 was
`newCommitmentsCount`, a count of commitment ROWS, not distinct donors
(the same donor can make more than one pledge in a month). The prior
round's generic rule ("never state a number of donors... unless the
data explicitly labels a field that way") did not stop this the first
time it was tried against this specific field. The rule in
`lib/assistant/protocol.ts`'s compose prompt is now strengthened with
concrete, named field examples (`newCommitmentsCount`,
`moneyReceivedTransactionCount`) rather than speaking only in the
abstract, and re-verified live: the identical question, re-asked after
the fix, now correctly answers "4 new pledges or gifts, totaling
$1,910" with no donor count at all.

Also verified: explicit dated payment-review assignments (unchanged,

## Final Financial Reporting Integrity and Data Isolation Review (2026-10-16)

A fifth independent review found two real, distinct defects in the
immediately prior round's own reconstruction fix: a mislabeling (a
balance snapshot was being presented as a verified cash receipt) and a
genuine cross-owner data-isolation gap in the reconstruction query
itself. Both are fixed here, the second verified as a real exploit (not
a theoretical one) before and after the fix. Code/tests committed as
`9bd0863`, on top of `960ba6a`/`36eddff`/`8431f49`/`9789649` (the four
prior independent-review rounds on this feature, above). No Production
file was read or written. No parallel or forked agent was used for any
part of this round's investigation, implementation, Staging deployment,
database access, or verification.

### 1. Were reconstructed balances mislabeled as actual receipts? Yes -- confirmed and fixed

The prior round's `verifiedMoneyReceivedCents` field combined two
different kinds of evidence under one "verified" name: (a) real, dated
payment-review transactions, and (b) a new commitment-category row's
reconstructed paid_cents as of this period's end. (b) is a fact about
WHICH ROW/PERIOD a snapshot belongs to -- it is not proof of WHEN the
underlying cash was received. The review's own example confirms this
directly: a donor who actually paid $500 in September, whose pledge is
not imported into Fundraising OS until October, would have had that
entire $500 counted as "verified money received in October" -- which is
false. The money was recorded in October; nothing in this schema says
it was received then.

**Fix**: three categories, now never conflated anywhere in code, test,
prompt, or capability description:
- **A. Verified dated payments** (`verifiedDatedPaymentsCents`) -- a
  real, individually-dated transaction confirmed through the payment-
  review screen. The ONLY figure this feature will ever call "received"
  or "verified."
- **B. Recorded paid balance** (`recordedPaidBalanceCents`) -- what a
  pledge/gift first recorded this period shows as paid, reconstructed
  to its value as of this period's own end. A record-keeping fact,
  explicitly described everywhere as "recorded as paid"/"shown as
  paid," never "received."
- **C. New commitments** (`newCommitmentsCents`, unchanged) -- never
  confused with money received of any kind.

The old `recordedCumulativePaidTotal` ("live, today" balance) field was
removed entirely -- it was a fourth, confusing number that did not map
onto any of the task's three required categories; Category B (as-of-
period-end) already covers what it was meant for.

### 2. `source_fingerprint`'s exact uniqueness and ownership guarantees -- investigated directly, not assumed

- **`giving_activities` itself**: unique per `(owner_user_id,
  external_source, source_fingerprint)` -- confirmed via
  `drizzle/0004_personalization_live_data.sql`, which explicitly
  *replaced* an original 2-column `(external_source,
  source_fingerprint)` unique index specifically because it was too
  broad. Two different users CAN share an identical fingerprint without
  colliding in this table; two different donors under the SAME user
  CANNOT (the 3-column index would reject the second insert outright --
  proven directly in this round's own tests, Section 5, not merely
  inferred from the index's name).
- **`source_fingerprint` itself**: a pure SHA-256 hash of row CONTENT
  only (`lib/import/jl-donations.ts`'s `canonicalFingerprint`: JL code,
  date, item, description, campaign, amount, company) -- no user or
  donor identity is folded into the hash at all. It is NOT globally
  unique by construction; uniqueness is only ever enforced by whichever
  table's own index says so.
- **`giving_activity_import_changes`** (the change-log table the
  reconstruction reads from): its ONLY key is `(import_id,
  source_fingerprint)` -- confirmed directly against
  `drizzle/0003_jl_donation_import.sql`, the migration that created it,
  with no later migration ever adding an owner/user column. **It has no
  owner-scoping of its own at all.** The only path to a user is through
  `data_imports.user_id`, via `import_id`.
- **Conclusion, not assumed**: two different users whose JL exports
  happen to produce an identical fingerprint (plausible in practice --
  JL "Code" values are small, organization-assigned integers, easily
  reused across unrelated accounts) could, before this round's fix,
  have one user's balance reconstruction silently read a different
  user's change-log row.

### 3. The fix: an owner-scoped join, and the removed `created_at` fallback

`RECORDED_PAID_BALANCE_ROWS_SQL`'s correlated subquery now joins through
`data_imports` and requires `di.user_id = ga.owner_user_id` -- the
historical import that produced a change-log entry must belong to the
SAME user as the row being reconstructed, or that entry is never
considered. This is the only thing that closes the gap described in
Section 2, since `giving_activity_import_changes` itself cannot be
scoped any other way.

Separately, `VERIFIED_DATED_PAYMENT_AUDITS_SQL` no longer accepts
`COALESCE(payment_date, created_at)` as a stand-in for a missing payment
date -- it now requires `payment_date IS NOT NULL` explicitly. A
payment-review decision with no recorded date is instead surfaced by
the new `UNDATED_PAYMENT_AUDITS_SQL`, excluded from BOTH Category A
(no date to verify) and Category B (its own giving_activities row, if
any, is excluded from the balance figure too, so the money is never
silently re-presented under a different label) -- and disclosed as its
own dynamic `limitations` entry with a count and dollar total, never
silently dropped. In practice this should be rare to nonexistent:
`lib/import/jl-payment-assignment.ts`'s own `buildPaymentCandidates`
already blocks (never commits) a payment row with no parseable date
before it can ever reach this table -- confirmed live on Staging
(Section 7): zero undated rows exist in the real dataset today. This
query no longer assumes that invariant holds, though; it verifies
`payment_date` itself, every time.

### 4. Was a payment applied via ordinary reimport ever counted as dated? No, re-confirmed

Every `jl_payment_assignment_audits` row in the real Staging dataset
(91 rows total, 11 with a `payment_date` in October) was confirmed, live,
to already have a genuine `payment_date` -- zero rows depend on, or are
affected by, the removed fallback. Reversal/correction behavior is
unchanged from the prior round: `pledge_balance_corrections` is a
separate overlay table this capability never reads, confirmed (again)
to have zero effect on either category; a `workspace_status`-reversed
row is fully excluded from both. Double-counting protection (the
fingerprint-based dedup between a new giving_activities row and its own
audit decision, including the derived `:remainder` fingerprint for
overpayment splits) is unchanged and re-verified.
