### 5. Deployment and rollback plan (prepared, not executed)

**Exact release commit**: `354b889e6bb8178abfd639364311d484b5b79f1c` on `release/trip-confirmation-production`, pushed to `origin`. **Review PR**: **https://github.com/shimmy12345/ner-yisroel-fundraising-studio-v3/pull/21** -- opened against `feature/trip-meeting-add-to-google-calendar` (the branch sitting exactly at the live Production commit, not `main`), so the PR's own diff is the complete, exact diff from what Production runs today. Not merged; this is for review only, consistent with this codebase's established pattern of deploying an isolated release branch directly via `wrangler deploy`, never through a `main` merge.

**Exact additive migration SQL** (both already committed as `drizzle/0050_trip_attribution_confirmation.sql` and `drizzle/0051_trip_reconciliation_concurrency_guard.sql` on the release branch):

```sql
-- 0050_trip_attribution_confirmation.sql
ALTER TABLE `trip_financial_attributions` ADD COLUMN `donor_confirmed_at` integer;
ALTER TABLE `trip_financial_attributions` ADD COLUMN `commitment_kind` text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'new_commitment' CHECK (`commitment_kind` IN ('new_commitment','preexisting_pledge_collection'));
ALTER TABLE `trip_financial_attributions` ADD COLUMN `reported_cash_collected_cents` integer;
ALTER TABLE `trip_financial_attributions` ADD COLUMN `reconciled_pending_attribution_id` text;

-- 0051_trip_reconciliation_concurrency_guard.sql
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX `trip_financial_attributions_active_reconciled_pending_uidx` ON `trip_financial_attributions` (`reconciled_pending_attribution_id`) WHERE `removed_at` IS NULL AND `reconciled_pending_attribution_id` IS NOT NULL;
```

Both are purely additive (new nullable/safely-defaulted columns, one new partial index); neither alters, drops, or renames any existing column, index, or row, and neither touches any table besides `trip_financial_attributions`.

**Deployment order**:
1. Fresh, confirmed-successful Production backup immediately before anything else (Workspace Health UI, authenticated -- see Section 4).
2. Apply `0050` then `0051` to `fundraising-os-production-db` via `wrangler d1 execute --remote --file=...`, in that order (0051's index depends on 0050's column existing) -- **before** deploying any new Worker code. The currently-live Worker code (`adb97c0`, unaware of these columns) is completely unaffected by their existence: it never selects, inserts, or reads them, so applying the migration first is a true no-op for current traffic -- old code keeps working exactly as it does today, both before and immediately after the migration runs.
3. Verify the migration applied cleanly (re-query `sqlite_master` for the new columns/index; re-confirm the Bashevkin row count and `donor_confirmed_at` value -- see Section 6).
4. Only then deploy the new Worker version (`wrangler deploy --config wrangler.production.jsonc` from the `release/trip-confirmation-production` branch) -- the new code is the first and only code that ever reads or writes the four new columns or relies on the new index.

**Rollback compatibility**: if the new Worker code needs to be rolled back after deployment, **roll back the Worker version only** (`wrangler rollback` to `b79b0182-0422-49b2-bc76-059fd73d8c69`, or redeploy from `adb97c0`) -- **leave the additive schema changes in place**. The old code was already proven safe to run against the new schema in Step 2 above (it simply never references the new columns/index), so there is no need to, and no script exists to, reverse the migration. This matches the task's own explicit instruction and this codebase's established precedent (every prior Production release in this project follows the same "migrate first, additive only, never reversed on rollback" pattern).

## AI Meeting Notes from Trip Planning, and the Bashevkin/Cohen JL Reconciliation Diagnosis (2026-10-21)

Two items handled together per the owner's own combined instruction. Item 1 (AI meeting notes) was implemented, tested, and deployed to Staging only. Item 2 (JL reconciliation) was investigated read-only on Production; no code or data changed for it.

### Item 1 -- AI meeting notes directly from Trip Planning

**What changed.** A trip prospect's own card (`app/travel-planning/[id]/TripDashboardExperience.tsx`) now shows a "✦ AI meeting notes" link beside the meeting-time line, for any prospect whose status is `meeting_scheduled` or `meeting_completed` -- exactly the two statuses that already have a real `interactions` row (`trip_prospects.linked_interaction_id`; see `lib/relationships/trip-model.ts`'s `statusRequiresInteraction()`). For an earlier-stage prospect (not yet scheduled), the link is simply absent -- never a guessed or fabricated interaction, matching the feature's own existing "must not automatically create false donor interactions" discipline.

Clicking it opens a new page, `app/travel-planning/[id]/prospects/[prospectId]/meeting-notes/page.tsx`, which renders the **same** `MeetingNotesExperience` component the donor profile's own "+ Add Meeting Notes" button already uses (same Organize-with-AI review screen, same structured fields, same `/api/meeting-notes/organize` AI call). The only differences, gated by a new optional `tripContext` prop:
- The meeting date/type pickers are hidden (with an inline note: "This meeting's date and type are set from the trip itself and aren't changed here") -- the real date/time/location belong to the trip meeting itself and are load-bearing for the Add-to-Google-Calendar sync on that same interaction; this screen only ever touches `summary`.
- The screen is pre-loaded with the interaction's **existing** saved summary (`initialSummaryText`), so reopening it later shows what was already saved -- there is no separate structured copy to restore into the individual fields (interactions.summary has always been a single free-text column; see `lib/meeting-notes/format.ts`'s own header comment), so reopening shows the flattened text, exactly like the donor-profile flow's own save format.
- Saving posts to a **new, dedicated route** -- `app/api/trips/[id]/prospects/[prospectId]/meeting-notes/route.ts` -- not a branch of the existing `/api/meeting-notes/route.ts` (that file is completely unmodified except for one explanatory comment; diff confirmed functionally empty). This keeps every Trip Planning write under the `/api/trips/**` prefix, which is the one the Staging write guard's existing carve-out covers (`lib/operations/staging-write-guard.ts`, enforced by a repo-wide route walk in `tests/staging-write-guard.test.mjs`) -- folding trip-scoped saves into the donor-profile route would have silently lost that carve-out and made the feature untestable on Staging without the blanket `STAGING_WRITES_ENABLED` override.

**The reliable interaction link, used throughout:** a new `getProspectMeetingNotesTarget(userId, tripId, prospectId)` in `lib/relationships/trips-data.ts` re-derives the authoritative `trip_prospects.linked_interaction_id` (never guesses by donor/date), confirms the linked `interactions` row actually exists, and returns `{ donorId, donorDisplayName, interactionId, existingSummary }` or an explicit `{ reason: "not_found" | "no_meeting_yet" }`. Both the new page (server component, returns `notFound()` on failure -- a defensive backstop, since the card itself never links here without a valid meeting) and the new API route call this same function independently (never trusting a client-supplied id).

**Same underlying notes and meeting interaction, not a separate copy.** The save route's interaction write is a plain `UPDATE interactions SET summary = ?, updated_at = ? WHERE id = ? AND donor_id = ? AND user_id = ?` against the exact row `scheduleProspectMeeting`/`completeProspectMeeting` already created -- never an INSERT, never a second interaction. Verified live on Staging:
- Saved from the trip -> appeared immediately on the donor's own Unified Relationship Timeline, with the same Edit link (`/interactions/{id}/edit`) every other interaction has.
- Edited from the donor profile (the existing generic `/interactions/{id}/edit` -> `CaptureExperience` flow, completely unmodified) -> reopening "AI meeting notes" from the trip showed the edited text.
- Re-opened and re-saved (via Organize Notes + Save) -> the donor's timeline still showed exactly one "Meetings" entry, not two; the earlier text was replaced (last-write-wins), never duplicated.

**Multiple meetings for the same donor stay independent.** Added the same synthetic donor to two different trips, scheduled a meeting on each, and saved distinct AI notes on each. The donor's Unified Relationship Timeline showed "Meetings 2" with each entry's own distinct content intact and unaffected by the other -- confirmed because each trip_prospects row carries its own `linked_interaction_id` (`trip-meeting-{prospectId}`, deterministic per prospect row, never per donor), so cross-trip and multi-meeting separation falls out of the existing id scheme for free; no new logic was needed for this.

**Completed trips.** Marked one of the two test meetings "Meeting Completed" (via the trip's own existing required-notes completion flow) and confirmed the "✦ AI meeting notes" link remains present and still opens/saves correctly for a completed meeting, reviewed from a past trip.

**Idempotency.** Follow-up actions created from this screen are still deduplicated server-side exactly like the donor-profile flow, but now keyed by the client's own per-save `idempotencyKey` rather than by the (now-stable, reusable) interaction id -- the new route's own doc comment explains why: the target interaction is a stable id that already existed before this save and will still exist after it, so follow-up dedup must be scoped to one save attempt, not to the meeting's whole lifetime of saves. The interaction's own `summary` UPDATE can never itself PRIMARY-KEY-conflict (it's an UPDATE, not an INSERT); only a follow-up INSERT can, from a genuine double-click/retry of the identical idempotencyKey -- verified by code review against the existing, already-tested `followUpListsMatch`/replay-vs-reject pattern (`lib/meeting-notes/idempotency.ts`), reused unchanged.

**A known, pre-existing interaction, not introduced by this change:** marking a meeting "Meeting Completed" via the trip card's own required "Meeting notes" field (a feature that predates this round) unconditionally overwrites `interactions.summary` with `"Trip meeting with {donor}.\n{notes}"` (see `completeProspectMeeting` in `lib/relationships/trips-data.ts`, unmodified). Observed live: AI-organized notes saved while a meeting was still "Scheduled" were replaced by the plain completion-notes text the moment the meeting was marked completed. This is existing behavior of the already-shipped scheduling/completion feature, not something this round changed -- flagged here as a real workflow interaction a fundraiser could hit (use "✦ AI meeting notes" again *after* completing, to re-organize/restore richer notes, rather than relying on the completion field for anything beyond a brief note).

**Schema:** none required or added -- the feature reuses `interactions` and `recommendations` exactly as they already exist.

### Item 2 -- Bashevkin/Cohen JL reconciliation: diagnosis, not a defect

Investigated read-only on Production (trip "Teaneck-10/20/26", `trips.id 6535f09f-...`). Full detail (exact record IDs, SQL evidence, UI confirmation) is in the investigation's own report; summarized here:

- **Both** real JL financial records (Bashevkin's $10,000 gift, Cohen's $5,000 pledge) imported correctly and matched the correct donor in the same import batch -- this was **not** an import failure for either donor.
- The difference is category-driven, by existing design: `lib/giving/management.ts`'s automatic JL-import reconciliation (`pendingGiftMatches()`/`CONFIRM_PENDING_GIFT_SQL`) only ever auto-matches `category = 'pending_gift'`. Bashevkin's entry was a `pending_gift` -> auto-resolved to "Confirmed via import." Cohen's was a `pending_pledge` -> that code's own existing header comment documents this as a deliberate, previously-reviewed exclusion ("extending it to pledges is a materially bigger, separately reviewable change than this feature needs"), so it stays "Awaiting JL" until the fundraiser manually clicks "Associate an existing donation or pledge" and selects the real imported pledge -- the same manual step that already exists and already works for this exact case.
- **No double-counting:** no `confirmed_by_activity_id` is claimed by more than one active attribution workspace-wide; a reconciled attribution counts once, and partial payments against a pledge only move cash-collected, never double the commitment total. Verified against the trip's own live totals.
- **Scope:** Cohen is currently the only donor workspace-wide showing this unresolved-but-already-available pattern. It is a real, recurring usability gap (nothing proactively tells the fundraiser a matching real pledge already arrived), not a one-off, and will recur for any future donor-confirmed pledge whose real JL pledge later lands -- but it is not a software defect, and no Production data is inconsistent.
- **No Production change made or proposed as urgent.** The existing manual action (visible on Cohen's own trip card) is the correct, already-available fix for this one donor; the owner can take it directly in Production whenever convenient. If a system-wide fix (extending the pledge-category to the automatic matcher) is wanted later, that is a separate, explicitly out-of-scope, separately-reviewable change per the code's own existing caution about that path.

### Unresolved limitations / explicitly out of scope under this round

- The pre-existing "Meeting Completed" overwrite-of-AI-notes interaction (above) was observed, not changed -- changing `completeProspectMeeting`'s write behavior is a separate, reviewable change against the already-shipped, Production-deployed trip-confirmation feature.
- No automatic calendar sync work was touched (the Add-to-Google-Calendar link and the existing pending/synced/failed sync badge were left completely alone; the new interaction UPDATE deliberately never writes `occurred_at`/`end_at`/`location`/`source`).
- The pledge-category exclusion from automatic JL reconciliation (item 2) was diagnosed, not changed; no system-wide fix was implemented.
- This round did not merge anything into `main`, did not touch Production, and did not change any donor confirmation status.

## Pending-Pledge JL Import Reconciliation, and Preserving AI Meeting Notes Through Trip Completion (2026-10-21)

Follow-up round, same day. Two items, both authorized for Staging implementation/testing, read-only on Production, no `main` merge, no Production deployment. Code+tests commit on this working branch: **`d6ed2ed84397a15968a81e5ac202c72dae17ffd2`** (`feature/independent-cloudflare-sandbox`).

### Item 1 -- closes the pending-pledge reconciliation gap the Bashevkin/Cohen diagnosis (above) identified

The prior round's diagnosis was correct as a description of *why* Cohen's entry stayed "Awaiting JL," but this round treats the asymmetry itself as a real, fixable gap rather than a permanent design limit, per this round's own instruction.

**What already existed and needed no change:** the *manual* reconciliation path -- "Associate an existing donation or pledge" on a trip prospect's card, backed by `attributeGivingActivityToTrip`'s `reconcilesAttributionId` option (`lib/relationships/trips-data.ts`) -- was already fully generic across `pending_gift` and `pending_pledge` (`listReconcilableTripAttributions` filters on both categories; `REAL_COMMITMENT_CATEGORIES` includes every real pledge/gift category). This is the action Cohen's own trip card already offers today in Production; this round did not touch it, only proved it still works end to end (see Staging evidence below).

**What was missing, and is now added:** the *automatic*, import-time reconciliation `pending_gift` has always had (`pendingGiftMatches`/`CONFIRM_PENDING_GIFT_SQL`, `lib/giving/management.ts`) had no pledge-side counterpart -- a `pending_pledge` was, by a previously-reviewed and documented deliberate scope limit, never offered as a match during JL import at all. That limit is what this round reverses:

- `pendingPledgeMatches`/`CONFIRM_PENDING_PLEDGE_SQL` (`lib/giving/management.ts`) mirror the gift-side functions exactly in guard shape, with one deliberate difference: the imported side is filtered to `open_pledge`/`partially_paid_pledge` categories only (pendingGiftMatches has no such filter on its imported side), so a brand-new *gift* can never resolve a pending *pledge*. Matching is on `committed_cents` only -- a pledge's total commitment never changes across its lifetime, so this stays correct however much (if anything) has already been paid toward the real pledge by the time it's matched; `paid_cents`/`balance_cents` are never compared.
- `app/api/import/preview/route.ts` and `app/api/import/route.ts` now also compute pending-pledge matches (from the import's own brand-new pledge rows, never a payment-assignment candidate, which only ever applies to an *already-existing* open pledge) and require an explicit `pendingPledgeDecisions` entry for every suggested match before commit, exactly mirroring `pendingGiftDecisions` -- commit is rejected with "Review every suggested pending pledge match before importing" otherwise, and a `claimedPendingPledgeIds` guard prevents one pending pledge from being claimed by two incoming rows.
- `app/onboarding/import/ImportExperience.tsx` gained a second "PENDING PLEDGE MATCHES" review panel, visually and behaviorally identical to the existing pending-gift one (same "choose the pending entry to confirm, or keep both records separate" copy), gating the Confirm/Import button the same way.
- No schema change: reuses the existing `confirmed_by_activity_id` column (migration `0016`, already live in Production since well before this round) exactly the way `CONFIRM_PENDING_GIFT_SQL` already does. Once merged, `lib/relationships/trips-data.ts`'s `listTripFinancialAttributions` -- completely unmodified by this round -- already resolves a merged pending record to its confirmed target's own live category/committed/paid/balance figures at read time, so the trip view automatically starts showing "Confirmed via import" with the *real* pledge's own numbers the moment the merge lands; nothing new had to be taught to the trip display.

**Tests added:** `tests/pending-pledge-matching.test.mjs` (real in-memory SQLite, mirrors `tests/pending-gift-matching.test.mjs`'s structure) covers an unambiguous match, an ambiguous match (two pending pledges for the same donor requiring an explicit choice), a brand-new gift never resolving a pending pledge, a partially-paid real pledge still matching by its stable committed amount, donor-boundary and near-amount safeguards, a retry/double-claim guard, and structural assertions that the import route and UI actually wire this in. `tests/pending-pledge.test.mjs` (pre-existing) had its own assertion that the import pipeline must *never* reference `pending_pledge` -- that assertion encoded the exact limit this round reverses, so it was rewritten to assert the opposite (the pipeline *must* reference `pendingPledgeMatches`/`CONFIRM_PENDING_PLEDGE_SQL` and *must* still block commit on an unreviewed match).

**Staging verification performed** (temporary Staging-writes-enabled window, `wrangler.staging.jsonc`'s `STAGING_WRITES_ENABLED` uncommented for this one window only, reverted and redeployed immediately after -- confirmed via `git diff wrangler.staging.jsonc` returning zero lines against the committed baseline):
- A real `/api/import/preview` call against a seeded `pending_pledge` ($15,000, matching JL code/amount/date window) returned exactly one `pendingPledgeMatches` entry; `pendingGiftMatches` stayed empty.
- Committing without a decision for it: `422`, `"Review every suggested pending pledge match before importing."`
- Committing with an explicit `merge` decision: `201`; the pending row's `workspace_status` flipped to `'merged'` with `confirmed_by_activity_id` pointing at the new real `open_pledge` row, plus a `giving_activity_management_audits` row (`action='pending_matched'`).
- Ambiguous case: two pending pledges for the same donor, same amount, two days apart -- preview returned both as candidates; a `merge` decision with no `pendingPledgeId` was rejected (`422`, never auto-picked); naming the specific candidate merged only that one, leaving the other untouched/active.
- **The live Cohen-shaped scenario, reproduced directly**: a donor-confirmed pending pledge attributed to a trip showed "New pledges secured $10,000 (1 awaiting JL)" / outstanding balance "$10,000 provisional, awaiting JL." Importing and merging a matching **partially-paid** real pledge ($3,000 paid / $7,000 balance) flipped the trip view to "New pledges secured $10,000, 1 pledge" (the awaiting-JL line gone), "Cash collected $3,000 ($3,000 recorded in JL)," "Outstanding pledge balance $7,000," and the attribution row read "Pledge (partially paid) · $10,000 ($3,000 paid) · Confirmed via import" -- proving the trip now uses the real record's own actual commitment/paid/balance, never an invented figure.
- Retry of an already-committed request (same `attemptId`): rejected (session no longer reusable); DB confirmed exactly 2 giving_activities rows for that donor afterward, never 3 -- no duplicate.
- One non-bug observation worth recording: `import_preview_sessions` rows did not stay reusable very long after their own commit during this test -- pre-existing session-draft lifecycle behavior, unrelated to this round's own code, not investigated further here.
- Cleanup: every temporary record from this item (deleted in FK-safe order, extending `lib/operations/staging-reset.ts`'s own documented `STAGING_RESET_TABLE_ORDER` list by two tables discovered live during cleanup that list omits -- `import_preview_session_chunks` before `import_preview_sessions`, and `calendar_event_link_history`/`calendar_event_links` before `interactions`; worth a follow-up fix to that list itself, not done here) -- final counts confirmed to match the pre-test baseline exactly.

### Item 2 -- AI meeting notes preserved through trip meeting completion, rescheduling, and reopening

The prior round's own handoff entry flagged this as "a known, pre-existing interaction, not introduced by this change." This round fixes it.

**Root cause:** `scheduleProspectMeeting` and `completeProspectMeeting` (`lib/relationships/trips-data.ts`) are the only two trip actions that write the linked interaction's `summary` (confirmed by inspecting every `SET.*summary`/`summary = ?` site across the codebase -- the donor-profile and trip meeting-notes save routes are the only other writers, and both are the intended, correct ones, unmodified here). Both used an `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT(id) DO UPDATE SET summary = excluded.summary` upsert that unconditionally overwrote `summary` on every call, including a reschedule/reopen (scheduling) or a second completion (completing) of the SAME deterministic interaction a prior AI-notes save had already written real content to.

**Fix:**
- `scheduleProspectMeeting`: `summary` is no longer in the `DO UPDATE SET` list at all. The placeholder (`"Trip meeting scheduled with {donor}."`) is still written in full on the very first schedule (the `INSERT` branch, unaffected by this change); every reschedule or reopen after that leaves `summary` completely untouched, whatever it currently holds.
- `completeProspectMeeting`: now reads the existing summary first. If it's empty or still exactly the scheduling placeholder (`isMeaningfulMeetingSummary` helper), nothing of value exists yet and the full `"Trip meeting with {donor}.\n{notes}"` is written, exactly as before this fix. If real content already exists, the completion note is **appended** (`"{existing}\n\n--- Marked completed {date} ---\n{notes}"`) rather than replacing it -- never silently destroying the earlier notes. Retry-safe: if the existing summary's own tail already ends with the exact incoming notes text, nothing is re-appended (an identical retry is a true no-op).
- `app/travel-planning/[id]/TripDashboardExperience.tsx`: the Complete-meeting panel now shows a "✦ Review saved meeting notes before completing" link (when a linked interaction exists) and an explicit hint that any notes already saved are kept, never replaced -- letting the fundraiser see what's already there before adding today's note, which is the practical form "let the user review any intentional replacement" takes here, since nothing is ever actually replaced.

**Tests added:** `tests/trip-meeting-notes-preservation.test.mjs`, following the exact same "real local D1, intercept `cloudflare:workers`" rigor as `tests/trip-reconciliation-concurrency.test.mjs` (calls the real, unmodified `scheduleProspectMeeting`/`completeProspectMeeting`/`getProspectMeetingNotesTarget`, never a hand-copied reproduction). Covers: rescheduling after AI notes are saved (notes untouched, confirmed via both the raw `interactions.summary` row and `getProspectMeetingNotesTarget`'s own read); completing a meeting with no prior real notes (full summary written, unchanged behavior); completing a meeting that already has AI notes (both the earlier notes and the new completion note present afterward); a retried identical completion (no duplicate block); and two separate meetings for the same donor across two different trips staying fully independent through a completion on one of them. All passing (`node tests/trip-meeting-notes-preservation.test.mjs` run directly; `completeProspectMeeting` makes no calendar call at all by its own design, and `scheduleProspectMeeting`'s best-effort calendar step is gated behind a per-user `calendar_sync_enabled` flag never set for this test's synthetic user, so neither function attempts any live network call in this harness).

**Staging verification performed** (no write-guard flag needed -- `/api/trips/**` is always allowed):
- Scheduled a meeting, saved an AI-organized note via the trip's own meeting-notes screen, cancelled to `meeting_requested` and rescheduled to a new date (the reopen path) -- `summary` unchanged (confirmed via direct `wrangler d1 execute --remote` SQL on `interactions.summary`), `occurred_at` updated to the new time, `source` correctly reset off its `cancelled:` prefix.
- Marked the same meeting Completed with a different note -- final summary contained both the original AI note and, appended below a `"--- Marked completed 2026-10-21 ---"` marker, the new completion note. The live Complete panel showed the new review-link and hint text.
- Donor-profile consistency: the donor's own Unified Relationship Timeline showed the identical combined summary with no extra step.
- Two trips, same donor: a second trip/prospect for the same donor got its own independent note; completing the first trip's meeting never touched the second's.
- Cleanup: every temporary record from this item deleted and confirmed removed (folded into the same cleanup pass and final-count check as Item 1, above).

## Closing Two Review Gaps: Lost Notes Under Concurrent Saves, and Falsely-Audited Stale Pending-Match Claims (2026-10-21, third round)

Independent review of the two items above found two real, narrower gaps -- both closed this round, same day. Code+tests commit on this working branch: **`8b737da`** (`feature/independent-cloudflare-sandbox`). Authorized for Staging implementation/testing; no Production deployment, migration, donor-note edit, donor-confirmation change, or Production reconciliation; no `main` merge.

### Item 1 -- lost notes during concurrent saves

**The gap.** `completeProspectMeeting` read `interactions.summary`, computed an appended value in application code (append the completion note onto whatever was there), then wrote it back with a plain, unconditional `UPDATE`. Anything that wrote to the SAME row between that read and that write -- a donor-profile edit via `/interactions/{id}/edit`, or a save from the trip's own AI meeting-notes screen -- would be silently overwritten the moment completion's own write landed. The symmetric risk also existed the other way: an editor that had loaded the summary BEFORE a completion appended its note could save afterward and wipe the completion note out, since neither the trip AI-notes save route nor the generic interaction-edit route checked whether the row had changed since they read it.

**The fix.**
- `completeProspectMeeting` (`lib/relationships/trips-data.ts`) now runs a bounded retry loop (5 attempts). Each attempt re-reads the CURRENT `summary` immediately before writing, and the write is a compare-and-swap: `UPDATE interactions SET summary = ? ... WHERE ... AND summary = ?`, bound to the EXACT value this attempt just read. A CAS miss is not an error -- it means something else wrote first -- so the loop re-reads the new value and recomputes its own append on top of THAT, rather than failing or silently discarding the newer content. The companion `trip_prospects` write in the same batch is guarded by `WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM interactions WHERE ... AND summary = ?)` bound to the intended NEW summary -- since D1 batch statements observe earlier statements' own writes within the same transaction, this only evaluates true when the interactions UPDATE, moments earlier in the SAME batch, actually applied. The meeting is never recorded or reported as completed unless the notes write itself actually landed. A brand-new, never-scheduled completion (no existing interaction row) uses a plain `INSERT`, never `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` -- a genuinely concurrent first-time completion for the same prospect now conflicts loudly on the shared deterministic id and retries (taking the append branch) rather than one silently clobbering the other. Exhausting all 5 attempts (persistent, genuine contention) returns a new `notes_conflict` reason -- wired into `app/api/trips/[id]/prospects/[prospectId]/route.ts`'s error mapping as a 409, "Nothing was lost -- try marking it completed again."
- The trip AI-notes save route (`app/api/trips/[id]/prospects/[prospectId]/meeting-notes/route.ts`) gained the identical compare-and-swap, now extracted into a new shared module (`lib/meeting-notes/concurrent-save.ts`, `buildConcurrentSummarySaveStatements`/`concurrentSummarySaveApplied`) so the exact same SQL shape is both production code and the test target. The CAS baseline is a new, optional `expectedSummary` field the client sends -- `MeetingNotesExperience.tsx`'s own `initialSummaryText` (the summary this editing session actually started from), never a value re-read moments before writing -- because the real risk here is a browser tab left open across someone else's change, not a sub-second race within one request. A CAS miss is disambiguated after the fact: if the row already holds exactly the summary this save intended to write, it's treated as a safe replay (200, no-op); otherwise it's a genuine conflict (409, "Your unsaved text has not been discarded -- copy it if you want to keep it, then reload..."). The follow-up `recommendations` INSERTs are themselves conditioned on the SAME interactions UPDATE having applied (`WHERE EXISTS (...)`), so a lost CAS can never leave orphaned follow-ups for a save that never actually landed.
- The generic `/interactions/{id}/edit` route (`app/api/interactions/[id]/route.ts`) gained the same `expectedSummary` field and a pre-write comparison against the row it just read, rejecting with the same style of 409 before building or running any statements if the two differ. Deliberately scoped to this one check, not a full DB-level CAS on every statement in that route's own batch (which also touches reminders and relationship-fact acceptance) -- the realistic risk here is a tab staying open for minutes, not a sub-second race between two edits of the same interaction, and guarding every one of those secondary writes together would be a materially larger change than that risk calls for. `CaptureExperience.tsx`'s `InitialActivity` type gained the raw `summary` field (the page already loads it; the form only ever submits the re-split subject/note) so it can be sent back as `expectedSummary` on save. On any 409 from any of the three paths above, the client's existing catch/`setErrorMessage` handling already preserves the user's typed text (it never clears component state on error) -- "give the user an actionable conflict response that preserves their unsaved text" required no additional client-side change beyond sending the field.

**What was deliberately NOT changed:** `scheduleProspectMeeting` already stopped writing `summary` on conflict at all in the prior round (nothing to compare-and-swap, since it never touches the field after the first schedule) -- unaffected by this round, still correct.

**Tests added:** `tests/trip-meeting-notes-concurrency.test.mjs`, calling the REAL `completeProspectMeeting`/`scheduleProspectMeeting` and the real `buildConcurrentSummarySaveStatements`/`concurrentSummarySaveApplied` against a real local-D1 database (same rigor as `tests/trip-reconciliation-concurrency.test.mjs`), covering all four scenarios required: (1) completion reads, a concurrent edit lands via `interceptFirstBatch` (the same technique `tests/trip-entrypoints-atomicity.test.mjs` already uses -- wraps `.batch()` so a side-effecting write runs between a function's own read and its write) between completion's read and write, then completion writes -- the concurrent edit survives AND completion's own note is still appended on top of it; (2) a stale editor (its own baseline is the pre-completion summary) saves after completion has already appended its note -- rejected outright, the completion note untouched; (3) two genuinely competing completions via `Promise.all` (real microtask interleaving) -- both succeed, both notes survive; (4) an identical retry -- no duplicate block. All passing.

**Staging verification performed** (no write-guard flag needed -- `/api/trips/**` is always allowed):
- Scheduled, saved an AI note, rescheduled (cancel/reopen cycle) -- note survived unchanged; `occurred_at` updated; `source` reset off `cancelled:`.
- Marked Completed with a different note -- final summary held both notes, separated by a `--- Marked completed 2026-10-21 ---` marker; the new "✦ Review saved meeting notes before completing" link and preservation hint rendered live in the Complete panel.
- **A genuine live double-submit**: fired two near-simultaneous `fetch()` PATCHes from the browser's own devtools console to `/api/trips/{tripId}/prospects/{prospectId}`, both `{status:"meeting_completed", ...}` with different notes ("RACE NOTE X" / "RACE NOTE Y") against a real, unseeded completion. Both returned `200 {"ok":true}`; the final summary contained BOTH notes -- a real, live race producing zero data loss, not just the local test harness's simulated one.
- `/interactions/{id}/edit` regression check: a normal single-editor edit still pre-fills, edits, and saves correctly -- the new `expectedSummary` field is transparent to ordinary use.
- Cleanup: every temporary record removed, confirmed via a final count sweep across donors/trips/trip_prospects/interactions/giving_activities/data_imports/giving_activity_management_audits/calendar_event_links -- all zero for the synthetic ids used.

### Item 2 -- falsely-audited stale pending-match claims

**The gap.** `CONFIRM_PENDING_GIFT_SQL`/`CONFIRM_PENDING_PLEDGE_SQL` are guarded (`WHERE ... confirmed_by_activity_id IS NULL`) so a competing request that already reconciled the same pending entry correctly affects zero rows. But the import route's own audit-row `INSERT` ran unconditionally in the SAME batch regardless of that CONFIRM's own rowcount -- a losing claim still got permanently, falsely recorded in `giving_activity_management_audits` as `pending_matched`, even though the pending entry itself was never actually touched by that request. The existing test for this SQL only checked the guarded UPDATE's own result in isolation; it never exercised how the full import transaction handled a failed claim.

**The fix.** A new shared module, `lib/giving/pending-reconciliation.ts` (`buildPendingReconciliationStatements`/`resolvePendingReconciliationOutcomes`), used identically by both the pending-gift and pending-pledge paths in `app/api/import/route.ts` -- closing the same gap for both categories at once, per the review's own "inspect shared gift-side logic" instruction, by literally sharing the code rather than fixing it twice.
- The audit `INSERT` is now `INSERT OR IGNORE`, conditioned on `WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM giving_activities WHERE id = ? AND confirmed_by_activity_id = ? AND workspace_status = 'merged')` -- checking that THIS request's own CONFIRM, immediately earlier in the same D1 batch, actually applied (D1 batch statements observe earlier statements' own writes within the same transaction). The audit row's own `id` is now deterministic (`pending-match-${candidate.id}`), not `crypto.randomUUID()` -- this is the detail that took an extra iteration to get right: the EXISTS check alone cannot distinguish "my own CONFIRM just succeeded" from "a retry targeting the SAME already-merged candidate, where the end state looks identical to a fresh success but my OWN CONFIRM affected zero rows this time." A pending entry can only ever be confirmed once, ever (the guard is permanent -- `confirmed_by_activity_id` never reverts to NULL), so "one audit row per candidate, ever," enforced by a real PRIMARY KEY plus `OR IGNORE`, is the correct invariant -- the same way the CONFIRM statements themselves enforce "confirmed at most once" on the pending row via a real constraint, never a read-then-decide check. (This was caught by the new test below failing on first run, before ever reaching Staging -- see "what was directly verified" at the end of this section.)
- `app/api/import/route.ts` tracks each plan's own statement offset within the combined batch, and after the batch commits, reads back each candidate's own CONFIRM rowcount via `resolvePendingReconciliationOutcomes` -- never inferring success from having submitted a merge decision alone. A stale claim is excluded from `pendingGiftsConfirmed`/`pendingPledgesConfirmed` and surfaces as a `warnings` entry ("N pending {gift/pledge} match(es) could not be confirmed because the entry was already reconciled by another request in the meantime... use 'Associate an existing donation or pledge' on the trip to finish linking it"). The import itself is never rejected or rolled back over a losing claim -- the real new activity row always still imports correctly (`activityStatements` is never conditioned on the CONFIRM at all), satisfying "preserve valid imports." The already-committed `report_json` (bound into the SAME batch, before the batch's own results are known) is corrected with a best-effort follow-up `UPDATE data_imports SET report_json = ?` ONLY when a stale claim was found -- the HTTP response returned to the caller is always the corrected one regardless of whether that follow-up write succeeds; a failure there only means a later history replay of that one import would show the pre-correction counts, never an incorrect financial record.
- The pre-existing, earlier validation check ("The selected pending gift/pledge no longer matches this JL record. Refresh the preview.") is unchanged and still catches the common case (the candidate list the client is reviewing has already gone stale by the time it submits). This round's fix closes the narrower, later window: the target going stale AFTER that validation but BEFORE the write, within the SAME request.

**Tests added:** `tests/pending-reconciliation-transaction.test.mjs`, calling the REAL, unmodified shared module against a real local-D1 database built from this repo's own migrations, with `.batch()` emulating D1's real one-transaction, statements-see-earlier-writes semantics (`tests/helpers/d1-sqlite-adapter.mjs`) -- never a hand-copied reproduction of the SQL. Covers all five scenarios required: (1) two independent import attempts (two separate plans, two separate batches) claim the same pending pledge -- exactly one confirms, the loser's own real pledge import still succeeds unaffected, and exactly one audit row exists (this is the test that caught the determinism bug above on its first run); (2) the target becomes unavailable AFTER validation but BEFORE the write, simulated by mutating the row directly between building the plan and running its batch -- the stale request never overwrites the entry someone else already claimed, and writes no audit row; (3) an identical retry of the exact same decision -- the second run's own CONFIRM finds the guard already closed and affects zero rows, and exactly one audit row survives; (4) a valid explicit "keep separate" decision -- builds zero statements, touches nothing; (5) the existing pending-GIFT path through the SAME shared module, confirming the extraction did not regress the original, narrower behavior. Two structural assertions close the file, confirming `app/api/import/route.ts` actually wires the shared module in (`buildPendingReconciliationStatements`/`resolvePendingReconciliationOutcomes`/`staleCandidateIds` all present in its source), matching this codebase's existing convention (`tests/pending-pledge.test.mjs`) of pairing behavioral tests with a structural backstop.

**Staging verification performed** (temporary `STAGING_WRITES_ENABLED` window, reverted and redeployed immediately after -- confirmed `git diff wrangler.staging.jsonc` empty against the committed baseline):
- An ordinary merge through the REAL HTTP routes (`/api/import/preview` then `/api/import`): pending_pledge $5,000 correctly listed as a match, commit returned `201` with `pendingPledgesConfirmed:1`, DB confirmed `workspace_status='merged'`, `confirmed_by_activity_id` set to the real new pledge row, exactly one audit row under the new deterministic id. The same for a pending-gift spot check -- no regression from the shared-module extraction.
- A true mid-request race against a live remote Worker isn't deterministically reproducible on demand, so the stale-claim mechanism was instead proven by running the LITERAL production SQL (`CONFIRM_PENDING_PLEDGE_SQL` plus the literal conditional `INSERT OR IGNORE ... WHERE EXISTS` audit statement, copy-pasted verbatim from `lib/giving/pending-reconciliation.ts`) directly against REAL remote D1, on a pending row pre-staled to simulate "a competing request already reconciled it": the stale CONFIRM affected 0 rows, the pending row's `confirmed_by_activity_id` stayed exactly the competing activity's id (never overwritten), and zero audit rows were created for the losing claim -- confirmed by a direct follow-up query. This is a genuine, independent confirmation on the real D1 engine, complementing (not replacing) the local test suite, which is what actually proves the full post-batch outcome-resolution/warnings/report-correction logic end to end via true interleaving.
- Cleanup: this round's own Staging cleanup surfaced real gaps in `lib/operations/staging-reset.ts`'s documented `STAGING_RESET_TABLE_ORDER` beyond the two already flagged by the prior round -- `giving_activity_import_changes` before `data_imports`; `import_preview_session_chunks` (joined on `session_id`, not `preview_session_id`) before `import_preview_sessions`; `trip_prospects` before `interactions` (via `linked_interaction_id`); and `donor_views` before `donors`. All resolved during cleanup; none fixed in that file itself this round (see unresolved limitations below). Final sweep confirmed zero remaining rows for every synthetic id pattern used.

### What was directly verified vs. inferred

**Directly verified:** both fixes' core correctness via real local-D1 tests with genuine statement-level interleaving (not merely "the code looks right") -- including a determinism bug in the FIRST version of the pending-match audit guard that the test itself caught before any Staging or Production exposure, which is direct evidence the testing approach here was doing real work, not rubber-stamping. Both fixes' live behavior on Staging, including one genuine live concurrent race (the double-submit `fetch()` pair) and one direct real-D1 SQL proof (the stale-claim rejection) -- not merely local-test-only claims. The full test suite, lint, and both builds passing identically on the working branch and the re-ported isolated release branch.

**Inferred / not independently re-verified this round:** that `app/api/interactions/[id]/route.ts`'s narrower, app-level-only staleness check (rather than a full DB-level CAS across its entire batch) is an acceptable, proportionate scope decision rather than a residual gap -- this was a deliberate judgment call documented in the code and in this entry, not something re-litigated against a live, deliberately-racing request against that specific route this round. The `import_preview_sessions` reusability-window behavior flagged by the prior round was not revisited.

## Closing the Remaining Meeting-Notes Gaps: Pre-Write-Only Staleness Checks That Never Guarded the Actual Write (2026-10-21, fourth round)

Independent review of the round above found that both of its documented, deliberate design choices -- the generic `/interactions/{id}/edit` route's app-level-only staleness check, and `completeProspectMeeting`'s own `trip_prospects` companion-write guard -- shared the exact bug class the SAME round had just closed in the trip meeting-notes save: a check against the row's resulting CONTENT is not proof that THIS request's own write produced it. This round closed all three instances of that one underlying pattern as a single bounded release, after reviewing every writer of the shared `interactions` row (trip scheduling/rescheduling/reopening/completion, trip AI meeting notes, donor-profile interaction edits, follow-up creation/retry) and the full pending-gift/pending-pledge reconciliation path end to end -- no new defects found in the reconciliation path itself this round; it was re-confirmed, not re-fixed. Code+tests commit on this working branch: **`44fa7b7`** (`feature/independent-cloudflare-sandbox`). Authorized for Staging implementation/testing; no Production deployment, migration, donor-note edit, donor-confirmation change, or Production reconciliation; no `main` merge.

### Defect A -- the generic interaction-edit route's write was unconditional

**The gap.** `app/api/interactions/[id]/route.ts`'s PATCH handler compared the client's `expectedSummary` against the row it had just read, and rejected up front on a mismatch -- but that was a one-time, pre-write check. If a trip completion or another notes save landed on the SAME interaction between that check and this route's own `UPDATE`, the UPDATE still ran unconditionally and silently overwrote it, along with whatever reminder, donor-reassignment archival, or relationship-fact acceptance this edit also requested. The prior round's own write-up called the app-level-only check "a documented, proportionate scope decision" -- true as far as it went, but it was never actually a compare-and-swap at the point of the write itself, which is the gap this round closed.

**The fix.** Extracted the PATCH handler's write logic into a new module, `lib/capture/interaction-edit.ts` (`applyInteractionEdit`), so it is directly testable against a real D1SqliteAdapter rather than only reachable through the Worker route. The primary `UPDATE interactions SET ... WHERE id = ? AND user_id = ? AND summary = ?` now runs ALONE via `.run()` (not folded into a larger batch), bound to the exact `casBaseline` (the client's `expectedSummary` when sent, else this request's own fresh read -- same baseline semantics as before). Its own `meta.changes` is read back immediately: zero means someone else wrote first, and the function returns `{status:"conflict", currentSummary}` without building or running a single further statement -- the reminder upsert/delete, the donor-reassignment archival (`planFactArchival`), and the relationship-fact acceptance (`planFactAcceptance`) are only ever assembled and run as one batch AFTER that rowcount has already proven the primary write applied. The route (`app/api/interactions/[id]/route.ts`) now just calls `applyInteractionEdit` and maps `{status:"conflict"}` to the same 409 message as before, preserving the unsaved text contract unchanged. The pre-write `expectedSummary` check in the route itself is kept as a fast-path rejection (saves a round-trip for a client already known to be stale), explicitly documented as not the only guard -- the CAS at the write is what actually closes the gap.

### Defect B -- the trip meeting-notes save's follow-up guard proved the wrong thing

**The reproduced case** (as reported): the current summary already equals the requested `newSummary`; the client submits a stale `expectedSummary` and fresh follow-up ids; the summary UPDATE affects zero rows; the follow-ups still insert because the old guard's `WHERE EXISTS (... summary = ?)` checked the NEW value, which happened to already be true -- by coincidence, not because this request's own write landed. The route returned success with a dishonest `followUpsCreated` count while having actually inserted tasks nobody asked it to keep.

**The fix.** `lib/meeting-notes/concurrent-save.ts` was rewritten around a new `saveConcurrentSummaryAndFollowUps`, replacing the old `buildConcurrentSummarySaveStatements`/`concurrentSummarySaveApplied` pair. Same split-write pattern as Defect A: the summary UPDATE runs alone first; its own rowcount decides everything else. On a CAS hit (`>0` rows), the follow-ups are now unconditional INSERTs (safe, since success is already proven), with a PK-collision re-read-and-compare fallback for genuine retries. On a CAS miss, the function re-reads the current summary and explicitly branches: if it doesn't match `newSummary` at all, `{conflict, "summary_stale"}`; if it matches AND the requested follow-ups already exist with matching content (or none were requested), `{replayed}` (a safe, honest no-op); if it matches but the requested follow-ups do NOT already exist or differ, `{conflict, "followup_mismatch"}` -- the exact reported case, now correctly rejected with zero follow-ups created. The explicitly-required positive case -- a NON-stale baseline where the text also happens not to have changed, plus a genuinely new follow-up -- is handled correctly as a true `{applied, followUpsCreated:1}`, because SQLite's `UPDATE ... WHERE summary = ?` reports a real `changes=1` whenever the WHERE clause's own comparison value still matches the row's CURRENT state, independent of whether the SET value differs from it. The route (`app/api/trips/[id]/prospects/[prospectId]/meeting-notes/route.ts`) was updated to call the new function and branch on its `status`, with the old manual PK-conflict disambiguation logic removed (it now lives inside the shared module).

### Defect class C -- the same pattern, confirmed and closed in `completeProspectMeeting`

Reviewing every writer of the shared `interactions` row surfaced the identical pattern a third time, latent and narrower than the other two (no concrete external repro was reported for this one, but the mechanism is the same): `completeProspectMeeting`'s own companion `trip_prospects` write was guarded by `WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM interactions WHERE ... AND summary = ?)` bound to the intended NEW summary -- the prior round's own fix for the *notes* write, carried over unchanged for the *prospect-status* write, with the exact same latent flaw. Closed the same way: the interactions UPDATE now runs alone via `.run()`, its own `meta.changes` is checked, and the `trip_prospects` status write only runs (as its own unconditional `.run()`, no EXISTS guard needed) once that rowcount has already proven success. The bounded retry loop (5 attempts), the deterministic-id-plus-plain-INSERT handling for a brand-new, never-scheduled completion, and the `notes_conflict` exhaustion reason are all unchanged from the prior round -- only the one guard's mechanism changed.

**What else was reviewed and found NOT to need changes:** `app/api/meeting-notes/route.ts` (the donor-profile meeting-notes CREATE path) already uses a fundamentally different, already-robust idempotency mechanism (a real PK-conflict exception plus re-read-and-compare disambiguation, never an EXISTS-on-endstate trick) -- not vulnerable to this bug class. `setSimpleProspectStatus`'s cancellation path already has a proper CAS on `source`. `scheduleProspectMeeting` never touches `summary` on conflict at all (excluded from `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET` since the second round) -- not vulnerable to this bug class; its calendar-guard logic remains explicitly out of scope. The full pending-gift/pending-pledge reconciliation path (preview, commit, audit creation, import-history reports, trip totals) was re-read end to end against this round's own concurrency/ownership/stale-client/retry/companion-write-atomicity checklist -- no new defect found; the prior round's own fix (the deterministic `pending-match-${candidate.id}` audit id plus `INSERT OR IGNORE WHERE EXISTS`) already follows the identical "prove the primary write succeeded before trusting a companion write" principle this round applied to the other three call sites, so nothing further to change there.

**Tests added:** `tests/interaction-edit-concurrency.test.mjs` -- calls the REAL `applyInteractionEdit` against a real D1SqliteAdapter (via the established `cloudflare-workers-shim-loader.mjs` technique, which works for `fact-accept.ts`'s own exported functions despite an older test file's now-outdated comment claiming otherwise): an ordinary non-stale edit applies and creates its reminder; the reported defect -- a concurrent write lands between this edit's read and write, and the edit (also requesting a donor reassignment plus relationship-snapshot acceptance) is rejected with the concurrent value returned, with direct queries confirming donor_id, summary, the reminder row, and both donors' relationship-facts are ALL untouched; a legitimate donor-reassignment edit on a non-stale baseline still correctly archives the old donor's current fact (regression check that the fix didn't suppress real writes). `tests/meeting-notes-concurrent-save.test.mjs` -- calls the real `saveConcurrentSummaryAndFollowUps` directly: an ordinary save; the exact reported defect (stale baseline, coincidentally-matching current text, fresh follow-up ids) rejected with zero follow-ups created; the same coincidence with zero follow-ups requested treated as a safe replay; the required positive case (non-stale baseline, unchanged text, a genuinely new follow-up) applies and creates it; an identical retry replays without duplicating; a changed-payload retry (new text) rejected as `summary_stale`; a changed-payload retry where the text re-matches but the follow-up id collides with different content rejected as `followup_mismatch`. `tests/trip-meeting-notes-concurrency.test.mjs`'s existing interleaving test was updated to call the new `saveConcurrentSummaryAndFollowUps` API, and its `interceptFirstBatch` helper was generalized to `interceptFirstWrite` (now wrapping a standalone bound-statement `.run()` as well as `.batch()`), since `completeProspectMeeting`'s CAS write is no longer part of a batch. Two existing structural-assertion test files (`tests/relationship-fact-accept-wiring.test.mjs`, `tests/relationship-fact-edit-donor-reassignment.test.mjs`) had their regex patterns updated to read the new `lib/capture/interaction-edit.ts` module rather than the route file they used to check, after the extraction moved the code their assertions were locating.

**Staging verification performed** (temporary `STAGING_WRITES_ENABLED` window for the generic interactions route; `/api/trips/**` needed no flag):
- Defect B's exact reported reproduction, live: scheduled a real meeting, saved a real AI note with a real follow-up (regression check -- succeeded, follow-up created), then submitted a stale `expectedSummary` with the summary coincidentally equal to the current value and a brand-new follow-up -- got the correct `409`, and a direct query confirmed zero follow-up rows were created for that request's id.
- The required positive case, live: a non-stale `expectedSummary` equal to the current text, plus a fresh follow-up -- `200 {"followUpsCreated":1}`, and the follow-up row was confirmed created.
- Defect class C's regression check, live: two genuinely concurrent `PATCH .../meeting_completed` requests (`Promise.all`, real browser-side race, different completion notes) against the same not-yet-completed prospect -- both returned `200`, and the final summary contained BOTH notes, separated by their own "Marked completed" markers, with `trip_prospects.status` correctly settled to `meeting_completed`.
- Defect A's exact reproduction, live: created a real interaction, captured its baseline summary, simulated the concurrent write landing in the gap via direct SQL (mirroring a real competing save), then submitted a PATCH using the now-stale baseline that ALSO requested a donor reassignment and relationship-snapshot acceptance -- got the correct `409`, and direct queries confirmed `donor_id`, `summary`, the reminder row (`recommendations`), and `donor_relationship_facts` for both donors were all completely untouched (still exactly the concurrent write's own state, never the stale edit's). A follow-up legitimate, non-stale edit on the same interaction then correctly succeeded (`200`), confirming the fix doesn't block ordinary saves.
- **A real deployment-pipeline defect found and fixed during this round's own verification, not a code defect in the application:** redeploying Staging via a bare `wrangler deploy --config wrangler.staging.jsonc` (rather than the dedicated `build:staging-independent` script) reused a stale `dist/` build whose own manifest read `"environment": "production-independent"`. Since `shouldBlockStagingWrite` only ever blocks when `deploymentEnvironment === "staging-independent"` exactly, the write-guard was silently inert the entire time this mismatch was in effect, independent of the `STAGING_WRITES_ENABLED` flag's own state -- confirmed by a live write succeeding (`201`) with the flag explicitly unset. The D1 binding itself was never affected by this (every deploy in this round, correct build or not, bound `env.DB` to `fundraising-os-staging-db`, confirmed in each deploy's own binding list and by every query throughout this round), so no Production data was ever at risk. Rebuilt with `npm run build:staging-independent`, confirmed the manifest read `"staging-independent"`, redeployed, and reconfirmed live: a mutating request now correctly receives `403` with the flag unset, and the `/api/trips/**` carve-out still passes through to route-level validation as before.
- Cleanup: every synthetic record created this round (the test trip, prospect, both AI-notes save attempts' follow-up rows, the calendar-event-link/history rows the trip's own meeting-scheduling created, the interaction-edit test's own interaction, and the two stray interactions created while diagnosing the deployment-pipeline issue above) removed in FK-safe order (recommendations/calendar_event_link_history/calendar_event_links before trip_prospects/interactions, interactions before trips), with a final broad content-pattern sweep (not just the specific ids already deleted) confirming zero remaining rows. The two reusable synthetic donor fixtures from prior rounds were reused, not recreated, and confirmed unchanged (`relationship_summary`/`institutional_memory` still `NULL`) at the end.

### What was directly verified vs. inferred

**Directly verified:** all three fixes' core correctness via real local-D1 tests with genuine statement-level interleaving, including the exact reported Defect B reproduction and the exact described Defect A race. All three fixes' live behavior on Staging against the real deployed routes, including two genuine live concurrent races (the completion double-submit, and the Defect A stale-edit-vs-concurrent-write sequence) and the Defect B bug reproduction with a direct-query zero-rows proof. The full test suite (222/222 on the release branch; 239/240 on the working branch, the one failure being `tests/backup-identity-metadata.test.mjs`, confirmed pre-existing and unrelated by reproducing it against the clean, unmodified branch HEAD -- an environment/line-ending-sensitive check against an unrelated GitHub Actions workflow file, not this round's code), lint (94 pre-existing errors on both branches, unchanged, zero new), and all builds (default, staging-independent, production-independent) passing identically on both branches. The Staging write-guard's actual deployed state, by directly provoking both the false-pass and the correct-block, rather than trusting the config file's own intent.

**Inferred / not independently re-verified this round:** that the full pending-gift/pending-pledge reconciliation path has no further defects beyond the prior round's own fix -- this was a careful re-read against this round's checklist, not a new round of live-race testing against that path (which the prior round already did directly). Whether this deployment-pipeline gap (bare `wrangler deploy` silently reusing a mismatched build) has affected any PRIOR round's own "write-guard restored" claim was not investigated -- this round only confirms its OWN restoration was real, verified live, at the end.
